title: East Lake Hot Springs
contentHtml:
East Lake Hot Springs are natural, undeveloped springs on the south shore of East Lake in the Newberry Caldera, about 0.4 mile west of the Forest Service Hot Springs Boating Site. Boating is the best way there: head west from the ramp toward the tan rock outcrops and look for bubbling gas and a rotten-egg smell, then dig fingers or toes into the bubbling sand to find hot water, about 104 to 120 degrees F.

The East Lake Health Resort operated nearby from 1913 to 1941. From Bend, drive 23.5 miles south on Highway 97, then 17.3 miles east on County Road 21.
excerpt: East Lake Hot Springs are natural, undeveloped springs on the south shore of East Lake in the Newberry Caldera, about 0.4 mile west of the Forest Service Hot Sp
note: The springs are underwater at high lake levels; late summer and fall are best. Recreation pass or $5 per vehicle per day at the boating site (vault toilet, no drinking water; day use only). The caldera road is closed by snow in winter.
address: Hot Springs Boating Site, East Lake, Newberry National Volcanic Monument, OR

title: Paulina Lake Hot Springs
contentHtml:
Paulina Lake Hot Springs are natural geothermal pools at Hot Springs Beach on the north shore of Paulina Lake in the Newberry Caldera. Many vents are under the lake, and the shoreline pools, dug in the sand and tempered by lake water, run about 90 to 115 degrees F with little sulfur smell.

From Bend, drive about 23 miles south on US 97, then 14 miles east on Paulina-East Lake Road to Little Crater Campground. Walk about 2 to 2.3 miles on the Paulina Lakeshore Loop Trail from the end of the campground, or come by boat.
excerpt: Paulina Lake Hot Springs are natural geothermal pools at Hot Springs Beach on the north shore of Paulina Lake in the Newberry Caldera. Many vents are under the
note: Use existing pools and don't dig new ones (sensitive shoreline). No camping or fires on Hot Springs Beach. A day-use fee or recreation pass may apply. Pools are underwater at high lake levels, and the caldera road is snow-closed in winter.
address: Little Crater Campground trailhead, Paulina Lake, Newberry National Volcanic Monument, OR

title: Lava River Cave
contentHtml:
Lava River Cave in Newberry National Volcanic Monument is the longest continuous lava tube in Oregon, its northwest section running 5,211 feet. The self-guided walk is about 2.2 miles round trip and takes about 1.5 hours, starting down 55 stairs, then over boardwalk, uneven ground and more stairs. It stays about 42 degrees F all year and is home to a bat colony.

From Bend, take Highway 97 south to Exit 151 (Cottonwood Rd), turn left through the underpass and follow the signs about 1 mile.
excerpt: Lava River Cave in Newberry National Volcanic Monument is the longest continuous lava tube in Oregon, its northwest section running 5,211 feet. The self-guided
note: Open May 15 to September 15 (2026 season), Friday to Monday; last entry 2 PM. Timed-entry ticket required from Recreation.gov (half released 7 days ahead, half 24 hours ahead, at 7 AM). $5 per vehicle or a recreation pass. Bring two light sources or rent lights on site ($7). Wear warm clothes and closed-toe shoes. No pets. Don't wear or bring clothing or gear used in any other cave or mine (white- nose syndrome). Vault toilets; no drinking water.
address: Off Highway 97 at Exit 151 (Cottonwood Rd), south of Bend, OR

title: The Last Blockbuster
contentHtml:
The last Blockbuster in the world still rents movies from its store in Bend, with more than 21,000 titles. Opened in 1992 as a Pacific Video and turned into a Blockbuster franchise in 2000, it became the last one in the U.S. in 2018 and the last on the planet in 2019.

The store is packed with Blockbuster memorabilia and film props and sells branded merchandise. Its story is told in the 2020 documentary The Last Blockbuster, made by Bend filmmakers.

title: Arnold Ice Cave
contentHtml:
Arnold Ice Cave is a lava tube southeast of Bend that traps cold air and holds ice all year. In the early 1900s its ice was mined and sold to supply Bend and Central Oregon, and the ice miners' old stairs still stand in the entrance pit. The cave itself can't be entered because it is filled with ice.

From Bend, drive about 4 miles (6 km) south on Highway 97, turn left on China Hat Road and continue about 9 miles (14 km). The cave is on the left.

note: Closed October 1 to April 30 to protect hibernating bats. The cave is inside the Cabin Butte project area, closed to all public entry since May 2025 for forest restoration. Check with the Deschutes National Forest ((541) 383-5300) before you go.
address: China Hat Road, southeast of Bend, OR (Deschutes National Forest)

title: Boyd Cave
contentHtml: Boyd Cave is a well-preserved 1,880-foot lava tube on the flank of Newberry Volcano, entered by a steel stairway and explored on your own with your own lights. It stays near 40 degrees F, and is free and normally open year-round.
excerpt: Boyd Cave is a well-preserved 1,880-foot lava tube on the flank of Newberry Volcano, entered by a steel stairway and explored on your own with your own lights.
note: The cave is inside the Cabin Butte project area, closed to all public entry since May 2025 for forest restoration. Check with the Deschutes National Forest ((541) 383-5300) before you go.

title: Hidden Forest Cave
contentHtml:
Hidden Forest Cave, part of the Arnold Ice Cave system, is a lava tube whose roof collapsed into a deep, steep-walled pit, where ponderosa pines now grow on the floor: a forest inside a cave, visible from the rim. A trail drops down one side to the cave entrance on the other. The site is sacred to Native peoples.

From Bend, drive about 4 miles (6 km) south on Highway 97, turn left on China Hat Road and continue about 9 miles (14 km). The cave is on the right.

note: Normally closed November to April 15 for hibernating bats. Fires, parties and pets are not allowed, and disturbing archaeological sites is a federal crime. The cave is inside the Cabin Butte project area, closed to all public entry since May 2025 for forest restoration. Check with the Deschutes National Forest ((541) 383-5300) before you go.

title: Redmond Caves
contentHtml:
The Redmond Caves are five small caves formed by the collapse of a single lava tube from Newberry Volcano, preserved in a BLM recreation site inside Redmond's city limits and managed with the City of Redmond. Caves 1, 3 and 4 can be entered. Native Americans used the caves for about 6,000 years.

From Highway 97 take the SW Airport Way exit, head east about a mile and park in the lot on the north side of Airport Way.

note: Free, self-guided and open year-round. No toilets or other facilities. Bring three light sources and sturdy shoes, go with someone, and watch for rattlesnakes. No pets in the caves.
address: SW Airport Way, about 0.8 mile south of Redmond Airport, Redmond, OR

title: Skylight Cave
contentHtml:
Skylight Cave is a lava tube northwest of Sisters, about 1,000 feet long, pierced by three natural skylights. On sunny summer mornings, around 8 to 10 AM, beams of sunlight angle down into the large main room, whose ceiling is about 25 feet high. A ladder leads down through the collapsed entrance.

From Highway 20/126 turn onto FR 2061 (across from the Camp Sherman turnoff) for about 5.5 miles, left on FR 1028 for about a mile, then left on FR 260 for about a mile; the entrance is on the right near a small marker for Road 266.
excerpt: Skylight Cave is a lava tube northwest of Sisters, about 1,000 feet long, pierced by three natural skylights. On sunny summer mornings, around 8 to 10 AM, beams
note: Open May 1 to September 14 only, closed the rest of the year for hibernating Townsend's big-eared bats. It is about 40 degrees F inside. Bring at least two lights, watch your head where the roof drops to 3 feet, and take care on the sharp lava.

title: 10 Barrel Brewing
contentHtml:
10 Barrel Brewing was founded in Bend in 2006, and its original West Side brewpub on NW Galveston Ave pours 20 taps with a patio and welcomes minors at all hours. The brewery is best known for Apocalypse IPA.

A second Bend pub, the East Side pub, sits at the production brewery and headquarters at 62950 18th St. 10 Barrel is now owned by Tilray.
excerpt: 10 Barrel Brewing was founded in Bend in 2006, and its original West Side brewpub on NW Galveston Ave pours 20 taps with a patio and welcomes minors at all hour
note: Hours shown are for the West Side Pub.
address: West Side Pub: 1135 NW Galveston Ave, Bend, OR 97703

title: Ale Apothecary
imageAlt: The original brewery in the woods

banner.alt: The original brewery in the woods

contentHtml:
The Ale Apothecary was founded in 2011 by Paul Arney and makes barrel-aged, all-natural wild, sour and spontaneously fermented farmhouse ales with foraged and local ingredients.

In 2026 the brewery moved from Bend to Redmond, into the former Kobold brewery space. It now focuses on brewing and its Ale Club, with no regular taproom. Beer is sold through the club and the online store, which ships to most states.
excerpt: The Ale Apothecary was founded in 2011 by Paul Arney and makes barrel-aged, all-natural wild, sour and spontaneously fermented farmhouse ales with foraged and l
note: No regular taproom; check the website for releases.
address: 675 NE Hemlock Ave, Ste 111, Redmond, OR

title: Bend Brewing Company
contentHtml:
Bend Brewing Company opened in 1995, making it the second-oldest brewpub in Bend. The downtown brewpub and beer garden overlook Mirror Pond on the Deschutes River.

Its Because Science Hazy IPA has won gold at the World Beer Cup and the Oregon Beer Awards.
excerpt: Bend Brewing Company opened in 1995, making it the second-oldest brewpub in Bend. The downtown brewpub and beer garden overlook Mirror Pond on the Deschutes Riv
address: 1019 NW Brooks St, Bend, OR 97703

title: Bevel Craft Brewing
contentHtml:
Bevel Craft Brewing was started in April 2019 by disc golf world champions Nate Doss and Valarie Jenkins. The 7-barrel brewery in southeast Bend makes hop-forward ales such as Weekend Warrior Hazy IPA.

The dog-friendly patio has four food carts (Nosh Street Food, Tacos El Nava, Little Red Kitchen and Lao Teng) and a putting course with free Discraft rental discs. Live music plays on summer Thursdays from 6 to 8 PM.
excerpt: Bevel Craft Brewing was started in April 2019 by disc golf world champions Nate Doss and Valarie Jenkins. The 7-barrel brewery in southeast Bend makes hop-forwa
address: 911 SE Armour Rd, Bend, OR 97702

title: Boneyard Beer
contentHtml:
Boneyard Beer was founded in 2010 in a former auto shop, with a brewhouse built from equipment salvaged from 13 breweries. The original Lake Place tasting room sells crowlers and six-packs and has seating among hop bines.

Signature beers are RPM IPA, Bone-A-Fide Pale and Hop Venom Double IPA. Boneyard has been owned by Deschutes Brewery since 2021.
excerpt: Boneyard Beer was founded in 2010 in a former auto shop, with a brewhouse built from equipment salvaged from 13 breweries. The original Lake Place tasting room
note: Wednesday is locals' day. The Boneyard Pub on NE Division St closed on Oct 11, 2026.
address: Tasting Room: 37 NW Lake Place, Bend, OR 97703

title: Bridge 99 Brewery
contentHtml:
Bridge 99 Brewery is a small-batch brewery that has been growing since 2013. It is named for a bridge on the Metolius River.

The taproom has a full bar and food, and kids and dogs are welcome.
excerpt: Bridge 99 Brewery is a small-batch brewery that has been growing since 2013. It is named for a bridge on the Metolius River.
note: The brewery was listed for sale in 2026 but is still pouring.
address: 63063 Layton Ave, Bend, OR 97701

title: Cascade Lakes Brewing Company
contentHtml:
Cascade Lakes Brewing Company was founded in Redmond in 1994 and is Central Oregon's first and only not- for-profit brewery. Its original 7th Street pub is in Redmond.

There is also a Pub on Reed Market at 21175 SE Reed Market Rd in Bend (458-836-7866) and the production brewery at 2141 SW 1st St in Redmond (541-923-3110).
excerpt: Cascade Lakes Brewing Company was founded in Redmond in 1994 and is Central Oregon's first and only not- for-profit brewery. Its original 7th Street pub is in R
note: Part of the Oregon Beverage Collective, formed in 2026.
address: 7th Street Pub: 855 SW 7th St, Redmond, OR 97756

title: Craft Kitchen & Brewery
contentHtml:
Craft Kitchen & Brewery is a small-batch brewpub in northeast Bend that pairs beer from its 7-barrel system with from-scratch barbecue smoked in house over local orchard wood.

Brisket and burnt ends are served daily.
excerpt: Craft Kitchen & Brewery is a small-batch brewpub in northeast Bend that pairs beer from its 7-barrel system with from-scratch barbecue smoked in house over loca
address: 62988 Layton Ave #103, Bend, OR 97701

title: Crux Fermentation Project
contentHtml:
Crux Fermentation Project opened in 2012 in a former transmission shop and is known for barrel-aged and experimental beers, using methods such as decoction mashing, open fermentation, oak barrel aging and wild yeast.

Its tasting room and big lawn on SW Division St are one of Bend's most popular outdoor hangouts, with views of the Cascade Range at sunset.
excerpt: Crux Fermentation Project opened in 2012 in a former transmission shop and is known for barrel-aged and experimental beers, using methods such as decoction mash
note: Brewing moved to a production facility in northeast Bend after Crux was acquired by the Oregon Beverage Collective in February 2026. The Division St tasting room and lawn remain open.
address: 50 SW Division St, Bend, OR

title: Deschutes Brewery
contentHtml:
Deschutes Brewery opened in 1988 and is Oregon's largest craft brewery, family and employee owned. The downtown Bend Public House is where it brewed its first beers, including Black Butte Porter and Jubelale; Mirror Pond Pale Ale is another flagship.

The pub has 19 taps, farm-to-table pub food and an upstairs game room with shuffleboard and vintage video games. There is also a Tasting Room at the production brewery, 901 SW Simpson Ave.
excerpt: Deschutes Brewery opened in 1988 and is Oregon's largest craft brewery, family and employee owned. The downtown Bend Public House is where it brewed its first b
note: Hours shown are for the Bend Public House.
address: Bend Public House: 1044 NW Bond St, Bend, OR 97703

title: Funky Fauna Artisan Ales
contentHtml:
Funky Fauna Artisan Ales was opened in Sisters in late 2021 by Michael Frith and Danielle Burns. It makes oak- fermented, fruit-forward saisons and farmhouse ales with a wild yeast culture captured from Central Oregon air, using Oregon-grown malt and hops.

In April 2025 the brewery moved to Bend, into the former Humm Kombucha taproom in the Central District.
excerpt: Funky Fauna Artisan Ales was opened in Sisters in late 2021 by Michael Frith and Danielle Burns. It makes oak- fermented, fruit-forward saisons and farmhouse al
address: 1125 NE 2nd St, Bend, OR

title: GoodLife Brewing Company
contentHtml:
GoodLife Brewing Company was founded in Bend in 2011 and brews balanced ales with Northwest and imported hops and Central Oregon water. The name reflects the outdoor lifestyle of its hometown, and the brewery has won three GABF medals.

It is best known for Sweet As! Pacific Ale; other beers include Wave Park Hazy IPA, Descender IPA and Comatose Imperial IPA. The brewery and biergarten are on SW Century Dr.
excerpt: GoodLife Brewing Company was founded in Bend in 2011 and brews balanced ales with Northwest and imported hops and Central Oregon water. The name reflects the ou
note: Now part of the Oregon Beverage Collective (2026).
address: 70 SW Century Dr, Bend, OR 97702

title: Initiative Brewing
contentHtml:
Initiative Brewing was founded in 2019 by Ryan and Chris, and makes its beer, food and cocktails in house. The original pub, The Hub, is in downtown Redmond.

The menu includes burgers, Bavarian pretzels, jerk wings and bowls. Catering, private parties and online reservations are available.
excerpt: Initiative Brewing was founded in 2019 by Ryan and Chris, and makes its beer, food and cocktails in house. The original pub, The Hub, is in downtown Redmond.
note: Other locations: The Station beer garden in Prineville (Crook County) and The Fortress in Madras (Jefferson County).
address: The Hub: 424 NW 5th St, Redmond, OR 97756

title: Kobold Brewing
contentHtml:
Kobold Brewing was started in Redmond in 2015 by Steve Anderson. The Vault, its original taphouse in downtown Redmond, is family friendly, with sports on TV, cards and cribbage, and a patio with a fire pit.

A Westside Taco Co. food truck parks on the patio, and the taphouse sells popcorn and Schatz pretzels. Kobold also has The Lair at 1043 NW Bond St in Bend.
excerpt: Kobold Brewing was started in Redmond in 2015 by Steve Anderson. The Vault, its original taphouse in downtown Redmond, is family friendly, with sports on TV, ca
note: Hours shown are for The Vault and may change for events and private parties.
address: The Vault: 245 SW 6th St, Redmond, OR 97756

title: Monkless Belgian Ales
contentHtml:
Monkless Belgian Ales has brewed only Belgian-style ales since 2014. The Brasserie is its riverfront restaurant, pairing the beers with traditional European dishes.

The Abbey tasting room is inside the production brewery at 900 SE Wilson Ave. Featured beers include Samaritan's Saison, Four Devils strong golden ale and Pour Pour Pitiful Me, a World Beer Cup silver medalist.
excerpt: Monkless Belgian Ales has brewed only Belgian-style ales since 2014. The Brasserie is its riverfront restaurant, pairing the beers with traditional European dis
note: Hours shown are for The Brasserie. The Abbey is open Wednesday to Saturday, 3 - 8 PM.
address: The Brasserie: 803 SW Industrial Way, Bend, OR 97702

title: Oblivion Brewing
contentHtml:
Oblivion Brewing has brewed in Bend since 2013. Its public home is now Oblivion Pour House, a sports bar and grill in southeast Bend that shows NFL games and UFC fights.

The menu includes pizza, wings, burgers, BBQ ribs and fish and chips in Oblivion IPA batter.
excerpt: Oblivion Brewing has brewed in Bend since 2013. Its public home is now Oblivion Pour House, a sports bar and grill in southeast Bend that shows NFL games and UF
note: The former brewery and tasting room at 63027 Plateau Dr is permanently closed.
address: Oblivion Pour House: 61276 S Hwy 97, Ste 140, Bend, OR 97702

title: Porter Brewing Company
contentHtml:
Porter Brewing Company is Oregon's only all-cask brewery, making 100% cask-conditioned real ales. The unfiltered, unpasteurized beers are naturally carbonated in the cask, hand-pumped through English beer engines and served at cellar temperature.

The Cellar, its basement pub in downtown Bend, pours small-batch English ales, IPAs, stouts and porters in 20 oz pints, 10 oz half pints and tasting flights.
excerpt: Porter Brewing Company is Oregon's only all-cask brewery, making 100% cask-conditioned real ales. The unfiltered, unpasteurized beers are naturally carbonated i
note: Production moved to La Pine in 2023; the original Redmond taproom has closed.
address: The Cellar: 206 NW Oregon Ave #2, Bend, OR 97703

title: Shade Tree Brewing
imageAlt: Corvette Strong Ale with its awards

banner.alt: Corvette Strong Ale with its awards

contentHtml:
Shade Tree Brewing is a tiny microbrewery opened in 2012 and run solely by Larry Johnson, a former mechanic, from a shop on his property in Deschutes River Woods in south Bend. The taps are made from Hurst shifters, and a classic Ford Mustang sits inside the brewery.

It brews English- and German-style beers. Its Corvette Strong Ale won bronze at the 2017 Best of Craft Beer Awards.
excerpt: Shade Tree Brewing is a tiny microbrewery opened in 2012 and run solely by Larry Johnson, a former mechanic, from a shop on his property in Deschutes River Wood
note: Visits by appointment only. Book by phone or through the website. Beer is sold only at the brewery.
address: 19305 Indian Summer Rd, Bend, OR
photoCredit: Shade Tree Brewing (via The Source Weekly)

title: Silver Moon Brewing
contentHtml:
Silver Moon Brewing has poured beer since 2000, making it Bend's third-oldest brewery. The downtown pub hosts more than 300 live music events a year across three stages, plus trivia and mic nights, with food carts on site.

Beers include its Flagship IPA, Hazy IPA, Craft Mexican Lager and World Famous Mango Ale.
excerpt: Silver Moon Brewing has poured beer since 2000, making it Bend's third-oldest brewery. The downtown pub hosts more than 300 live music events a year across thre
note: Part of the Oregon Beverage Collective. The property was listed for sale with a leaseback in 2026, and the pub continues to operate.
address: 24 NW Greenwood Ave, Bend, OR 97703

title: Spider City Brewing Company
contentHtml: Spider City Brewing Company is a woman-owned Bend brewery that has operated since 2018.
excerpt: Spider City Brewing Company is a woman-owned Bend brewery that has operated since 2018.
note: Temporarily closed. The brewery left its building at 1177 SE 9th St in September 2026 and is relocating to a new location that has not been announced yet.

title: Sunriver Brewing Company
contentHtml:
Sunriver Brewing Company is an independent, locally owned brewery founded in Sunriver in 2012. Its original Sunriver Pub is in The Village at Sunriver.

It was named Brewery and Brewer of the Year at the Great American Beer Festival in 2017 and 2024. Other Central Oregon locations: the Tap Room at the production brewery (56840 Venture Ln, Sunriver), the Eastside Pub (1500 NE Cushing Dr, Bend) and the Redmond Pub (3750 SW Badger Ave).
excerpt: Sunriver Brewing Company is an independent, locally owned brewery founded in Sunriver in 2012. Its original Sunriver Pub is in The Village at Sunriver.
note: Hours shown are for the Sunriver Pub. Sunriver Brewing also has an Oakway Pub in Eugene.
address: Sunriver Pub: 57100 Beaver Dr, Bldg 4, Sunriver, OR 97707

title: Terranaut Beer
contentHtml:
Terranaut Beer was founded in 2024 by Bryon Pyka, formerly 10 Barrel's innovation brewer, and brews lagers, classic styles and experimental beers.

It was named Small Brewery of the Year at the 2025 Oregon Beer Awards.
excerpt: Terranaut Beer was founded in 2024 by Bryon Pyka, formerly 10 Barrel's innovation brewer, and brews lagers, classic styles and experimental beers.
note: 21 and over only.
address: 20750 High Desert Ln, Ste 106, Bend, OR 97701

title: UPP Liquids
contentHtml:
UPP Liquids is a brewer-owned brewery and restaurant that opened in 2025 in the Box Factory, in the former Immersion Brewing space. It was started by 10 Barrel's former innovation team, led by brewmaster Tonya Cornett, together with Immersion's owners.

It brews small-batch IPAs, lagers and seasonal beers with a from-scratch kitchen. At the 2025 Great American Beer Festival it won five medals and Brewery of the Year in its size category.
excerpt: UPP Liquids is a brewer-owned brewery and restaurant that opened in 2025 in the Box Factory, in the former Immersion Brewing space. It was started by 10 Barrel'
note: The Barrel Room next door is available for private events.
address: 550 SW Industrial Way, Ste 185, Bend, OR 97702

title: Van Henion Brewing Company
contentHtml:
Van Henion Brewing Company was founded in 2021 and is brewer owned and operated. It makes clean German-style lagers, each aged at least eight weeks in tank, plus bright IPAs.

The tasting room is in the northeast Bend brewers district, with a food truck always on site.
excerpt: Van Henion Brewing Company was founded in 2021 and is brewer owned and operated. It makes clean German-style lagers, each aged at least eight weeks in tank, plu
address: 63067 Plateau Ct, Bend, OR 97701

title: Wild Ride Brewing
contentHtml:
Wild Ride Brewing was founded in 2014 and calls itself a community-driven brewery. Its downtown Redmond home combines the production brewery with a family-friendly taproom, where you can watch the brewing from inside or from the dog-friendly patio.

Beers range from crisp lagers and hazy IPAs to winter stouts and seasonal releases, with rotating local food carts.
excerpt: Wild Ride Brewing was founded in 2014 and calls itself a community-driven brewery. Its downtown Redmond home combines the production brewery with a family-frien
note: A second location opened in May 2022 in Prineville (Crook County) at 1500 NE 3rd St.
address: 332 SW 5th St, Redmond, OR 97756

title: Worthy Brewing
contentHtml:
Worthy Brewing opened in east Bend in 2013 and is known for hop-forward beers and a full food menu. The tap list rotates between flagships, small-batch experiments and seasonal beers.

The pub is home to the Hopservatory, a dome above the pub with a 16-inch research-grade telescope, run by the Worthy Garden Club.
excerpt: Worthy Brewing opened in east Bend in 2013 and is known for hop-forward beers and a full food menu. The tap list rotates between flagships, small-batch experime
note: The Downtown location at 806 NW Brooks St is shown as permanently closed.
address: 495 NE Bellevue Dr, Bend, OR 97701

title: Faith, Hope and Charity Vineyards
contentHtml:
Faith, Hope and Charity Vineyards is a winery and estate vineyard in a canyon outside Terrebonne, with views of the Three Sisters peaks it is named for. The 15-acre vineyard of cold-hardy French-American hybrids sits on a 312-acre estate, and the winery also sources Merlot, Syrah and Pinot Noir grapes from the Columbia Valley and Eola-Amity Hills.

Visitors can taste in the tasting room, relax on the patio or walk the vineyard. The estate is also a major events and wedding venue, hosting live music, wine release parties and winemaker dinners.
excerpt: Faith, Hope and Charity Vineyards is a winery and estate vineyard in a canyon outside Terrebonne, with views of the Three Sisters peaks it is named for. The 15-
note: Live music Friday and Saturday, 5 - 8 PM.
address: 70450 NW Lower Valley Dr, Terrebonne, OR 97760

title: Lava Terrace Cellars
contentHtml:
Lava Terrace Cellars is a small, high-elevation winery and vineyard in Bend, owned by Duane and Dina Barker. About 5.5 acres at roughly 3,440 feet, once sagebrush and lava rock, grow cold-hardy hybrid grapes: La Crescent and Brianna for whites, and Marechal Foch and Marquette for reds.

Its wines have won silver and bronze medals at the Sunset International and San Francisco International wine competitions. Wine can be ordered on the website, with local delivery in Deschutes, Jefferson and Crook counties.
excerpt: Lava Terrace Cellars is a small, high-elevation winery and vineyard in Bend, owned by Duane and Dina Barker. About 5.5 acres at roughly 3,440 feet, once sagebru
note: Tastings by reservation and at limited events.
address: 20520 Bowery Ln, Bend, OR

title: Redside Ranch
imageAlt: Ryder Redfield and Kerry Damon at the vineyard

banner.alt: Ryder Redfield and Kerry Damon at the vineyard

contentHtml:
Redside Ranch is a research vineyard on a 400-acre ranch west of Terrebonne, near the Deschutes River. It grows about five acres of own-rooted Marquette, a cold-hardy hybrid grape, on a steep, south-facing hillside.

The Dunn family first planted the vineyard in 2009, and Kris Kibak bought the ranch in 2017. The wine is made by Elixir Wine Group in Bend, and the 2019 Redside Ranch Marquette won gold at the 21st San Francisco Wine Competition.
excerpt: Redside Ranch is a research vineyard on a 400-acre ranch west of Terrebonne, near the Deschutes River. It grows about five acres of own-rooted Marquette, a cold
note: Vineyard only. No public tasting room; tours only through occasional COCC classes.
address: Near Terrebonne, OR

title: The Grapeyard
contentHtml:
The Grapeyard is a high desert vineyard on the northern edge of Bend, where Frank and Carol Brian planted 9 of their 39 acres to cold-hardy hybrid grapes: Marquette, Frontenac Gris and La Crescent.

Overhead sprinklers protect the vines from frost.
excerpt: The Grapeyard is a high desert vineyard on the northern edge of Bend, where Frank and Carol Brian planted 9 of their 39 acres to cold-hardy hybrid grapes: Marqu
note: Vineyard only. No winery or tasting room.
address: Northern edge of Bend, OR

title: Bend Pine Nursery

gallery.alt: Hole 18 with a view of the mountains

contentHtml:
Bend Pine Nursery is a free 18-basket course in Bend Park and Recreation's Pine Nursery Park, with views of the Cascades. The main layout runs about 5,525 feet over sandy, hilly ground with natural lava outcroppings, juniper and sagebrush.

It has concrete tees, restrooms and drinking water. Dogs are allowed.
excerpt: Bend Pine Nursery is a free 18-basket course in Bend Park and Recreation's Pine Nursery Park, with views of the Cascades. The main layout runs about 5,525 feet
note: Free. Jagged lava rock can damage discs. Not cart or stroller friendly.
address: Pine Nursery Park, Bend, OR

title: Cline Falls
contentHtml:
Cline Falls is a free 18-hole course on BLM land along the Deschutes River near Redmond, established in 2010. The roughly 4,882-foot, par 55 layout winds through juniper over hilly ground, with tone poles as targets and views of Cline Falls and Cline Butte.

Tees are dirt, marked with blue squares, and rock arrows at each pin point to the next tee. Dogs are allowed.
excerpt: Cline Falls is a free 18-hole course on BLM land along the Deschutes River near Redmond, established in 2010. The roughly 4,882-foot, par 55 layout winds throug
note: Free. Park on the northeast side of the bridge and take the path at the end of the guardrail; Google Maps directions lead down an abandoned road. The land is shared with hikers and dog walkers.
address: Cline Falls, Redmond, OR (BLM land)

title: Dry Canyon
contentHtml:
Dry Canyon is a free 9-hole, par 27 course in Redmond's Dry Canyon park, with two baskets per hole. The flat, quick course on soft dirt with a few trees is popular with locals.

It has concrete tees and a portable toilet near the parking lot and dog park entrance. Dogs are allowed.
excerpt: Dry Canyon is a free 9-hole, par 27 course in Redmond's Dry Canyon park, with two baskets per hole. The flat, quick course on soft dirt with a few trees is popu
note: Free. No drinking water.
address: Dry Canyon, Redmond, OR

title: Hyzer Pines

gallery.alt: Basket 15 looking back to the tee

contentHtml:
Hyzer Pines is a free 18-hole course in Sisters, managed by Sisters Park & Recreation District on school district land and established in 2006. The flat, wooded course runs about 2.4 miles through ponderosa pines and sagebrush at about 3,100 feet, with one water hazard.

It has rubber mat tees, Innova DISCatcher Pro baskets, restrooms and drinking water. Dogs are allowed.
excerpt: Hyzer Pines is a free 18-hole course in Sisters, managed by Sisters Park & Recreation District on school district land and established in 2006. The flat, wooded
note: Free. No alcohol and no smoking.
address: Next to Sisters High School and Sisters Park & Recreation District, Sisters, OR

title: Paulina View DGC
contentHtml:
Paulina View is a free, challenging course in La Pine with 18 baskets on the main par 65 layout of about 7,000 feet. The flat course has mandos with marked drop zones, a hole with an ice-cream-cone-shaped green and two hanging baskets.

Tees are rubber mats, with benches around the course and lost-disc lockers at the start. Dogs are allowed.
excerpt: Paulina View is a free, challenging course in La Pine with 18 baskets on the main par 65 layout of about 7,000 feet. The flat course has mandos with marked drop
note: Free. Follow the power line road north to the first right, then about 600 ft to the parking lot. No restrooms or drinking water. High fire danger: no smoking or open flames.
address: La Pine, OR

title: Rockridge Park
contentHtml:
Rockridge Park has a free putting course with 9 baskets and 18 tees, established in 2017. All holes are short, built for practicing medium to long putts, which makes it beginner friendly and quick to play.

Tees are brick pavers on flat ground.
excerpt: Rockridge Park has a free putting course with 9 baskets and 18 tees, established in 2017. All holes are short, built for practicing medium to long putts, which
note: Free. Watch for sharp rocks.
address: Rockridge Park, Bend, OR

title: Sunriver SHARC
imageAlt: Course info at the first hole

banner.alt: Course info at the first hole

contentHtml:
Sunriver SHARC is a free 9-hole, par 27 course behind the SHARC tubing hill, established in 2016. The short holes play up, down and around the hill and through some woods.

It is a good beginner course and a practice course for advanced players.
excerpt: Sunriver SHARC is a free 9-hole, par 27 course behind the SHARC tubing hill, established in 2016. The short holes play up, down and around the hill and through
note: Free. Some baskets near the tubing hill may be removed in winter for sledding.
address: Behind the SHARC tubing hill, Sunriver, OR

title: Douglas County Museum of Natural & Cultural History
contentHtml:
The Douglas County Museum of Natural & Cultural History has collected, preserved and exhibited the area's natural and cultural history for more than 50 years. It is a division of Douglas County government, run with the Douglas County Museum Foundation.

Exhibits include a new O&C Railroad railcar exhibit and an exhibit on the 2020 Archie Creek Fire. There is a children's dig pit, the Museum Mercantile gift shop and an event space.
excerpt: The Douglas County Museum of Natural & Cultural History has collected, preserved and exhibited the area's natural and cultural history for more than 50 years. I
note: Off I-5 Exit 123, by the fairgrounds.
address: 123 Museum Dr, Roseburg, OR 97471

title: Umpqua River Lighthouse Museum
contentHtml:
The Umpqua River Lighthouse Museum is the second site of the Umpqua Valley Museums, below the lighthouse that towers over the beach where the Umpqua River meets the Pacific Ocean.

It offers lighthouse tours, a local artisans gallery and a cafe and gift shop.
excerpt: The Umpqua River Lighthouse Museum is the second site of the Umpqua Valley Museums, below the lighthouse that towers over the beach where the Umpqua River meets
note: Lighthouse tours are seasonal. Cafe and gift shop: 541-271-1894.
address: 1020 Lighthouse Rd, Winchester Bay, OR 97467

title: Umpqua Discovery Center
contentHtml:
The Umpqua Discovery Center is a 7,000-square-foot natural and cultural history museum on Reedsport's Umpqua riverfront. Its Tidewaters & Time exhibit covers local history from Native peoples and early explorers through pioneer life and logging, with a walk-through fish cannery and tidewater town.

The Pathways to Discovery wing is a simulated journey through an estuary, a winter forest with a bear cave, a weather station, a mountain meadow and a dune sunset. There is also a 50-seat theater, a 35-foot periscope, and a gift and book shop.
excerpt: The Umpqua Discovery Center is a 7,000-square-foot natural and cultural history museum on Reedsport's Umpqua riverfront. Its Tidewaters & Time exhibit covers lo
note: A totem pole marks the entrance, reached from the street or the riverfront boardwalk.
address: 409 Riverfront Way, Reedsport, OR 97467

title: Oakland Museum
contentHtml:
The Oakland Museum is run by volunteers of the Oakland Museum Historical Society in an 1893 brick block in Oakland, Oregon's first historic district. Period-room displays show everyday life in the 1800s, alongside railroad and timber artifacts.

The museum also has a map for the town's self-guided historic walking tour.
excerpt: The Oakland Museum is run by volunteers of the Oakland Museum Historical Society in an 1893 brick block in Oakland, Oregon's first historic district. Period-roo
note: Free admission. Open every day except holidays.
address: 130 Locust St, Oakland, OR 97462

title: South Umpqua Pioneer–Indian Museum
contentHtml:
The South Umpqua Pioneer-Indian Museum, run by the South Umpqua Historical Society, tells the story of Southern Oregon's Native tribes and the pioneer settlement of south Douglas County. The main building holds pioneer furniture and needlework, and Native baskets, beadwork and tools, including Cow Creek Tribe items.

Other buildings hold a restored gold stamp mill, vintage tractors and cars, logging and mining displays, a wheelwright and blacksmith shop, a former Justice Court and a Cow Creek cedar plank house surrounded by native plants.
excerpt: The South Umpqua Pioneer-Indian Museum, run by the South Umpqua Historical Society, tells the story of Southern Oregon's Native tribes and the pioneer settlemen
note: Free admission; donations welcome. Group tours can be arranged.
address: 421 SW 5th St, Canyonville, OR 97417

title: Rogue River-Siskiyou National Forest
contentHtml:
The Rogue River-Siskiyou National Forest covers about 1.8 million acres of southwest Oregon, from the Cascades to the coast, managed through five ranger districts: High Cascades, Siskiyou Mountains, Wild Rivers, Gold Beach and Powers.

Highlights across the forest include Applegate Lake, Mount McLoughlin and the Siskiyou and Sky Lakes wilderness areas. In Douglas County the forest reaches the upper Rogue country along OR 230.
excerpt: The Rogue River-Siskiyou National Forest covers about 1.8 million acres of southwest Oregon, from the Cascades to the coast, managed through five ranger distric
note: Forest headquarters is in Medford.
address: 3040 Biddle Rd, Medford, OR 97504

title: Siuslaw National Forest
contentHtml:
The Siuslaw National Forest covers more than 630,000 acres of the Oregon coast and Coast Range, and is one of only two national forests in the lower 48 states with oceanfront land. Its landscapes run from mossy coastal mountain forests to sand dunes and Pacific beaches.

Highlights include Cape Perpetua Scenic Area with its rocky headlands, Cascade Head with native prairie and rare wildflowers, the Oregon Dunes National Recreation Area, and Marys Peak, the highest point in the Coast Range, just west of Corvallis. Visitors come for old-growth forest, waterfalls, camping and off-highway vehicle riding on the dunes.
excerpt: The Siuslaw National Forest covers more than 630,000 acres of the Oregon coast and Coast Range, and is one of only two national forests in the lower 48 states w
note: Forest headquarters is in Corvallis
address: 3200 SW Jefferson Way, Corvallis, OR 97331
photoCredit: USDA Forest Service, Siuslaw National Forest

title: Umpqua National Forest
contentHtml:
The Umpqua National Forest covers about 983,000 acres on the western slopes of the Oregon Cascades in Douglas, Lane and Jackson counties. Its landscape was shaped by high Cascade glaciers, volcanic activity and whitewater rivers, and it is known for its biodiversity, recreation and scenery.

It is managed through four ranger districts: Cottage Grove, Diamond Lake, North Umpqua and Tiller. Highlights include Toketee Falls and the waterfalls of the North Umpqua corridor, Diamond Lake, and the Boulder Creek, Mount Thielsen and Rogue-Umpqua Divide wilderness areas.
excerpt: The Umpqua National Forest covers about 983,000 acres on the western slopes of the Oregon Cascades in Douglas, Lane and Jackson counties. Its landscape was shap
note: Forest headquarters is in Roseburg.
address: Supervisor's Office: 777 NW Garden Valley Blvd, Roseburg, OR 97471
photoCredit: USDA Forest Service, Umpqua National Forest

title: Willamette National Forest
contentHtml:
The Willamette National Forest runs about 110 miles along the western slopes of the Oregon Cascades and covers 1,675,407 acres of high mountains, narrow canyons, fast streams and wooded slopes. About 61% of it lies in Lane County, with large areas in Linn, Marion and Douglas counties.

It holds eight wilderness areas and seven major volcanic peaks, and offers year-round hiking, backpacking, camping, fishing, waterfalls and skiing.
excerpt: The Willamette National Forest runs about 110 miles along the western slopes of the Oregon Cascades and covers 1,675,407 acres of high mountains, narrow canyons
address: Supervisor's Office: 3106 Pierce Parkway, Suite D, Springfield, OR 97477

title: Boulder Creek Wilderness
contentHtml:
The Boulder Creek Wilderness covers about 19,100 acres of the Umpqua National Forest, about 50 miles east of Roseburg, and was designated in 1984. Small waterfalls and rapids link quiet pools along Boulder Creek, a tributary of the North Umpqua River, with elevations from 1,600 to 5,600 feet.

Near the lower end, Pine Bench holds what may be the largest stand of ponderosa pines this far northwest of the Cascade crest. Rocky monoliths in the Umpqua Rocks Special Interest Geologic Area draw technical climbers.
excerpt: The Boulder Creek Wilderness covers about 19,100 acres of the Umpqua National Forest, about 50 miles east of Roseburg, and was designated in 1984. Small waterfa
note: The 1996 Spring Fire and 2008 Rattle Fire burned most of the area: expect dense brush and fallen trees on the roughly 10 miles of maintained trails. Groups up to 12 people, including livestock. No motorized or mechanized equipment.
address: Boulder Creek Trailhead, North Umpqua River, near Idleyld Park, OR

title: Devil's Staircase Wilderness
contentHtml:
The Devil's Staircase Wilderness protects about 30,000 acres of old-growth forest in the Oregon Coast Range between the Umpqua and Smith rivers. Designated in 2019, it is managed jointly by the U.S. Forest Service and the BLM, and named for the stair-step falls on Wasson Creek.

Douglas-fir, western hemlock and cedar tower over ferns and huckleberry, and the forest is home to northern spotted owls and marbled murrelets.
excerpt: The Devil's Staircase Wilderness protects about 30,000 acres of old-growth forest in the Oregon Coast Range between the Umpqua and Smith rivers. Designated in 2
note: Trailless, with no facilities and unsigned junctions: bring a map and compass. A high-clearance vehicle is recommended, and cell and GPS coverage is spotty. Contact: BLM Coos Bay District Office, 1300 Airport Lane, North Bend.
address: Wasson Lake area, Oregon Coast Range east of Reedsport, OR

title: Mount Thielsen Wilderness
contentHtml:
The Mount Thielsen Wilderness covers about 55,000 acres along the Cascade crest just north of Crater Lake, in the Umpqua, Deschutes and Fremont-Winema national forests. Designated in 1984, it rises from 5,000 feet to the 9,182-foot spire of Mount Thielsen, the 'Lightning Rod of the Cascades.'

About 78 miles of trails include 26 miles of the Pacific Crest Trail. The North Umpqua Trail leads to Lake Lucille and Maidu Lake, where the North Umpqua River begins. Alpine wildflowers peak in August.
excerpt: The Mount Thielsen Wilderness covers about 55,000 acres along the Cascade crest just north of Crater Lake, in the Umpqua, Deschutes and Fremont-Winema national
note: Groups up to 20 people, including livestock. The Mount Thielsen summit trail ends in a 200-foot hand- over-hand scramble.
address: Mount Thielsen, north of Crater Lake National Park, OR

title: Rogue–Umpqua Divide Wilderness
contentHtml:
The Rogue-Umpqua Divide Wilderness covers about 33,200 acres along the ridge between the Rogue and Umpqua rivers, in the Umpqua and Rogue River-Siskiyou national forests. Designated in 1984, it ranges from 3,000 feet to 6,783 feet at Fish Mountain.

Volcanic and sedimentary outcrops rise above dense conifer forest and subalpine meadows that bloom with wildflowers in summer. About 100 miles of trails include the Rogue-Umpqua Divide National Recreation Trail, and the Acker Divide and Cripple Camp trails pass through big old-growth stands.
excerpt: The Rogue-Umpqua Divide Wilderness covers about 33,200 acres along the ridge between the Rogue and Umpqua rivers, in the Umpqua and Rogue River-Siskiyou nationa
note: Usually snow-free by mid-July. Groups up to 20 people, including livestock.
address: Fish Mountain area, about 10 miles west of Crater Lake National Park, OR

title: Cavitt Creek Falls Recreation Site
imageAlt: Cavitt Creek Falls in early summer

banner.alt: Cavitt Creek Falls in early summer

contentHtml:
Cavitt Creek Falls Recreation Site is a quiet spot off the North Umpqua corridor, shaded by fir, maple and cedar. The main draw is a swimming hole at the base of a six-foot waterfall on Cavitt Creek, reached by a stairway.

Ten campsites sit on three terraced levels above the falls, with a day-use area, drinking water and vault restrooms. Trout fishing is open with artificial flies and lures only.
excerpt: Cavitt Creek Falls Recreation Site is a quiet spot off the North Umpqua corridor, shaded by fir, maple and cedar. The main draw is a swimming hole at the base o
note: $14 per night. Reservations required at least one day ahead on Recreation.gov. Maximum vehicle length 34 ft. From Roseburg, take Hwy 138 east 16.5 miles, Little River Rd south 6.7 miles, then New Bridge Rd (becomes Cavitt Creek Rd) 3.2 miles west.
address: Cavitt Creek Rd, Roseburg, OR (Roseburg District Office: 777 NW Garden Valley Blvd, Roseburg, OR 97471)

title: Eagleview Group Campground
contentHtml:
Eagleview Group Campground is a riverside group site on the Umpqua River between the coast and Roseburg, with 10 campsites for up to 100 campers.

It has a covered pavilion, group picnic area and fire pit, a grassy field for games, a small disc golf course and horseshoe pits. Depending on the season, anglers fish for Chinook and coho salmon, steelhead and smallmouth bass, and the river is used for kayaking, canoeing and swimming.
excerpt: Eagleview Group Campground is a riverside group site on the Umpqua River between the coast and Roseburg, with 10 campsites for up to 100 campers.
note: $145 per day plus a $200 deposit; reserve on Recreation.gov. From Sutherlin, take Hwy 138 west 12 miles, cross the Bullock Bridge, then turn right on Bullock Rd for 1 mile.
address: 1771 Bullock Rd, Oakland, OR 97462

title: East Shore Recreation Site
contentHtml:
East Shore Recreation Site is a small, shady campground one mile east of the main Loon Lake area, with a day- use area across the road.

Its 6 campsites (one accessible) each have a table, fire pit and barbecue grill, and there are 2 day-use picnic sites.
excerpt: East Shore Recreation Site is a small, shady campground one mile east of the main Loon Lake area, with a day- use area across the road.
note: First come, first served. Camping $15 per night, extra vehicle $7, day use $5; pay on site with the Recreation.gov app. 14-day limit. From Reedsport, take Hwy 38 east 13 miles, then Loon Lake Rd 8 miles.
address: Loon Lake Rd, Reedsport, OR (BLM Coos Bay District: 1300 Airport Lane, North Bend, OR 97459)

title: Fawn Creek Campground
contentHtml:
Fawn Creek Campground is a primitive two-site campground on the Smith River at the mouth of Fawn Creek, with a small boat ramp.

It is a quiet base for fishing, boating and picnicking.
excerpt: Fawn Creek Campground is a primitive two-site campground on the Smith River at the mouth of Fawn Creek, with a small boat ramp.
note: No fee. There is no sign at the site: about 25 miles up Smith River Rd from Hwy 101 near Reedsport, look for an old road between the main road and the river.
address: Smith River Rd, about 25 miles from Reedsport, OR

title: Lone Pine Group Campground
contentHtml:
Lone Pine Group Campground sits beside Rock Creek, a tributary of the North Umpqua River, on the site of a 1930s-1950s sawmill. Its 11 sites are on a loop, with a pavilion and ball field.

Swimming is popular in summer, and salmon and steelhead spawn upstream in spring and fall. The campground reopened in 2025 after the 2020 Archie Creek Fire.
excerpt: Lone Pine Group Campground sits beside Rock Creek, a tributary of the North Umpqua River, on the site of a 1930s-1950s sawmill. Its 11 sites are on a loop, with
note: $10 per night. Reservations required at least 5 days ahead on Recreation.gov. Rock Creek is closed to fishing. From Roseburg, take Hwy 138 east 22 miles, then Rock Creek Rd north about 5.25 miles.
address: 25006 Rock Creek Rd, Idleyld Park, OR 97447

title: Loon Lake Recreation Site
imageAlt: Loon Lake from the day-use beach

banner.alt: Loon Lake from the day-use beach

gallery.alt: A shady campsite with a lake view
The waterfall near the day-use area

contentHtml:
Loon Lake Recreation Site is a family campground in the Oregon Coast Range with a warm, sandy beach on a naturally dammed lake of about 260 acres, used for swimming, fishing, boating and paddling.

It has 53 campsites and 30 day-use picnic sites along the beach, plus a boat launch, fishing dock, swim area, amphitheater, children's play area and a short paved trail to a waterfall.
excerpt: Loon Lake Recreation Site is a family campground in the Oregon Coast Range with a warm, sandy beach on a naturally dammed lake of about 260 acres, used for swim
note: Camping $18 single, $36 double, $7 extra vehicle; day use $5 per vehicle. Reserve on Recreation.gov. No cell coverage. From Reedsport, take Hwy 38 east 13 miles, then Loon Lake Rd south 7 miles.
address: 7273 Loon Lake Rd, Reedsport, OR 97467

title: Millpond Recreation Site
contentHtml:
Millpond Recreation Site is a forested campground and day-use area on Rock Creek near the North Umpqua River, with 12 campsites on a loop.

It has a swimming beach, pavilion, playground, horseshoe pits, a ball field and the roughly 1-mile Sawmill Trail.
excerpt: Millpond Recreation Site is a forested campground and day-use area on Rock Creek near the North Umpqua River, with 12 campsites on a loop.
note: Closed until further notice due to wildfire damage.
address: 25005 Rock Creek Rd, Idleyld Park, OR 97447

title: Rock Creek Recreation Site
contentHtml:
Rock Creek Recreation Site is a secluded 17-site campground on the forested banks of Rock Creek, about seven miles from the North Umpqua River corridor.

It has accessible campsites and restrooms, a swimming area, a reservable day-use pavilion, horseshoe pits and a volleyball court. An active bald eagle nest is visible across the creek, and salmon migrate and spawn here.
excerpt: Rock Creek Recreation Site is a secluded 17-site campground on the forested banks of Rock Creek, about seven miles from the North Umpqua River corridor.
note: Closed indefinitely due to wildfire damage.
address: Rock Creek Rd, Idleyld Park, OR (Roseburg District Office: 777 NW Garden Valley Blvd, Roseburg, OR 97471)

title: Scaredman Recreation Site
contentHtml:
Scaredman Recreation Site is a minimally developed campground on Canton Creek, with 10 campsites, riverside picnic sites and several natural swimming holes on Canton and Steamboat creeks.

The North Umpqua River, about 3 miles downstream, offers fly-fishing and whitewater rafting.
excerpt: Scaredman Recreation Site is a minimally developed campground on Canton Creek, with 10 campsites, riverside picnic sites and several natural swimming holes on C
note: $10 per night. Reservations required at least 5 days ahead on Recreation.gov; no on-site payment. Canton and Steamboat creeks are closed to fishing. From Roseburg, take Hwy 138 east 40 miles, Steamboat Creek Rd north, then Canton Creek Rd 3 miles.
address: Canton Creek Rd, Roseburg, OR (Roseburg District Office: 777 NW Garden Valley Blvd, Roseburg, OR 97471)

title: Smith River Falls Campground
contentHtml:
Smith River Falls Campground offers riverside camping just above the falls on the Smith River, in a peaceful old-growth forest. Visitors come to picnic, wade, fish and watch for bald eagles.

Its 10 campsites have picnic tables and fire rings, with accessible restrooms and a boat launch.
excerpt: Smith River Falls Campground offers riverside camping just above the falls on the Smith River, in a peaceful old-growth forest. Visitors come to picnic, wade, f
note: No fee; first come, first served. No drinking water. 14-day limit. From Reedsport, go north on US 101 a short way, then east on Smith River Rd 26.4 miles.
address: Smith River Rd, 26.4 miles from Reedsport, OR

title: Susan Creek Campground
contentHtml:
Susan Creek Campground is a forested campground on the Wild and Scenic North Umpqua River, near the Umpqua National Forest, popular for hiking, picnicking and fly-fishing (fly-only).

Its 29 sites on a loop each have a paved parking spur and fire ring. There are flush restrooms with showers, a day-use area with a shelter, nature trails and an amphitheater with summer evening programs.
excerpt: Susan Creek Campground is a forested campground on the Wild and Scenic North Umpqua River, near the Umpqua National Forest, popular for hiking, picnicking and f
note: Reservations required at least one day ahead on Recreation.gov. Extra vehicle $5.
address: Hwy 138 just past milepost 28, Idleyld Park, OR

title: Tyee Campground (Umpqua River)

gallery.alt: View of the Umpqua from the campground

contentHtml:
Tyee Campground sits on the Umpqua River in a broad canyon with forested mountainsides, between the coast and Roseburg. It is popular for salmon, steelhead and bass fishing.

Its 15 campsites have sand tent pads, fire rings and picnic tables, with drinking water, accessible vault toilets, horseshoe pits and a reservable pavilion.
excerpt: Tyee Campground sits on the Umpqua River in a broad canyon with forested mountainsides, between the coast and Roseburg. It is popular for salmon, steelhead and
note: $14 per night. Reservation only on Recreation.gov (same-day reservations available). No cell service. From I-5 in Sutherlin, take Hwy 138 west 12 miles, cross Bullock Bridge, then turn right on Bullock Rd for 0.5 mile. Not the Forest Service dunes campground of the same name.
address: Bullock Rd, Oakland, OR (Roseburg District Office: 777 NW Garden Valley Blvd, Roseburg, OR 97471)

title: Vincent Creek Campground
contentHtml:
Vincent Creek Campground is a small, 5-site campground where Vincent Creek joins the Smith River, with a small swimming hole under tall Douglas-firs.

The old Vincent Creek Guard Station, once used by wildland firefighters, still stands nearby.
excerpt: Vincent Creek Campground is a small, 5-site campground where Vincent Creek joins the Smith River, with a small swimming hole under tall Douglas-firs.
note: No fee. Vault restroom; no drinking water. From US 101 just north of Reedsport, take Smith River Rd east 30.4 miles.
address: Smith River Rd, 30.4 miles from Reedsport, OR

title: Bolon Island Tideways State Scenic Corridor

gallery.alt: Bolon Island Tideways State Scenic Corridor

contentHtml:
Bolon Island Tideways State Scenic Corridor is a quiet day-use area on an island in the Umpqua River at Reedsport. A trail loops about halfway around the island, with views of the river.

Since 1988 the river-side shoreline has hosted a large rookery of double-crested cormorants, whose nests fill the trees.
excerpt: Bolon Island Tideways State Scenic Corridor is a quiet day-use area on an island in the Umpqua River at Reedsport. A trail loops about halfway around the island
note: Free day use. No restrooms or drinking water.
address: West of US 101, just north of the Umpqua River Bridge, Reedsport, OR

title: Umpqua Lighthouse State Park

gallery.alt: Lake Marie and its sandy shore

contentHtml:
Umpqua Lighthouse State Park sits less than a mile from Salmon Harbor on Winchester Bay, within the towering dunes of the Oregon Dunes National Recreation Area. Its campground and day-use areas center on Lake Marie, a small freshwater lake with a sandy swimming beach, open to fishing and non-motorized boating.

Camping includes full-hookup, electrical and tent sites, rustic and deluxe yurts, rustic log cabins and a hiker/biker camp, with hot showers. The 65-foot Umpqua River Lighthouse and its museum stand next to the park.
excerpt: Umpqua Lighthouse State Park sits less than a mile from Salmon Harbor on Winchester Bay, within the towering dunes of the Oregon Dunes National Recreation Area.
note: Lighthouse and museum tours: 541-271-4631 (run by Douglas County Parks).
address: 460 Lighthouse Rd, Winchester Bay, OR 97467
