title: Jasper State Recreation Site
contentHtml:
Jasper State Recreation Site is a riverside park popular for weddings, reunions and large family picnics, with four reservable group shelters that have cooking areas, sinks and picnic tables, plus nearby flush restrooms.

Ball fields, a playground, volleyball and riverside trails fill the park, and walking trails wind through a streamside forest at the upstream end. Anglers fish this stretch, and canoes and kayaks launch here onto the Willamette River Water Trail.
excerpt: Jasper State Recreation Site is a riverside park popular for weddings, reunions and large family picnics, with four reservable group shelters that have cooking
address: Near Springfield, OR

title: Jessie M. Honeyman Memorial State Park
contentHtml:
Jessie M. Honeyman Memorial State Park, halfway up the Oregon coast, has more than 350 campsites, hiking trails and sand dunes that stretch to the ocean. Its two freshwater lakes are Cleawox, good for swimming, and Woahink, with a public boat ramp and canoe rentals.

Pink rhododendrons bloom in spring, summer brings family reunions, and huckleberries and blackberries ripen in fall. Camping includes full-hookup, electrical and tent sites, 10 yurts (5 pet-friendly), six seasonal group tent areas and a hiker/biker camp.
excerpt: Jessie M. Honeyman Memorial State Park, halfway up the Oregon coast, has more than 350 campsites, hiking trails and sand dunes that stretch to the ocean. Its tw
note: Four accessible campsites and two accessible yurts. RV dump station; firewood for sale.
address: Three miles south of Florence on US 101, OR

title: Lowell State Recreation Site
contentHtml:
Lowell State Recreation Site is a day-use park on the north shore of Dexter Lake, which is kept full year-round. A reservable picnic shelter overlooks the lake, with a wooded picnic area, playground, basketball court, a big lawn and a swim beach.

A marina with rentable moorage, a large courtesy dock and a four-lane launch ramp serve sailors, water skiers, anglers, paddlers and rowers; the Oregon Association of Rowers and the University of Oregon keep boathouses here. Rowing regattas are held each spring and drag boat races each summer, and bald eagles and wintering waterfowl are common.
excerpt: Lowell State Recreation Site is a day-use park on the north shore of Dexter Lake, which is kept full year-round. A reservable picnic shelter overlooks the lake,
note: Flush restroom.
address: North shore of Dexter Lake, Lowell, OR

title: Stonefield Beach State Recreation Site

gallery.alt: Beach with cliffs and a log

contentHtml: Stonefield Beach State Recreation Site offers easy beach access, with Tenmile Creek just to the north. It is a good place to sit in the sun and watch for whales.
excerpt: Stonefield Beach State Recreation Site offers easy beach access, with Tenmile Creek just to the north. It is a good place to sit in the sun and watch for whales
address: At the mouth of Tenmile Creek, Yachats, OR

title: Tokatee Klootchman State Natural Site
contentHtml: Tokatee Klootchman State Natural Site sits a few feet above the ocean with an excellent view, and it is a great place to watch for whales.
excerpt: Tokatee Klootchman State Natural Site sits a few feet above the ocean with an excellent view, and it is a great place to watch for whales.
address: Off US 101, about 16 miles north of Florence, OR

title: Willamette River Greenway and Water Trail
imageAlt: Paddlers on the Willamette River Water Trail (area photo)

banner.alt: Paddlers on the Willamette River Water Trail (area photo)

contentHtml:
The Willamette River and its middle and coast forks run more than 255 miles from Cottage Grove north to Portland, where the river meets the Columbia. Greenway lands along the banks are low-key open spaces: some preserve native trees, plants and animals, others protect scenic views and historic sites or offer places to land a canoe, fish or walk the shore.

The Willamette is a nationally recognized water trail. Some access sites have boat launches and vault toilets; others have no facilities.
excerpt: The Willamette River and its middle and coast forks run more than 255 miles from Cottage Grove north to Portland, where the river meets the Columbia. Greenway l
note: Call 541-517-8580 for location information. Hunting and trapping are allowed in some greenway areas with restrictions; follow ODFW rules. Do not bring outside firewood (emerald ash borer quarantine).
address: Pengra Access, southeast of Pleasant Hill, and Marshall Island Access, southeast of Junction City (Lane County access sites)

title: Alder Dune Campground
contentHtml:
Alder Dune Campground sits in lush coastal forest between Alder and Dune lakes in the Siuslaw National Forest, with native shrubbery giving its sites privacy. It has 39 sites, shade and paved roads.

A day-use area near Dune Lake is the trailhead for the 1-mile Alder Dune Trail loop, and hiking, fishing and picnicking are popular.
excerpt: Alder Dune Campground sits in lush coastal forest between Alder and Dune lakes in the Siuslaw National Forest, with native shrubbery giving its sites privacy. I
note: Drinking water and pit toilets. No hookups. Reservations and info: Recreation.gov.
address: 89630 Hwy 101, Florence, OR 97439 (6 miles north of Florence, west side of the highway)

title: Alder Springs Campground
contentHtml: Alder Springs is a small, rustic campground right beside the historic McKenzie Pass Highway, surrounded by Douglas fir. Camping is tents only.
excerpt: Alder Springs is a small, rustic campground right beside the historic McKenzie Pass Highway, surrounded by Douglas fir. Camping is tents only.
note: $10 per night; extra vehicle $5. No drinking water. First come, first served; pay on site with the Recreation.gov app's Scan and Pay (download it before you arrive, as cell service is limited). OR 242 closes in winter; check TripCheck.com.
address: 57600 McKenzie Highway (OR 242), Blue River, OR 97413

title: Archie Knowles Campground
contentHtml: Archie Knowles Campground sits beside Highway 126 in a forest of Douglas fir, spruce and huckleberry, with Knowles Creek flowing gently alongside. It is on the Siuslaw National Forest and run by Lane County Parks.
excerpt: Archie Knowles Campground sits beside Highway 126 in a forest of Douglas fir, spruce and huckleberry, with Knowles Creek flowing gently alongside. It is on the
note: Drinking water and picnic tables. No horses. Reservations through Lane County Parks.
address: Off Highway 126, about 4 miles east of Mapleton, OR

title: Baker Beach Campground
contentHtml: Baker Beach Campground has four rustic campsites with tables and fire rings, plus limited facilities for horses. Trails from the Baker Beach Trailhead lead west to the beach (about half a mile) and east to Lily Lake.
excerpt: Baker Beach Campground has four rustic campsites with tables and fire rings, plus limited facilities for horses. Trails from the Baker Beach Trailhead lead west
note: $22 per night; extra vehicle $12; day use $10 per vehicle. First come, first served. Vault toilets; no drinking water or hookups. Weed-free feed required. Snowy plover restrictions March 15 to September 15.
address: Baker Beach Trailhead, north of Florence, OR (Central Coast Ranger Station: 1130 Forestry Lane, Waldport, OR 97394)

title: Bedrock Campground
contentHtml: Bedrock Campground has 22 sites on a terrace above Fall Creek. The camp was shaped by fire, and the surrounding hillsides now bloom with fireweed in summer. Summer weekends are busy.
excerpt: Bedrock Campground has 22 sites on a terrace above Fall Creek. The camp was shaped by fire, and the surrounding hillsides now bloom with fireweed in summer. Sum
note: Dry camping: no drinking water, electricity or dump station. Check current status before you go.
address: Forest Road 18, about 14 miles from Lowell, OR

title: Big Pool Group Campground
contentHtml: Big Pool is a small, shady group campground between Forest Road 18 and Fall Creek. Expect heavy use on summer weekends.
excerpt: Big Pool is a small, shady group campground between Forest Road 18 and Fall Creek. Expect heavy use on summer weekends.
note: Reservations and info: Recreation.gov.
address: Between Forest Road 18 and Fall Creek, east of Lowell, OR

title: Black Canyon Campground
imageAlt: The river from Black Canyon Campground

banner.alt: The river from Black Canyon Campground

contentHtml:
Black Canyon Campground sits beside the Middle Fork of the Willamette River, shaded by hemlock, cedar and Douglas fir. Fishing and kayaking are popular.

It has 75 sites, 19 of them reservable, each with a picnic table and fire ring with grill.
excerpt: Black Canyon Campground sits beside the Middle Fork of the Willamette River, shaded by hemlock, cedar and Douglas fir. Fishing and kayaking are popular.
note: Drinking water and accessible vault toilets. Large RVs not recommended. Reservations and info: Recreation.gov.
address: Highway 58, about 8 miles west of Oakridge, OR (1 mile east of Lookout Point Reservoir)

title: Blair Lake Campground
contentHtml:
Blair Lake Campground is a small, high-elevation campground on the north shore of Blair Lake, a 35-acre, 20- foot-deep lake stocked with brook and rainbow trout. It has seven tent sites, four of them walk-in.

Wildflowers bloom in early summer and huckleberries ripen in late summer and early autumn. The historic Blair Lake Trail starts nearby and is open to hikers, riders and mountain bikers.
excerpt: Blair Lake Campground is a small, high-elevation campground on the north shore of Blair Lake, a 35-acre, 20- foot-deep lake stocked with brook and rainbow trout
note: First come, first served; pay on site with the Recreation.gov app's Scan and Pay (download it before you arrive, as cell service is limited). Small, unimproved parking area best for smaller vehicles. Mosquitoes are heavy early in the season.
address: North shore of Blair Lake, Willamette National Forest, OR

title: Blue Pool Campground
contentHtml:
Blue Pool Campground sits beside Highway 58 in old-growth forest along Salt Creek, with 24 sites, a large creekside picnic area and a big grassy area for play. Fishing and swimming are popular.

The McCredie Day Use Area and its unimproved hot springs are half a mile east on Highway 58; the pool water is very hot, so use caution.
excerpt: Blue Pool Campground sits beside Highway 58 in old-growth forest along Salt Creek, with 24 sites, a large creekside picnic area and a big grassy area for play.
note: Not reservable on Recreation.gov.
address: Beside Highway 58 on Salt Creek, near Oakridge, OR

title: Box Canyon Horse Camp
contentHtml:
Box Canyon Horse Camp is a primitive campground that gives riders and hikers access to the wilderness and roadless areas west of the Cascade crest, among conifer groves and meadows near the Three Sisters Wilderness and the Box Canyon Trail Area.

It has tables, fire rings, ample parking, hitching posts, corrals and a stock water trough.
excerpt: Box Canyon Horse Camp is a primitive campground that gives riders and hikers access to the wilderness and roadless areas west of the Cascade crest, among conife
note: No fee. Vault toilet; no drinking water (trough water for stock only in summer). Pack out trash. Maximum trailer length 30 feet; 14-day limit in 60 days; no chainsaws. Forest Road 19 is not plowed in winter.
address: West side of Forest Road 19 (Aufderheide Drive) at the top of the pass, about 31 miles south of Highway 126, OR

title: Broken Bowl Campground
contentHtml: Broken Bowl is a small, family-friendly campground with 16 sites, nine of them tent-only, shaded by mature forest with access to Fall Creek.
excerpt: Broken Bowl is a small, family-friendly campground with 16 sites, nine of them tent-only, shaded by mature forest with access to Fall Creek.
note: Reservations and info: Recreation.gov.
address: Fall Creek, Forest Road 18, east of Lowell, OR

title: Campers Flat Campground
imageAlt: The Middle Fork at Campers Flat

banner.alt: The Middle Fork at Campers Flat

contentHtml:
Campers Flat is a group campground on an open river terrace below Forest Road 21, in a grove of Douglas fir, ponderosa pine and cedar. The Middle Fork of the Willamette runs alongside, and its sound largely masks the road.

Fishing, hiking and mountain biking, including the Young's Rock Trail, are popular.
excerpt: Campers Flat is a group campground on an open river terrace below Forest Road 21, in a grove of Douglas fir, ponderosa pine and cedar. The Middle Fork of the Wi
note: Hand-pump drinking water (bring a backup supply or filter), one restroom and trash service. Locked gate; the combination comes with your reservation. From Highway 58 just past milepost 37 on the east side of Oakridge, turn right on Kitson Springs Road, then right on Forest Road 21 to milepost 20.
address: Forest Road 21, milepost 20, south of Oakridge, OR

title: Cedar Creek Campground
contentHtml: Cedar Creek Campground sits on a river terrace under an old-growth canopy near Brice Creek and nearby trailheads. It has 10 first-come, first-served sites, and hiking, mountain biking, fishing and berry picking are popular.
excerpt: Cedar Creek Campground sits on a river terrace under an old-growth canopy near Brice Creek and nearby trailheads. It has 10 first-come, first-served sites, and
note: Closed for the 2026 summer season. Vault toilet; no drinking water. Quiet hours 10 PM - 8 AM; no fireworks or OHVs. From Cottage Grove, take Row River Road east 19 miles, then right on Road 2470 along Brice Creek about 4 miles.
address: Brice Creek Road (County Road 2470), about 4 miles from Row River Road, east of Cottage Grove, OR

title: Clark Creek Organization Camp
contentHtml:
Clark Creek Organization Camp is a group camp built by the Civilian Conservation Corps, with five sleeping shelters of eight bunks each and a large field for tents and games. Up to 125 guests can visit by day and 80 can stay overnight.

It has a picnic shelter, campfire circles, an amphitheater, a ball field, horseshoe pits and volleyball, plus the Clark Creek Nature Trail and a path to the Ta-Wa-Si Chapel.
excerpt: Clark Creek Organization Camp is a group camp built by the Civilian Conservation Corps, with five sleeping shelters of eight bunks each and a large field for te
note: Closed because of wildfire until further notice; check Recreation.gov. Drinking water and vault toilets.
address: Forest Road 18, 12.7 miles past the forest boundary, east of Lowell, OR

title: Cougar Crossing Campground
contentHtml:
Cougar Crossing Campground sits among conifers beside the South Fork of the McKenzie River at the south end of Cougar Reservoir. It is the closest campground to Terwilliger Hot Springs, with the Three Sisters Wilderness and French Pete Trail nearby.

It has 11 RV or tent sites on gravel spurs.
excerpt: Cougar Crossing Campground sits among conifers beside the South Fork of the McKenzie River at the south end of Cougar Reservoir. It is the closest campground to
note: Vault toilets; firewood for sale; no drinking water. From Blue River, go 4 miles east on Highway 126 to Aufderheide Drive (Forest Road 19), bear right at the Y, climb past the reservoir and continue 5 miles. Road 19 is not plowed in winter.
address: Aufderheide Drive (Forest Road 19), south end of Cougar Reservoir, Blue River, OR

title: Delta Campground
contentHtml:
Delta Campground is one of the largest and most scenic campgrounds on the McKenzie River Ranger District, along the West Cascades Scenic Byway. It gives access to the McKenzie River for rafting and drift-boat fishing, with hiking and mountain bike trails nearby.

It has 38 sites and a day-use area with an amphitheater.
excerpt: Delta Campground is one of the largest and most scenic campgrounds on the McKenzie River Ranger District, along the West Cascades Scenic Byway. It gives access
note: No hookups. Reservations May to mid-September; first come, first served outside that season. From Highway 126, turn south on Aufderheide Drive at the Cougar Reservoir turnoff, cross the river and turn right on Forest Road 400 for about 1 mile.
address: Forest Road 400 off Aufderheide Drive, near Blue River, OR

title: Dolly Varden Campground
contentHtml: Dolly Varden is the first campground along the Fall Creek drainage on Forest Road 18, near the start of the 13.7-mile Fall Creek National Recreation Trail. Its five tent-only sites include three along the creek and two walk-in sites across the road.
excerpt: Dolly Varden is the first campground along the Fall Creek drainage on Forest Road 18, near the start of the 13.7-mile Fall Creek National Recreation Trail. Its
note: Partly reservable. Reservations and info: Recreation.gov.
address: Forest Road 18, Fall Creek drainage, east of Lowell, OR

title: Driftwood II Campground
contentHtml:
Driftwood II is an off-road vehicle campground in the Oregon Dunes National Recreation Area with direct sand access. The Driftwood II route leads north from camp into open dunes that stretch to South Jetty Road.

It has 67 sites, including 10 RV pull-through sites without tables or fire rings.
excerpt: Driftwood II is an off-road vehicle campground in the Oregon Dunes National Recreation Area with direct sand access. The Driftwood II route leads north from cam
note: Flush toilets, drinking water, trash and recycling; no hookups. Reservations preferred. 14-day limit in 30 days across the Siuslaw National Forest. From Highway 101, turn west on Siltcoos Beach Access Road for 1.3 miles to the entrance.
address: Siltcoos Beach Access Road, about 7 miles south of Florence, OR

title: Dry Lake Horse Camp
contentHtml: Dry Lake Horse Camp sits along the Cape Mountain Trails and offers tent camping for riders and hikers; overnight vehicle camping is not allowed. Riders get priority, since horse camps are limited.
excerpt: Dry Lake Horse Camp sits along the Cape Mountain Trails and offers tent camping for riders and hikers; overnight vehicle camping is not allowed. Riders get prio
note: No fee. No water or trash service; pack it out. Forest Road 789 has not been maintained recently and may not suit trailers or large campers.
address: Dry Lake Trailhead, Herman Peak Road, 3 miles east of Highway 101 (5 miles north of Florence), OR

title: French Pete Campground
contentHtml: French Pete Campground, at 1,800 feet where French Pete Creek meets the South Fork of the McKenzie River, is a popular escape from summer heat under a thick canopy of conifers. It has 16 first-come, first- served sites, two of them tent-only.
excerpt: French Pete Campground, at 1,800 feet where French Pete Creek meets the South Fork of the McKenzie River, is a popular escape from summer heat under a thick can
note: Toilets, hand-pump water, fire rings and garbage service. Extra vehicle $8 per night.
address: Aufderheide Drive (Forest Road 19), 11 miles south of Highway 126, Blue River, OR

title: Frissell Crossing Campground
contentHtml: Frissell Crossing Campground sits on the South Fork of the McKenzie River and was built by the Civilian Conservation Corps in 1934. It is well off the main road, with some of its 11 first-come, first-served sites around an open meadow.
excerpt: Frissell Crossing Campground sits on the South Fork of the McKenzie River and was built by the Civilian Conservation Corps in 1934. It is well off the main road
note: Vault toilets, hand-pump drinking water, fire rings, picnic tables and garbage collection. From Blue River, go 4 miles east on Highway 126 to Aufderheide Drive (Forest Road 19), then bear right at the Y and continue 20 miles.
address: Aufderheide Drive (Forest Road 19), about 20 miles south of Highway 126, McKenzie Bridge, OR

title: Gold Lake Campground
contentHtml:
Gold Lake Campground sits near the Cascade crest, some of its 21 sites beside small Gold Lake, in a quiet alpine forest with autumn huckleberries. Deer, elk and beaver can be seen in the bog next to camp.

The lake is fly-fishing only; gas motors are banned and electric motors must go at no-wake speed. A historic log shelter in the day-use area serves cross-country skiers overnight in winter.
excerpt: Gold Lake Campground sits near the Cascade crest, some of its 21 sites beside small Gold Lake, in a quiet alpine forest with autumn huckleberries. Deer, elk and
note: $26 per night; extra vehicle $10; day use $10 per vehicle. First come, first served (Scan and Pay). Vault toilets and drinking water. Check-in 2 PM, check-out noon; 14-day limit in 60 days.
address: End of Gold Lake Road, off Highway 58 just below Willamette Pass, 28 miles east of Oakridge, OR

title: Hard Rock Campground
contentHtml: Hard Rock is a small, primitive group campground on the South Fork of the McKenzie River just south of Cougar Reservoir, with one tent-only site for up to 10 people. Hiking and river fishing are close by.
excerpt: Hard Rock is a small, primitive group campground on the South Fork of the McKenzie River just south of Cougar Reservoir, with one tent-only site for up to 10 pe
note: Portable toilets, fire rings, picnic tables and trash collection; no water or hookups.
address: Aufderheide Drive (Forest Road 19), 10 miles past the Y, just south of Cougar Reservoir, Blue River, OR

title: Harralson Horse Camp
contentHtml: Harralson Horse Camp is a small, quiet horse camp away from Waldo Lake and the busier North Waldo and Islet campgrounds. It is a staging area for rides into the Three Sisters and Waldo Lake wilderness areas, and the Harralson Trail connects to the Pacific Crest Trail.
excerpt: Harralson Horse Camp is a small, quiet horse camp away from Waldo Lake and the busier North Waldo and Islet campgrounds. It is a staging area for rides into the
note: Listed as closed under the Cedar Creek Fire closure order; check alerts. Tables, fire rings, garbage and vault toilet; no drinking water (available at North Waldo) and no corrals. Weed-free feed required. Day use $5 per vehicle. From Highway 58, take Waldo Lake Road about 12 miles; where the pavement curves sharply left, go straight on the gravel road.
address: Off Waldo Lake Road (Forest Road 5897), about 35.7 miles northeast of Oakridge, OR

title: Hobo Camp Campground
contentHtml:
Hobo Camp is a small roadside campground on Brice Creek Road, where a short winding trail leads to the rocky shore of Brice Creek and nearby Hobo Creek invites exploring. It has four sites and one group site, first come, first served.

Cedar Creek and Lund Park campgrounds and the Brice Creek Trailhead are nearby.
excerpt: Hobo Camp is a small roadside campground on Brice Creek Road, where a short winding trail leads to the rocky shore of Brice Creek and nearby Hobo Creek invites
note: Closed for the 2026 summer season. Vault toilet; no drinking water or garbage service. No horses.
address: Brice Creek Road (Forest Road 2470), 7.5 miles from Row River Road, east of Cottage Grove, OR

title: Horse Creek Campground
contentHtml: Horse Creek Campground is a horse camp along the Cape Mountain Trails, with 11 equestrian sites and a shelter site; every site must have a horse.
excerpt: Horse Creek Campground is a horse camp along the Cape Mountain Trails, with 11 equestrian sites and a shelter site; every site must have a horse.
note: One vault toilet; no drinking water or power (on-site water is for horses only). The trail trough can dry up in late summer. No cell service. Weed-free feed required; clean up manure.
address: Horse Creek Road (Forest Road 58), 4.7 miles east of Highway 101, 10.5 miles north of Florence, OR

title: Horse Creek Group Campground
imageAlt: Group area with picnic tables and grills

banner.alt: Group area with picnic tables and grills

contentHtml: Horse Creek Group Campground sits on the banks of Horse Creek under shady Douglas fir, with a picnic area for grilling and gatherings. It holds up to 100 campers and 23 vehicles.
excerpt: Horse Creek Group Campground sits on the banks of Horse Creek under shady Douglas fir, with a picnic area for grilling and gatherings. It holds up to 100 camper
note: Drinking water, picnic tables, vault toilets and fire rings. Bring local firewood. Call the McKenzie River Ranger Station at least 72 hours before arrival for the gate combination.
address: Horse Creek Road (Road 2638), about 2 miles southeast of Highway 126, McKenzie Bridge, OR

title: Indigo Springs Campground
contentHtml: Indigo Springs is a small, first-come, first-served campground beside Indigo Springs, near old-growth forest, Chuckle Springs, the Middle Fork of the Willamette and the Diamond Peak Wilderness. The short Indigo Springs Loop passes a day-use area.
excerpt: Indigo Springs is a small, first-come, first-served campground beside Indigo Springs, near old-growth forest, Chuckle Springs, the Middle Fork of the Willamette
note: One restroom and trash service; no drinking water. Not suited to RVs or trailers (no turnaround). From Highway 58 just past milepost 37 on the east side of Oakridge, turn right on Kitson Springs Road, then right on Forest Road 21 to milepost 29.
address: Forest Road 21, milepost 29, south of Oakridge, OR

title: Islet Campground
contentHtml:
Islet Campground sits on the north end of Waldo Lake, one of Oregon's largest natural lakes, among Douglas fir and mountain hemlock. Sailing, canoeing and swimming are popular, sandy beaches line the shore, and afternoon winds help keep mosquitoes down.

It has 55 sites, 31 of them reservable, each with a fire ring and picnic table.
excerpt: Islet Campground sits on the north end of Waldo Lake, one of Oregon's largest natural lakes, among Douglas fir and mountain hemlock. Sailing, canoeing and swimm
note: Vault toilets in camp and at the boat launch. From Oakridge, take Highway 58 east 23.3 miles, Waldo Lake Road 12.8 miles, then left on Forest Road 5898 for 1.2 miles.
address: FR 5898 at Waldo Lake, Oakridge, OR 97463

title: Kiahanie Campground
contentHtml: Kiahanie Campground has 20 first-come, first-served sites off Forest Road 19 near the Middle Fork Ranger Station.
excerpt: Kiahanie Campground has 20 first-come, first-served sites off Forest Road 19 near the Middle Fork Ranger Station.
note: Hand-pump drinking water (bring a backup supply) and two restrooms. From Highway 58 just past milepost 31, turn left across from the Middle Fork Ranger Station, cross the bridge and turn left on Forest Road 19.
address: Forest Road 19, just past milepost 19, near Oakridge, OR

title: Lagoon Campground
contentHtml: Lagoon Campground sits in the Oregon Dunes National Recreation Area about 8 miles south of Florence, its sites surrounded by coastal shrubbery. Fishing, hiking and the Lagoon Trail loop are popular, and the ocean beach is within walking distance.
excerpt: Lagoon Campground sits in the Oregon Dunes National Recreation Area about 8 miles south of Florence, its sites surrounded by coastal shrubbery. Fishing, hiking
note: $22 per night. Flush toilets, drinking water, trash and recycling; no hookups. Dump station at Honeyman State Park. From Highway 101, turn west on Siltcoos Beach Access Road for 1 mile.
address: Siltcoos Beach Access Road, about 8 miles south of Florence, OR

title: Limberlost Campground
contentHtml: Limberlost is a small, rustic, secluded group campground beside Lost Creek under towering Douglas fir and cedar, near the Three Sisters and Mount Washington wildernesses and Belknap Hot Springs.
excerpt: Limberlost is a small, rustic, secluded group campground beside Lost Creek under towering Douglas fir and cedar, near the Three Sisters and Mount Washington wil
note: Vault toilets and garbage service; no drinking water. Firewood sold at Olallie Campground.
address: Highway 242, about 2 miles east of Highway 126, near McKenzie Bridge, OR

title: Lookout Campground and Boat Launch
contentHtml: Lookout Campground sits in a sunny, open meadow on the northeast shore of Blue River Reservoir, with a day-use picnic area, boat launch and floating dock. It has 20 first-come, first-served sites.
excerpt: Lookout Campground sits in a sunny, open meadow on the northeast shore of Blue River Reservoir, with a day-use picnic area, boat launch and floating dock. It ha
note: Drinking water, vault toilets, firewood for sale and a camp host. From Blue River, go 3 miles east on Highway 126 and turn left on Forest Road 15 for 4 miles.
address: Forest Road 15, 4 miles north of Highway 126, Blue River, OR

title: Lund Park Campground
contentHtml:
Lund Park Campground sits in cool, quiet forest beside Brice Creek and makes a base for nearby trails such as the Brice Creek Trail. In the early 1900s it was a stopover for miners heading to the Bohemia Mines, and a concrete foundation from that time remains near site 1.

It has 10 tent-only sites with tables and fire rings.
excerpt: Lund Park Campground sits in cool, quiet forest beside Brice Creek and makes a base for nearby trails such as the Brice Creek Trail. In the early 1900s it was a
note: Two vault toilets; no drinking water or garbage service (pack it out). Extra vehicle $5.
address: Brice Creek Road (County Road 2470), 7 miles from Row River Road, east of Cottage Grove, OR

title: McKenzie Bridge Campground
contentHtml:
McKenzie Bridge Campground is a small, quiet campground along the McKenzie River shaded by Douglas fir and western red cedar, about an hour east of Eugene. Many sites have river access, and osprey, great blue herons and bald eagles are common.

Fishing and birdwatching are favorites, and restaurants and Tokatee Golf Course are a few miles away.
excerpt: McKenzie Bridge Campground is a small, quiet campground along the McKenzie River shaded by Douglas fir and western red cedar, about an hour east of Eugene. Many
note: Vault toilets, drinking water and a boat ramp; no hookups.
address: Highway 126, about 55 miles east of Eugene, near McKenzie Bridge, OR

title: Mineral Camp Campground
contentHtml: Mineral Camp is a small, free campground with three sites along Sharps Creek under Douglas fir, at the base of the historic Hardscrabble Grade. It was once a stopover for miners heading up to the Bohemia Mining District.
excerpt: Mineral Camp is a small, free campground with three sites along Sharps Creek under Douglas fir, at the base of the historic Hardscrabble Grade. It was once a st
note: No fee; first come, first served. Vault toilet; no drinking water or tables. Vehicles 20 feet maximum. From Cottage Grove, take Row River Road east 15 miles, Sharps Creek Road 10 miles, then the gravel section 2 miles.
address: Sharps Creek Road 2460, about 12 miles from Row River Road, southeast of Cottage Grove, OR

title: Mona Campground
contentHtml:
Mona Campground lines the northwest shore of Blue River Reservoir in a long, narrow strip of mixed conifers that gives each site privacy. The reservoir is popular for fishing, boating and canoeing.

It has 20 single and 2 double sites with tables and fire rings.
excerpt: Mona Campground lines the northwest shore of Blue River Reservoir in a long, narrow strip of mixed conifers that gives each site privacy. The reservoir is popul
note: Drinking water, vault toilets, firewood for sale and a camp host. Reservations May to mid-September.
address: Blue River Reservoir Road (Forest Road 15), about 4 miles north of Highway 126, Blue River, OR

title: North Waldo Campground
contentHtml:
North Waldo is the most popular of the Waldo Lake campgrounds, on one of Oregon's largest natural lakes among Douglas fir and mountain hemlock. It is a base for sailing, canoeing and swimming, and the 20-mile Jim Weaver Loop trail circles the lake.

It has 58 sites, 34 of them reservable, plus a boat launch and day-use area.
excerpt: North Waldo is the most popular of the Waldo Lake campgrounds, on one of Oregon's largest natural lakes among Douglas fir and mountain hemlock. It is a base for
note: From Oakridge, take Highway 58 east to Waldo Lake Road (FS Road 5897), then FS Roads 5898 and 5895.
address: FS Road 5895 at Waldo Lake, Oakridge, OR 97463

title: Packard Creek Campground
contentHtml:
Packard Creek is a popular, family-friendly campground on the west side of Hills Creek Reservoir, among tall trees with lake views. It has 36 sites (14 reservable), some with their own boat docks, and a reservable group camp for up to 80 people with a large shelter.

The day-use area has a fishing dock, swimming area and boat ramp.
excerpt: Packard Creek is a popular, family-friendly campground on the west side of Hills Creek Reservoir, among tall trees with lake views. It has 36 sites (14 reservab
note: Check-in 2 PM, check-out 1 PM.
address: Forest Road 21, about 5.2 miles south of Highway 58, Oakridge, OR

title: Paradise Campground
contentHtml:
Paradise Campground sits on a bend of the McKenzie River at about 1,600 feet among old-growth Douglas fir and western red cedar. Anglers fish for trout and steelhead (catch and release), rafters and kayakers run the river, and the McKenzie River National Recreation Trail starts nearby.

Its 59 first-come, first-served sites include some on the river.
excerpt: Paradise Campground sits on a bend of the McKenzie River at about 1,600 feet among old-growth Douglas fir and western red cedar. Anglers fish for trout and stee
note: Flush toilets, paved spurs, an amphitheater with programs and a boat ramp.
address: Highway 126, about 4 miles east of McKenzie Bridge, OR

title: Puma Campground
contentHtml: Puma Campground sits in shady, mature forest as the last developed camp along Forest Road 18 in the Fall Creek drainage. It has 11 sites, is popular with families and is busy on summer weekends; the Fall Creek National Recreation Trail is nearby.
excerpt: Puma Campground sits in shady, mature forest as the last developed camp along Forest Road 18 in the Fall Creek drainage. It has 11 sites, is popular with famili
note: Reservations and info: Recreation.gov.
address: Forest Road 18, Fall Creek drainage, east of Lowell, OR

title: Red Diamond Campground
contentHtml: Red Diamond is a rustic riverside group camp on the South Fork of the McKenzie River, shaded by Douglas fir, maple and alder, for up to 25 guests.
excerpt: Red Diamond is a rustic riverside group camp on the South Fork of the McKenzie River, shaded by Douglas fir, maple and alder, for up to 25 guests.
note: Picnic tables, fire rings, parking, portable toilets and trash collection; no water.
address: Aufderheide Drive (Forest Road 19), 13 miles south of Highway 126, Blue River, OR

title: Roaring River Group Campground
contentHtml: Roaring River Group Campground is a wooded camp for up to 50 overnight guests, where the aptly named Roaring River runs past the sites. Fishing, hiking and Three Sisters Wilderness trails are nearby.
excerpt: Roaring River Group Campground is a wooded camp for up to 50 overnight guests, where the aptly named Roaring River runs past the sites. Fishing, hiking and Thre
note: Picnic tables, dumpsters, vault toilets and fire rings; no water. Parking for 10 vehicles. Locked gate with combination.
address: Aufderheide Drive (Forest Road 19), 22 miles south of Highway 126, OR

title: Rock Creek Campground
contentHtml: Rock Creek Campground sits in a grove of large spruce and Douglas fir along Rock Creek near an Oregon coast beach, a place to relax on the sand, watch sunsets and hike nearby trails.
excerpt: Rock Creek Campground sits in a grove of large spruce and Douglas fir along Rock Creek near an Oregon coast beach, a place to relax on the sand, watch sunsets a
note: Vault toilets and drinking water; tables and fire rings; no hookups.
address: 93825 Hwy 101 N, Florence, OR 97439 (about 10 miles south of Yachats)

title: Rujada Campground
contentHtml:
Rujada Campground is a shaded, private campground on a terrace above Layng Creek, about 45 minutes from Eugene. Visitors swim from the creek banks, walk the Swordfern Trail through riparian Douglas fir, and see a historic Civilian Conservation Corps shelter; there is a playground for kids.

It has 15 sites and a reservable day-use picnic area.
excerpt: Rujada Campground is a shaded, private campground on a terrace above Layng Creek, about 45 minutes from Eugene. Visitors swim from the creek banks, walk the Swo
note: Toilets, tables and fire rings; no water (pack in, pack out). Camp host in summer. Extra vehicle $5.
address: Layng Creek Road (Road 17), 2 miles off Row River Road, about 21 miles east of Cottage Grove, OR

title: Sacandaga Campground
imageAlt: The Middle Fork near the campground

banner.alt: The Middle Fork near the campground

contentHtml: Sacandaga Campground sits on the bank of the Middle Fork of the Willamette among Douglas fir and pine, near several peaks and springs. Seven sites are reservable; the rest are first come, first served.
excerpt: Sacandaga Campground sits on the bank of the Middle Fork of the Willamette among Douglas fir and pine, near several peaks and springs. Seven sites are reservabl
note: Hand-pump drinking water (bring a backup supply), two restrooms and trash service. From Highway 58 just past milepost 37 on the east side of Oakridge, turn right on Kitson Springs Road, then right on Forest Road 21.
address: Forest Road 21, just before milepost 25, south of Oakridge, OR

title: Salmon Creek Falls Campground
contentHtml:
Salmon Creek Falls Campground has 14 sites in old-growth forest along Salmon Creek, where two small waterfalls and deep, clear blue-green pools fill a rocky gorge. Wildflowers bloom in spring, thimbleberries and hazelnuts ripen in summer, and old wooden pipes from when the creek supplied Oakridge's water are still visible.

Swimming, fishing, hiking the Salmon Creek Trail, mountain biking and picnicking are popular.
excerpt: Salmon Creek Falls Campground has 14 sites in old-growth forest along Salmon Creek, where two small waterfalls and deep, clear blue-green pools fill a rocky gor
note: Closed for the 2026 season; reopens spring 2027. $21 per night; extra vehicle $10; day use $10. First come, first served. Vault toilets; no drinking water. From Highway 58 at Crestview Street in Oakridge, go north, bear right on East 1st Street (becomes Forest Road 24) and continue about 3.7 miles.
address: Salmon Creek Road (Forest Road 24), 5 miles east of Oakridge, OR

title: Sand Prairie Campground
imageAlt: The Middle Fork near Sand Prairie

banner.alt: The Middle Fork near Sand Prairie

contentHtml:
Sand Prairie Campground sits in a grove of Douglas fir, western hemlock, cedar, dogwood and hazelnut near the Middle Fork of the Willamette and Hills Creek Reservoir. The Middle Fork Willamette Trail begins at its south end and follows the river for about 30 miles.

It has 21 sites, each with a table and fire ring, and a free day-use area.
excerpt: Sand Prairie Campground sits in a grove of Douglas fir, western hemlock, cedar, dogwood and hazelnut near the Middle Fork of the Willamette and Hills Creek Rese
note: Restroom and trash service; no drinking water. First come, first served unless marked reserved. From Highway 58 just past milepost 37 on the east side of Oakridge, turn right on Kitson Springs Road, then right on Forest Road 21.
address: Forest Road 21, just past milepost 11, south of Oakridge, OR

title: Scott Lake Campground
contentHtml: Scott Lake Campground is a high-elevation, primitive campground where the snowcapped Three Sisters reflect in the lake on clear days, among subalpine fir, mountain hemlock and bear grass. It is next to the Benson/Tenas Trailhead, near the Mount Washington Wilderness.
excerpt: Scott Lake Campground is a high-elevation, primitive campground where the snowcapped Three Sisters reflect in the lake on clear days, among subalpine fir, mount
note: $5 per vehicle per day or recreation pass. First come, first served. Vault toilet; no drinking water. No trailers; vehicles 35 feet maximum. Mosquitoes are heavy in July and August. Highway 242 closes in winter.
address: Forest Road 260 off Highway 242, 14 miles east of Highway 126, near McKenzie Bridge, OR

title: Secret Campground
imageAlt: Sandy beach on the Middle Fork

banner.alt: Sandy beach on the Middle Fork

contentHtml: Secret Campground is a small, secluded group site well screened from Forest Road 21, with the Middle Fork of the Willamette running beside some of its six sites. Fishing, hiking, mountain biking and horseback riding are popular, with the Middle Fork National Recreation Trail nearby.
excerpt: Secret Campground is a small, secluded group site well screened from Forest Road 21, with the Middle Fork of the Willamette running beside some of its six sites
note: One restroom and trash service; no drinking water. Check ODFW fishing rules. From Highway 58 just past milepost 37 on the east side of Oakridge, turn right on Kitson Springs Road, then right on Forest Road 21.
address: Forest Road 21, just past milepost 18, south of Oakridge, OR

title: Shadow Bay Campground
contentHtml: Shadow Bay Campground sits on the shore of Waldo Lake among tall conifers, with sailing, canoeing, fishing and swimming, and the Jim Weaver Loop trail circling the lake. It has 92 sites, 19 of them reservable, and a boat ramp.
excerpt: Shadow Bay Campground sits on the shore of Waldo Lake among tall conifers, with sailing, canoeing, fishing and swimming, and the Jim Weaver Loop trail circling
note: No drinking water during water-system repairs; bring all you need. Garbage and gray-water disposal. From Oakridge, take Highway 58 east 23.3 miles, Waldo Lake Road 6.7 miles, then Forest Road 5896 for 1.7 miles.
address: Forest Road 5896, off Waldo Lake Road, Oakridge, OR

title: Skookum Creek Campground
imageAlt: Stream bridge on the trail from camp

banner.alt: Stream bridge on the trail from camp

contentHtml: Skookum Creek is a small, secluded campground near the wilderness, with trails leading from camp across a stream bridge into the backcountry.
excerpt: Skookum Creek is a small, secluded campground near the wilderness, with trails leading from camp across a stream bridge into the backcountry.
note: One restroom at the parking area; no drinking water. First come, first served; pay on site with the Recreation.gov app's Scan and Pay (download it before you arrive, as cell service is limited). The final 4 miles on Road 1957 are rough and brushy; a high-clearance vehicle is needed.
address: Forest Road 1957, about 4 miles off Forest Road 19, near Oakridge, OR

title: Slide Creek Campground
contentHtml: Slide Creek Campground sits on the east bank of Cougar Reservoir, about 50 miles from Eugene, with easy boating and water access and Terwilliger Hot Springs nearby. Its 15 sites suit tents, trailers or RVs.
excerpt: Slide Creek Campground sits on the east bank of Cougar Reservoir, about 50 miles from Eugene, with easy boating and water access and Terwilliger Hot Springs nea
note: Drinking water, vault toilets, boat ramp, swimming beach and trailer parking. From Blue River, go 4 miles east on Highway 126 to Aufderheide Drive (Forest Road 19), 9.5 miles to FS Road 1900-500, then 1.5 miles.
address: FS Road 1900-500, off Aufderheide Drive, east bank of Cougar Reservoir, Blue River, OR

title: Sunnyside Campground
contentHtml: Sunnyside Campground sits at 1,700 feet on the southeast side of Cougar Reservoir under a large grove of conifers, with easy lake access. It has 13 first-come, first-served sites, eight of them tent-only.
excerpt: Sunnyside Campground sits at 1,700 feet on the southeast side of Cougar Reservoir under a large grove of conifers, with easy lake access. It has 13 first-come,
note: Vault toilets and garbage collection; no water, so bring enough for drinking, cooking and washing. Steep entrance; motorhomes and trailers not recommended.
address: FS Road 1900-500, off Aufderheide Drive, southeast side of Cougar Reservoir, Blue River, OR

title: Sutton Campground
contentHtml:
Sutton Campground lies just off the coast, about 1.5 miles from Sutton Beach and 2 miles from Sutton Lake. Hiking is the favorite activity, and visitors also swim in Sutton Creek and fish or boat on Sutton Lake.

It has 77 sites, 22 with electric hookups, and three group sites.
excerpt: Sutton Campground lies just off the coast, about 1.5 miles from Sutton Beach and 2 miles from Sutton Lake. Hiking is the favorite activity, and visitors also sw
note: Flush toilets and drinking water. From Florence, take Highway 101 north 5 miles to the Sutton turnoff, then 1 mile.
address: 4840 Sutton Beach Rd, Florence, OR 97439

title: Taylor Burn Campground
contentHtml: Taylor Burn was built by the Civilian Conservation Corps in 1939 as one of the original forest camps of the Willamette National Forest. The Forest Service has permanently decommissioned the campground, and it now serves as a trailhead into the Waldo Lake Wilderness, with trails to Erma Bell Lakes and Williams Lake.
excerpt: Taylor Burn was built by the Civilian Conservation Corps in 1939 as one of the original forest camps of the Willamette National Forest. The Forest Service has p
note: No camping, water or toilets. From Highway 58, take Waldo Lake Road 11 miles, FR 5898 toward North Waldo, then Taylor Burn Road 7 miles.
address: End of FR 5898-514 (Taylor Burn Road), north of Waldo Lake, OR

title: Tyee Campground
imageAlt: Boat ramp on the Siltcoos River

banner.alt: Boat ramp on the Siltcoos River

contentHtml: Tyee Campground is a small campground on the north bank of the Siltcoos River near the outlet of Siltcoos Lake in the Oregon Dunes National Recreation Area, popular with families, anglers and kayakers. Its 14 reservable sites are tucked into coastal shrubbery or set in an open meadow by the water.
excerpt: Tyee Campground is a small campground on the north bank of the Siltcoos River near the outlet of Siltcoos Lake in the Oregon Dunes National Recreation Area, pop
note: Vault toilets and a boat ramp; no water or hookups. Dump station at Honeyman State Park.
address: Pacific Avenue off Highway 101, about 6 miles south of Florence, OR

title: Waxmyrtle Campground
contentHtml: Waxmyrtle Campground sits in the Oregon Dunes National Recreation Area near the beach, hiking trails and open dunes, and borders the Siltcoos River Estuary, a popular wildlife viewing spot. Coastal shrubbery gives its 54 sites privacy.
excerpt: Waxmyrtle Campground sits in the Oregon Dunes National Recreation Area near the beach, hiking trails and open dunes, and borders the Siltcoos River Estuary, a p
note: Drinking water, camp host, flush toilets, recycling and trash; no hookups. From Highway 101, take Siltcoos Beach Access Road west 1 mile and turn left across the bridge.
address: South shore of the Siltcoos River, off Siltcoos Beach Access Road, about 8 miles south of Florence, OR

title: Oregon Islands

gallery.alt: Refuge staff with a puffin decoy on an offshore rock

contentHtml:
Oregon Islands National Wildlife Refuge, established in 1935, is not one place but 1,853 rocks, reefs and islands plus two headlands, running from Tillamook Head near Seaside to the California border.

Most of Oregon's estimated 1.2 million nesting seabirds raise their young here, and seals and sea lions haul out and give birth on the rocks. All the rocks and islands except 1-acre Tillamook Rock are designated wilderness.

The islands are closed to entry, so watch from shore with binoculars or a spotting scope.
excerpt: Oregon Islands National Wildlife Refuge, established in 1935, is not one place but 1,853 rocks, reefs and islands plus two headlands, running from Tillamook Hea
note: Email: Oregoncoast@fws.gov
address: Offshore rocks and islands along the whole Oregon coast

title: Fern Ridge Wildlife Area
imageAlt: Small boat on Fern Ridge Wildlife Area waterways

banner.alt: Small boat on Fern Ridge Wildlife Area waterways

contentHtml:
The Fern Ridge Wildlife Area covers 5,794 acres around Fern Ridge Reservoir, about five miles west of Eugene on both sides of Highway 126. It is managed mainly for wintering and nesting waterfowl, and more than 250 bird species use it, from bald eagles, osprey and American white pelicans to western grebes, wood ducks and Canada geese.

Visitors watch wildlife year-round, walk the riparian Coyote Creek Nature Trail, fish for bass, catfish, crappie and trout, hunt upland birds, waterfowl and big game in fall and winter, and launch small boats and canoes.
excerpt: The Fern Ridge Wildlife Area covers 5,794 acres around Fern Ridge Reservoir, about five miles west of Eugene on both sides of Highway 126. It is managed mainly
note: Wildlife Area Parking Permit required. Some areas close seasonally to protect wintering waterfowl; check ODFW regulations.
address: 26969 Cantrell Road, Eugene, OR 97402

title: Bridge Creek Falls
contentHtml:
Bridge Creek Falls is a small, scenic, hidden waterfall near Oakridge that drops 64 feet as a veiling horsetail through a narrow alcove beneath a cliff about 150 feet tall, covered in moss and ferns.

It is hard to spot from Highway 58, especially westbound. A trail climbs the draw from the signed stream crossing; it is easy, though you may get your feet wet.
excerpt: Bridge Creek Falls is a small, scenic, hidden waterfall near Oakridge that drops 64 feet as a veiling horsetail through a narrow alcove beneath a cliff about 15
note: Flow drops in summer; best late April through June.
address: Bridge Creek, off Highway 58 near Oakridge, OR
photoCredit: Bryan Swan / Waterfalls of the Pacific Northwest

title: Diamond Creek Falls
imageAlt: Diamond Creek Falls from the base

banner.alt: Diamond Creek Falls from the base

contentHtml:
Diamond Creek Falls veils 134 feet down jagged, grooved basalt where the creek is about 75 feet wide. Its domed shape makes it look wider than tall from the base, while the height shows best from above. It is one of a pair of large waterfalls on Diamond Creek.

From the far end of the Salt Creek Falls parking loop, cross Salt Creek on the Diamond Creek Falls Trail and bear right. A spur at about 1.25 miles drops a quarter mile to the base, about 1.5 miles one way, and the trail continues about 500 feet to a view from the top.
excerpt: Diamond Creek Falls veils 134 feet down jagged, grooved basalt where the creek is about 75 feet wide. Its domed shape makes it look wider than tall from the bas
note: Many sources list the falls at about 90 feet; a 2023 survey and lidar data support 134 feet.
address: Salt Creek Falls day-use area off Highway 58, 21 miles east of Oakridge (5 miles west of Willamette Pass), OR
photoCredit: Bryan Swan / Waterfalls of the Pacific Northwest

title: Fall Creek Falls
imageAlt: The uppermost 50 feet of Fall Creek Falls

banner.alt: The uppermost 50 feet of Fall Creek Falls

contentHtml:
Fall Creek Falls drops about 90 feet in three steps in the Diamond Peak Wilderness west of Willamette Pass. The upper tier is a 50-foot veiling horsetail; below it the creek turns away from the trail and drops about 30 feet through a narrow horsetail hidden in the canyon.

From the Salt Creek Falls day-use area, take the Vivian Lake Trail across the Salt Creek footbridge, past Diamond Creek and the railroad tracks into the wilderness at about 1.5 miles, then about another mile to a viewpoint on the left marked by a faded sign, about 2.5 miles one way.
excerpt: Fall Creek Falls drops about 90 feet in three steps in the Diamond Peak Wilderness west of Willamette Pass. The upper tier is a 50-foot veiling horsetail; below
note: Fill out a wilderness permit at the boundary. Trees now block about half of the upper tier.
address: Vivian Lake Trail from the Salt Creek Falls day-use area off Highway 58, 21 miles east of Oakridge (5 miles west of Willamette Pass), OR
photoCredit: Bryan Swan / Waterfalls of the Pacific Northwest

title: Indian Holes Falls
contentHtml: Indian Holes Falls is a 117-foot waterfall on Separation Creek in the McKenzie River watershed.
excerpt: Indian Holes Falls is a 117-foot waterfall on Separation Creek in the McKenzie River watershed.
note: No directions or trail information are available.
address: Separation Creek, Three Sisters Wilderness area, OR

title: Lake Creek Falls

gallery.alt: The middle drop from the bottom of the stairs

contentHtml:
Lake Creek Falls is a series of small waterfalls and sliding cascades about half a mile below the outlet of Triangle Lake, 50 feet in all. The top tier is about 40 feet wide and 15 feet tall; the creek then slides down a long ramp to a 10-foot plunge and a final 25-foot slide into a pile of boulders. All three tiers have fish ladders.

From the signed parking area upstream, a trail follows the road to a flight of stairs down to the falls.
excerpt: Lake Creek Falls is a series of small waterfalls and sliding cascades about half a mile below the outlet of Triangle Lake, 50 feet in all. The top tier is about
note: Most impressive in winter and early spring.
address: Highway 36, about 1 mile west of Triangle Lake (26 miles east of Mapleton), OR
photoCredit: Bryan Swan / Waterfalls of the Pacific Northwest

title: Linton Falls
contentHtml:
Linton Falls is the largest waterfall on Linton Creek and in the Three Sisters Wilderness, dropping about 470 feet in eight to ten tiers; the uppermost is about 150 feet. The creek drains the west side of North and Middle Sister and feeds Linton Lake.

The whole falls cannot be seen from any one viewpoint.
excerpt: Linton Falls is the largest waterfall on Linton Creek and in the Three Sisters Wilderness, dropping about 470 feet in eight to ten tiers; the uppermost is about
note: Waterfalls of the Pacific Northwest gives no directions, as there is no developed or officially sanctioned access. The 2017 fire burned nearby trees; watch for hazards.
address: Linton Creek above Linton Lake, Three Sisters Wilderness, OR
photoCredit: Bryan Swan / Waterfalls of the Pacific Northwest

title: Lower Diamond Creek Falls
imageAlt: Lower Diamond Creek Falls seen through the trees

banner.alt: Lower Diamond Creek Falls seen through the trees

contentHtml:
Lower Diamond Creek Falls is where Diamond Creek drops 180 feet in four tiers into the canyon of Salt Creek, a counterpart to nearby Salt Creek Falls. A 60-foot sliding cascade is followed by a 35-foot horsetail, a 60-foot- tall, 60-foot-wide veil (the best of the series) and a final plunge of about 20 feet.

The middle tiers can be seen across the canyon through the trees, about two-thirds of a mile along the Diamond Creek Falls Trail from the Salt Creek Falls parking loop, with another viewpoint about 500 feet farther.
excerpt: Lower Diamond Creek Falls is where Diamond Creek drops 180 feet in four tiers into the canyon of Salt Creek, a counterpart to nearby Salt Creek Falls. A 60-foot
note: Reaching the base means many creek fords and dangerous scrambling and is not advised. The name is unofficial.
address: Salt Creek Falls day-use area off Highway 58, 21 miles east of Oakridge (5 miles west of Willamette Pass), OR
photoCredit: Bryan Swan / Waterfalls of the Pacific Northwest

title: Lower Linton Falls
contentHtml:
Lower Linton Falls is the last significant waterfall on Linton Creek, about a third of a mile above Linton Lake. It drops 111 feet over a basalt cliff into a narrow canyon, where its mist keeps the rock, logs and trees covered in moss, and a small spring runs alongside the main falls.

Fed by winter snow and porous volcanic ground, the creek flows steadily year-round.
excerpt: Lower Linton Falls is the last significant waterfall on Linton Creek, about a third of a mile above Linton Lake. It drops 111 feet over a basalt cliff into a na
note: Waterfalls of the Pacific Northwest gives no directions, as there is no developed or officially sanctioned access. The name is unofficial.
address: Linton Creek, about a third of a mile above Linton Lake, Three Sisters Wilderness, OR
photoCredit: Bryan Swan / Waterfalls of the Pacific Northwest

title: Lower Mesa Falls
contentHtml: Lower Mesa Falls is a 153-foot waterfall on Mesa Creek in the McKenzie River watershed.
excerpt: Lower Mesa Falls is a 153-foot waterfall on Mesa Creek in the McKenzie River watershed.
note: No directions or trail information are available.
address: Mesa Creek, McKenzie River watershed, OR

title: Middle Fall Creek Falls
contentHtml: Middle Fall Creek Falls is a 51-foot plunge about 15 feet wide on Fall Creek. It can be heard from the Vivian Lake Trail and glimpsed through the trees; a 2023 survey found it well downstream of Fall Creek Falls, so it is treated as a separate waterfall.
excerpt: Middle Fall Creek Falls is a 51-foot plunge about 15 feet wide on Fall Creek. It can be heard from the Vivian Lake Trail and glimpsed through the trees; a 2023
note: A clear view means scrambling into a brushy canyon. Waterfalls of the Pacific Northwest gives no directions, as there is no developed or officially sanctioned access. The name is unofficial.
address: Fall Creek, below the Vivian Lake Trail, Diamond Peak Wilderness, OR
photoCredit: Bryan Swan / Waterfalls of the Pacific Northwest

title: Middle Mesa Falls
contentHtml: Middle Mesa Falls is a 70-foot waterfall on Mesa Creek in the McKenzie River watershed.
excerpt: Middle Mesa Falls is a 70-foot waterfall on Mesa Creek in the McKenzie River watershed.
note: No directions or trail information are available.
address: Mesa Creek, McKenzie River watershed, OR

title: Moon Falls
contentHtml:
Moon Falls is a 190-foot veiling horsetail on Alex Creek, presumably the largest waterfall in the Layng Creek watershed, spilling over a steep wall of jagged basalt. From the trail it looks about half its real height.

From I-5 exit 174, take Row River Road east about 19.5 miles, Layng Creek Road (Road 17) 9 miles, Road 1702 about 2.75 miles past the Spirit Falls trailhead, then signed Road 1702-728 to its end. A muddy half-mile trail leads to the base.
excerpt: Moon Falls is a 190-foot veiling horsetail on Alex Creek, presumably the largest waterfall in the Layng Creek watershed, spilling over a steep wall of jagged ba
note: Flow drops to a trickle in late summer but usually holds into early July. No camping or swimming: Layng Creek supplies Cottage Grove's drinking water.
address: End of Road 1702-728, off Layng Creek Road, east of Cottage Grove, OR
photoCredit: Bryan Swan / Waterfalls of the Pacific Northwest

title: Mosquito Falls
contentHtml: Mosquito Falls is shown on USGS maps as a 311-foot waterfall in the McKenzie River watershed. The name is unofficial.
excerpt: Mosquito Falls is shown on USGS maps as a 311-foot waterfall in the McKenzie River watershed. The name is unofficial.
note: No directions or trail information are available.
address: McKenzie River watershed (French Mountain area), OR

title: Pinard Falls
contentHtml:
Pinard Falls drops 105 feet where East Fork Layng Creek is forced through a bedrock notch into a deep gorge. The water has carved a narrow alcove the falls twist into, so they stay shaded much of the day.

The Forest Service trail, completed in 2007, follows an old logging road and then drops steeply in places for about two-thirds of a mile to an overlook across the canyon.
excerpt: Pinard Falls drops 105 feet where East Fork Layng Creek is forced through a bedrock notch into a deep gorge. The water has carved a narrow alcove the falls twis
note: From I-5 exit 174, take Row River Road east about 19.5 miles, Layng Creek Road 9 miles, then bear right and continue 3.75 miles, staying right, to the trailhead. The trail is rough in places.
address: Signed trailhead off Layng Creek Road (Road 17), east of Cottage Grove, OR
photoCredit: Bryan Swan / Waterfalls of the Pacific Northwest

title: Proxy Falls

gallery.alt: Proxy Falls from the end of the trail

contentHtml:
Proxy Falls, fed by springs on the shoulder of North Sister, is among the most photographed waterfalls in Oregon. Proxy Creek drops 226 feet over a wall of mossy columnar basalt and splits into two streams.

The trailhead loop is easy; hiked clockwise it reaches Upper Proxy Falls first and Proxy Falls last, about two- thirds of a mile. Scramble paths lead from the viewpoint to the base.
excerpt: Proxy Falls, fed by springs on the shoulder of North Sister, is among the most photographed waterfalls in Oregon. Proxy Creek drops 226 feet over a wall of moss
note: Highway 242 closes in winter.
address: Proxy Falls Trailhead, Highway 242, about 6.5 miles east of Highway 126, OR
photoCredit: Bryan Swan / Waterfalls of the Pacific Northwest

title: Rainbow Falls
imageAlt: The final three tiers of Rainbow Falls from the base

banner.alt: The final three tiers of Rainbow Falls from the base

contentHtml:
Rainbow Falls is a long series of nearly continuous drops and cascades on Rainbow Creek, about 325 feet in at least six tiers, at the western edge of the Three Sisters Wilderness. Dense forest hides much of it from the viewpoint.

The Rainbow Falls Trail follows an old logging road and then a single-track path about 1.3 miles to a rocky viewpoint across the valley with views of the Three Sisters.
excerpt: Rainbow Falls is a long series of nearly continuous drops and cascades on Rainbow Creek, about 325 feet in at least six tiers, at the western edge of the Three
note: Afternoon light can make the falls hard to see. The base has no developed access, and the route is dangerous.
address: Rainbow Falls Trail, Foley Ridge Road (FS Road 2643), OR
photoCredit: Bryan Swan / Waterfalls of the Pacific Northwest

title: Rider Creek Falls
contentHtml: Rider Creek Falls is a 45-foot waterfall said to be on the main stem of Rider Creek, about half a mile above its mouth. The name was once used for the falls on the creek's south branch now called Terwilliger Falls.
excerpt: Rider Creek Falls is a 45-foot waterfall said to be on the main stem of Rider Creek, about half a mile above its mouth. The name was once used for the falls on
note: No directions or trail information are available.
address: Rider Creek, near Cougar Reservoir, OR

title: Salt Creek Falls
imageAlt: Salt Creek Falls from near its base

banner.alt: Salt Creek Falls from near its base

gallery.alt: Salt Creek Falls from the trail to the bottom

contentHtml:
Salt Creek Falls plunges 286 feet into a sheer-walled canyon, a glacier-carved valley later filled by lava flows, with walls of columnar basalt. The creek is named for nearby salt springs that drew wildlife, and Frank S. Warner and his guide found the falls in 1887.

The first viewpoints are wheelchair accessible, and an easy trail with many stairs leads toward the base.

note: Lidar suggests a height closer to 265 feet; a 2023 survey measured about 284.
address: Salt Creek Falls day-use area off Highway 58, 21 miles east of Oakridge (5 miles west of Willamette Pass), OR
photoCredit: Bryan Swan / Waterfalls of the Pacific Northwest

title: Separation Creek Falls
contentHtml: Separation Creek Falls is a 190-foot waterfall on Separation Creek in the McKenzie River watershed.
excerpt: Separation Creek Falls is a 190-foot waterfall on Separation Creek in the McKenzie River watershed.
note: No directions or trail information are available.
address: Separation Creek, McKenzie River watershed, OR

title: Sweet Creek Falls

gallery.alt: Stairs by a waterfall on the Sweet Creek Trail (photo: Gwyneth Manser)

contentHtml:
Sweet Creek Falls is the largest and best waterfall on the Sweet Creek Trail, which follows the creek through a Coast Range valley past 11 waterfalls framed by mossy rocks and ferns under Douglas fir, alder and bigleaf maple. The main falls drop about 70 feet in four tiers, including a 30-foot horsetail tucked into a narrow cliff recess.

Wooden bridges and metal catwalks carry the trail, and shallow pools along the way invite wading. The falls are about 0.4 mile from the Sweet Creek Falls Trailhead.
excerpt: Sweet Creek Falls is the largest and best waterfall on the Sweet Creek Trail, which follows the creek through a Coast Range valley past 11 waterfalls framed by
note: No fee. Leashed dogs welcome. The Homestead Trailhead and the boardwalk section to the Sweet Creek Falls Trailhead are closed (Forest Order through March 31, 2027); start at the Sweet Creek Falls Trailhead. Mossy rocks are slippery.
address: Sweet Creek Road, about 11 miles south of Highway 126 at Mapleton, OR

title: Terwilliger Falls
imageAlt: Terwilliger Falls from the road in early July

banner.alt: Terwilliger Falls from the road in early July

contentHtml:
Terwilliger Falls plunges about 100 feet straight into Cougar Reservoir and is easy to see from the road. When the reservoir is drawn down in winter, the falls reach about 150 feet.

Park at the Terwilliger Hot Springs lot just beyond the falls and walk back along the lagoon to view them.
excerpt: Terwilliger Falls plunges about 100 feet straight into Cougar Reservoir and is easy to see from the road. When the reservoir is drawn down in winter, the falls
note: Viewing is free; the hot springs charge a day-use fee. Tallest in winter and spring, prettiest when the reservoir is full. The name is proposed, not official.
address: Aufderheide Drive (FR 19) at Cougar Reservoir, about 7.6 miles from Highway 126, OR
photoCredit: Bryan Swan / Waterfalls of the Pacific Northwest

title: Trestle Creek Falls
contentHtml:
Trestle Creek Falls is a small but very attractive 45-foot horsetail at the back of a narrow gorge just off a popular trail. The creek drops into a pool framed by logs and mossy walls, then flows through lush forest to Brice Creek.

Park near the restrooms at the third bridge over Brice Creek, take Brice Creek Trail #1403 downstream about a quarter mile, then Trestle Creek Falls Trail #1403C up the creek about a third of a mile to the base. Upper Trestle Creek Falls Trail #1403D allows a loop.
excerpt: Trestle Creek Falls is a small but very attractive 45-foot horsetail at the back of a narrow gorge just off a popular trail. The creek drops into a pool framed
note: For photos, go within two hours of sunrise or sunset, or on an overcast day.
address: Brice Creek Road (Road 22), 8.3 miles from Row River Road, east of Cottage Grove, OR

title: Upper Bridge Creek Falls
contentHtml: Upper Bridge Creek Falls is a 45-foot horsetail that drops into a deep gorge, so the only easy views are from the side. It can be impressive with good flow but carries little water in dry seasons.
excerpt: Upper Bridge Creek Falls is a 45-foot horsetail that drops into a deep gorge, so the only easy views are from the side. It can be impressive with good flow but
note: Best in spring. Waterfalls of the Pacific Northwest gives no directions, as there is no developed or officially sanctioned access.
address: Bridge Creek, near Oakridge, OR

title: Upper Mesa Falls
contentHtml: Upper Mesa Falls is an 87-foot waterfall on Mesa Creek in the McKenzie River watershed. The name is unofficial.
excerpt: Upper Mesa Falls is an 87-foot waterfall on Mesa Creek in the McKenzie River watershed. The name is unofficial.
note: No directions or trail information are available.
address: Mesa Creek, McKenzie River watershed, OR

title: Upper Proxy Falls

gallery.alt: Looking across the pool at the falls

contentHtml:
Upper Proxy Falls is the lesser of the two waterfalls on the Proxy Falls loop near McKenzie Pass. Spring-fed, it cascades 153 feet down mossy cliffs in two channels that merge near the bottom.

Below the falls the stream runs to a small pool at the edge of a lava flow, then sinks underground and resurfaces at the springs where Lost Creek begins. It is about two-thirds of a mile of easy walking, via the first spur to the left.
excerpt: Upper Proxy Falls is the lesser of the two waterfalls on the Proxy Falls loop near McKenzie Pass. Spring-fed, it cascades 153 feet down mossy cliffs in two chan
note: Small volume but flows year-round. Highway 242 closes in winter.
address: Proxy Falls Trailhead, Highway 242, about 6.5 miles east of Highway 126, OR
photoCredit: Bryan Swan / Waterfalls of the Pacific Northwest

title: Cleawox Lake
imageAlt: Dock near a sandy beach, Honeyman State Park (area photo)

banner.alt: Dock near a sandy beach, Honeyman State Park (area photo)

contentHtml:
Cleawox Lake is a small freshwater lake beside towering dunes near Florence, with a forested shoreline, lily pads, marshy inlets and quiet coves. The suggested paddle is an easy 3.3-mile out-and-back on flatwater with no current or tide, about 1.5 to 2 hours.

Boat traffic is rare; electric motors are allowed.
excerpt: Cleawox Lake is a small freshwater lake beside towering dunes near Florence, with a forested shoreline, lily pads, marshy inlets and quiet coves. The suggested
note: $10 day-use parking permit. Best May through October.
address: Cleawox Lake Boat Ramp, Jessie M. Honeyman Memorial State Park, near Florence, OR

title: Cottage Grove Reservoir
contentHtml:
Cottage Grove Reservoir lies just south of Cottage Grove in the foothills at the south end of the Willamette Valley, with a forested shoreline, open views and coves. Quieter slow-no-wake sections are near Wilson Creek and Cedar Creek; motorboats use the rest.

Lakeside Park has a paved ramp, courtesy dock and day-use facilities, and downtown Cottage Grove, its covered bridges and the Row River Trail are close by.
excerpt: Cottage Grove Reservoir lies just south of Cottage Grove in the foothills at the south end of the Willamette Valley, with a forested shoreline, open views and c
note: Seasonal drawdown can expose shoreline and affect ramps later in the year. Wind and chop build on open water. Check Oregon Health Authority cyanobacteria advisories before paddling.
address: Lakeside Park boat ramp, just south of Cottage Grove, OR (also Wilson Creek and Shortridge)

title: Dexter Reservoir
contentHtml:
Dexter Reservoir is a flatwater reservoir off Highway 58 less than an hour from Eugene, kept near full pool year-round, so its level is fairly stable. Paddlers share it with motorboats, water skiers, sailboats and rowing crews.

Dexter State Recreation Site has a two-lane ramp and courtesy dock, and Lowell State Recreation Site on the north shore has a four-lane ramp, marina, restrooms and swim beach.
excerpt: Dexter Reservoir is a flatwater reservoir off Highway 58 less than an hour from Eugene, kept near full pool year-round, so its level is fairly stable. Paddlers
note: Day-use parking fees at both sites. Oregon Waterway Access Permit required for each kayak, canoe or paddleboard (children 13 and under exempt). Regattas and boat events can close parts of the lake; watch for wakes and wind. Clean, drain and dry your boat.
address: Dexter State Recreation Site or Lowell State Recreation Site, off Highway 58, OR

title: Dorena Reservoir
contentHtml:
Dorena Reservoir lies east of Cottage Grove among forested hills. Anglers and motorboats share it, and a designated slow-no-wake area suits kayaks, canoes and paddleboards.

Baker Bay Park has a ramp, marina, swimming area, campground and picnic area. Harms Park, usable when water levels allow, has a free ramp, vault toilet and access to the paved Row River Trail.
excerpt: Dorena Reservoir lies east of Cottage Grove among forested hills. Anglers and motorboats share it, and a designated slow-no-wake area suits kayaks, canoes and p
note: Oregon Waterway Access Permit required for each kayak, canoe or paddleboard (children 13 and under exempt). Changing levels can leave ramps dry. Wind can make open water rough. Check Oregon Health Authority cyanobacteria advisories before paddling.
address: Baker Bay Park (Lane County Parks) or Harms Park, east of Cottage Grove, OR

title: Fall Creek Reservoir
contentHtml:
Fall Creek Reservoir is a forest-lined lake southeast of Eugene and Springfield that stretches for several miles through the foothills at full pool. Its coves and creek arms invite exploring beyond the open water.

Winberry has a swim beach, swim dock and flush restrooms, and Cascara Campground has seasonal camping and drinking water.
excerpt: Fall Creek Reservoir is a forest-lined lake southeast of Eugene and Springfield that stretches for several miles through the foothills at full pool. Its coves a
note: Oregon Waterway Access Permit required for each kayak, canoe or paddleboard (children 13 and under exempt). Winberry day-use parking permit required. Slow-no-wake on upper Fall Creek and Winberry Creek. Drawdown can expose stumps and logs and leave ramps unusable.
address: North Shore, Winberry or Cascara ramps, Fall Creek Reservoir, southeast of Eugene, OR

title: Fern Ridge Reservoir
imageAlt: Small boat on Fern Ridge waterways

banner.alt: Small boat on Fern Ridge waterways

contentHtml:
Fern Ridge Reservoir is a large reservoir just west of Eugene with open water, extensive wetlands and abundant birdlife, including Oregon's largest breeding colony of purple martins. Kayaks, paddleboards, canoes and motorboats all use it.

Orchard Point Park has a ramp, dock, marina, restrooms and swimming; Perkins Peninsula, Richardson and Zumwalt parks and the rustic Shore Lane Park are other access points.
excerpt: Fern Ridge Reservoir is a large reservoir just west of Eugene with open water, extensive wetlands and abundant birdlife, including Oregon's largest breeding col
note: Lane County parking pass required at Orchard Point. Wind over open water can be strong; levels drop seasonally. Check Oregon Health Authority cyanobacteria advisories before paddling.
address: Orchard Point Park (north side), Fern Ridge Reservoir, west of Eugene, OR

title: Mercer Lake
contentHtml:
Mercer Lake is a freshwater coastal lake in forested hills just north of Florence, shared by kayaks, paddleboards, canoes, anglers and motorboats.

Mercer Lake Landing has a paved back-in ramp, an accessible vault restroom and a small gravel lot for about 10 cars and trailers uphill across the road.
excerpt: Mercer Lake is a freshwater coastal lake in forested hills just north of Florence, shared by kayaks, paddleboards, canoes, anglers and motorboats.
note: Lane County parking pass required. Oregon Waterway Access Permit required for each kayak, canoe or paddleboard (children 13 and under exempt). Summer boat traffic and wind. Check Oregon Health Authority cyanobacteria advisories before paddling.
address: Mercer Lake Landing (Lane County Parks), east shore, just north of Florence, OR

title: Munsel Lake
contentHtml: Munsel Lake is a compact, forested freshwater lake minutes from Florence, with water lilies, submerged trees, weathered timber and quiet coves. The suggested paddle is an easy 2.17-mile flatwater loop, about 1 to 1.5 hours.
excerpt: Munsel Lake is a compact, forested freshwater lake minutes from Florence, with water lilies, submerged trees, weathered timber and quiet coves. The suggested pa
note: Parking fee. Motorboats allowed at 10 mph. Afternoon wind; mornings are calmest. Best April through October.
address: Munsel Lake Landing County Park boat ramp, near Florence, OR

title: Siltcoos River
contentHtml: The upper Siltcoos River paddle runs from broad open water into a narrower forested channel, an easy 3.4- mile out-and-back of about 1.5 to 2.5 hours that turns around above the Siltcoos River dam.
excerpt: The upper Siltcoos River paddle runs from broad open water into a narrower forested channel, an easy 3.4- mile out-and-back of about 1.5 to 2.5 hours that turns
note: Lane County day-use parking pass (pay on site). Watch for overhanging trees, fallen timber, current and motorboats with no speed limit. Best May through October.
address: Westlake County Park boat ramp, Westlake, near Florence, OR

title: Siuslaw River Water Trail
contentHtml:
The Siuslaw Water Trail covers more than 30 river miles of the North Fork and mainstem Siuslaw between Mapleton and Florence, from the head of tide through estuary islands, coastal forest and sand dunes. Sea otters, blue herons, osprey and salmon live along the way.

Day trips can start from the Port of Siuslaw, Bender Landing or Mapleton. Paper brochures are at the Siuslaw Watershed Council office and the Florence Chamber of Commerce.
excerpt: The Siuslaw Water Trail covers more than 30 river miles of the North Fork and mainstem Siuslaw between Mapleton and Florence, from the head of tide through estu
note: Wear a life jacket, check weather and tides, and keep well clear of barges and large fishing boats. Email: watershed@siuslaw.org
address: Siuslaw Watershed Council, 10868 East Mapleton Road, Mapleton, OR 97453

title: Sutton Lake
contentHtml: Sutton Lake is a forest-framed freshwater lake minutes from Florence, with dark water, quiet coves and lily- covered shallows. The suggested paddle is an easy 2.9-mile flatwater out-and-back, about 1.5 to 2 hours, with little boat traffic.
excerpt: Sutton Lake is a forest-framed freshwater lake minutes from Florence, with dark water, quiet coves and lily- covered shallows. The suggested paddle is an easy 2
note: Motorboats allowed at 10 mph. Wind builds later in the day; go in the morning. Best May through September.
address: Sutton Lake Boat Ramp, just north of Florence, OR

title: Waldo Lake
contentHtml:
Waldo Lake is a large mountain lake in the western Cascades, about 9.8 square miles and roughly 427 feet deep at about 5,400 feet, famous for its very clear water and forested shore. It is not a small, sheltered beginner lake.

Shadow Bay, the main access, has ample parking, vault toilets and picnic tables but no drinking water.
excerpt: Waldo Lake is a large mountain lake in the western Cascades, about 9.8 square miles and roughly 427 feet deep at about 5,400 feet, famous for its very clear wat
note: $5 per vehicle per day or recreation pass. Oregon Waterway Access Permit required for each kayak, canoe or paddleboard (children 13 and under exempt). No gas engines; electric motors under 10 mph. Afternoon wind builds fast and the water is cold; mosquitoes heavy in early summer. Islet and North Waldo launches are closed under the Cedar Creek Fire order.
address: Shadow Bay Day Use Area, south end of Waldo Lake, east of Oakridge, OR

title: Willamette River Water Trail
imageAlt: Paddlers on the Willamette River Water Trail

banner.alt: Paddlers on the Willamette River Water Trail

contentHtml:
The Willamette River Water Trail follows 187 miles of the mainstem Willamette River, from the Eugene and Springfield area north to Portland. It passes forests, meadows, parks, farms and cities, and it is open to canoes, kayaks, stand-up paddleboards, rafts and drift boats.

Designated Water Trail campsites along the river let paddlers plan multi-day trips. The trail begins in the Eugene and Springfield area.

note: Oregon Waterway Access Permit required for paddle craft 10 ft and longer
