imageAlt: Boats on the lake, Honeyman State Park (area photo)

banner.alt: Boats on the lake, Honeyman State Park (area photo)

contentHtml: Woahink Lake is a freshwater lake just south of Florence with open water, narrow fingers and tucked-away coves. Lily pads, submerged logs and clear water line its forested shore. The suggested paddle is an easy 3.95- mile flatwater out-and-back, about 1.5 to 2 hours.
excerpt: Woahink Lake is a freshwater lake just south of Florence with open water, narrow fingers and tucked-away coves. Lily pads, submerged logs and clear water line i
note: Paved parking at the ramp. Motorboats share the lake. Afternoon wind; go in the morning.
address: East Woahink Lake Boat Ramp, just south of Florence, OR

title: South Sister
contentHtml: South Sister is a 10,358-foot volcano in the Three Sisters Wilderness, its summit on the Lane-Deschutes county line. The standard route, the South Sister Climber Trail from Devils Lake Trailhead, is about 12 miles round trip with about 4,900 feet of gain: no technical climbing, but very demanding. The Green Lakes/Soda Creek Trailhead is a longer alternative.
excerpt: South Sister is a 10,358-foot volcano in the Three Sisters Wilderness, its summit on the Lane-Deschutes county line. The standard route, the South Sister Climbe
note: From June 15 to October 15 a reserved Central Cascades Wilderness day-use permit is needed at the Devils Lake and Green Lakes trailheads, and an overnight permit for any night in the wilderness; book on Recreation.gov. A federal recreation pass is needed to park.
address: Devils Lake Trailhead, Cascade Lakes Highway (46), west of Bend, OR

title: Oregon Coast Trail
imageAlt: Oregon Coast Trail sign along a forested trail

banner.alt: Oregon Coast Trail sign along a forested trail

contentHtml:
The Oregon Coast Trail follows Oregon's coastline from the Columbia River to the California border, about 382 miles by the official guide and about 425 miles if no ferries are used around the estuaries. It passes through 28 coastal towns.

Most of the route is on the beach, with other sections through state parks and public lands, on private land under trail easements, and on road shoulders.

Hiker/biker tent sites, first-come first-served, are at nearly every coastal state park. Check tide times, as some areas are passable only at low tide. During western snowy plover nesting season (March 15 to September 15), walk on wet sand in protected areas, where dogs, camping and beach fires are not allowed.
excerpt: The Oregon Coast Trail follows Oregon's coastline from the Columbia River to the California border, about 382 miles by the official guide and about 425 miles if
note: Trail conditions change quickly; check Oregon State Parks notices and Trailkeepers of Oregon alerts before you go.
address: Runs the length of the Oregon coast, including Lane County

title: Oregon Timber Trail
contentHtml:
The Oregon Timber Trail is a 670-mile mountain bike and bikepacking route from the California border near Lakeview north to Hood River on the Columbia, managed by the nonprofit Oregon Timber Trail Alliance. It is split into four tiers: Fremont, Willamette, Deschutes and Hood.

Riders can take on the whole route or ride a shorter piece of any tier.

address: California border near Lakeview to Hood River, OR

title: Pacific Crest Trail
contentHtml:
The Pacific Crest National Scenic Trail runs 2,650 miles from Mexico to Canada through California, Oregon and Washington, managed by the Forest Service with the Pacific Crest Trail Association. Its roughly 455-mile Oregon section is the shortest and easiest on the trail, from near Siskiyou Summit to the Bridge of the Gods over the Columbia River.

In Lane County the trail follows the Cascade crest through the Diamond Peak, Three Sisters and Mount Washington wildernesses.

note: Central Cascades Wilderness permits apply in the Three Sisters Wilderness from June 15 to October 15.
address: Oregon section: California border near Ashland to the Bridge of the Gods, Cascade Locks, OR

title: Row River Trail
imageAlt: Bicyclists enjoying a lakeside vista along the Row River Trail

banner.alt: Bicyclists enjoying a lakeside vista along the Row River Trail

contentHtml:
The Row River Trail is a paved, multi-use National Recreation Trail on a former Oregon Pacific & Eastern Railroad line along the Row River and Dorena Reservoir. The trail is 8 to 10 feet wide with grades never over 5%, and parking and restrooms are spaced every 2 to 3 miles. BLM states that the trail and its facilities meet or exceed accessibility standards.

BLM manages 14 miles from Mosby Creek to Culp Creek; with the City of Cottage Grove's in-town segment the trail runs about 15.6 miles. Viewpoints overlook Dorena Lake and farmland, and the Harms Park trestle and other spots along the way appeared in Stand By Me, Emperor of the North and The General.
excerpt: The Row River Trail is a paved, multi-use National Recreation Trail on a former Oregon Pacific & Eastern Railroad line along the Row River and Dorena Reservoir.
note: Free. Day use only, no camping. No food or water on the trail; stores are in Cottage Grove, Dorena and Culp Creek. From I-5 exit 174, go east 3.5 miles on Row River Road, then right 1.2 miles on Layng Road.
address: Mosby Creek Trailhead, corner of Layng Road and Mosby Creek Road, Cottage Grove, OR

title: Salt Creek Falls Observation Site
imageAlt: Salt Creek Falls from near its base

banner.alt: Salt Creek Falls from near its base

gallery.alt: Salt Creek Falls from the trail to the bottom

contentHtml:
Salt Creek Falls, Oregon's second-highest single-drop waterfall at 286 feet, is seen from an observation platform about 50 yards from the parking lot. The platform is wheelchair accessible, with railings designed for wheelchair sight-lines.

A paved loop trail with interpretive signs follows the canyon rim to several viewpoints. The steep trail with stairs down to the base of the falls is not accessible. Vault toilets and picnic tables are on site; there is no drinking water.
excerpt: Salt Creek Falls, Oregon's second-highest single-drop waterfall at 286 feet, is seen from an observation platform about 50 yards from the parking lot. The platf
note: $5 per vehicle per day, or a Northwest Forest Pass or interagency pass. Normally closed in winter, when the lot is not plowed; park at the Salt Creek Sno-Park 0.4 mile up the road and walk in.
address: Forest Service Road 5893 off Highway 58 (east of milepost 57), 23 miles southeast of Oakridge, OR
photoCredit: Bryan Swan / Waterfalls of the Pacific Northwest

title: Darlingtonia State Natural Site Boardwalk
contentHtml:
Darlingtonia State Natural Site is Oregon's only state park dedicated to a single plant, the carnivorous cobra lily. A short, flat boardwalk loop of about 0.2 mile winds through the peat-bog fen and is described as wheelchair accessible.

The pavement is becoming uneven in a few spots, where a wheelchair user may need a hand. A restroom and picnic tables are on site.
excerpt: Darlingtonia State Natural Site is Oregon's only state park dedicated to a single plant, the carnivorous cobra lily. A short, flat boardwalk loop of about 0.2 m
note: Free. Open year-round.
address: 5400 Mercer Lake Rd, Florence, OR (5 miles north of Florence)

title: David's Chair - Florence
imageAlt: David's Chair on the beach in Florence

banner.alt: David's Chair on the beach in Florence

contentHtml:
David's Chair Outdoor Mobility Systems, a White City nonprofit founded in memory of Medford outdoorsman David Hartrick, lends powered, tracked all-terrain Action Trackchairs free of charge. A chair is stationed at Heceta Beach County Park in Florence, where it is used on the beach access north of Driftwood Shores.

Book a session (roughly 2 hours, usually Thursday to Sunday) online; a representative follows up to sign waivers, then a volunteer meets you at the park. Requests made less than 72 hours ahead may not be filled. The park also has a seasonal Mobi-Mat.
excerpt: David's Chair Outdoor Mobility Systems, a White City nonprofit founded in memory of Medford outdoorsman David Hartrick, lends powered, tracked all-terrain Actio
note: Free. Reserve at davidschair.org/request-fixed-location-chair. Lane County Parks day pass or annual pass required for parking.
address: Heceta Beach County Park, 88466 1st Ave, Florence, OR

title: David's Chair - Eugene (Mount Pisgah)
contentHtml:
Mount Pisgah Arboretum lends two narrow all-terrain track chairs made by Action Trackchair, so visitors with limited mobility can explore its more than seven miles of trails. The arboretum hosted chairs through David's Chair for two years and now owns two chairs and runs the program itself, with Lane County Parks and McKenzie River Trust as partners.

Volunteers check the chairs out and show users how to operate them. The arboretum also has an Improved Access Loop of lowland trails and a Barrier Free Loop.

note: Free. Reserve the Blue Chair or Green Chair online or call (541) 747-3817; note in the reservation if you need a paved ADA spot near the White Oak Pavilion. $5 Lane County Parks day pass required. Email: office@mountpisgaharboretum.com
address: Mount Pisgah Arboretum, 34901 Frank Parrish Road, Eugene, OR 97405

title: Mobi-Mat - Florence (Heceta Beach)
contentHtml:
Heceta Beach County Park, next to Driftwood Shores, has a Mobi-Mat: a non-slip, weather-proof pathway about 120 feet long and 6 feet wide that leads across the sand to the beach for wheelchairs, strollers, wagons and people with limited mobility. It was funded by an Oregon Coast Visitors Association grant with support from Travel Lane County.

The park also has a free David's Chair track chair, a shaded picnic area, vault restrooms and parking for about 20 cars.

title: Aufderheide Scenic Bikeway
imageAlt: Riders on the Aufderheide Scenic Bikeway (courtesy of Cycle Oregon)

banner.alt: Riders on the Aufderheide Scenic Bikeway (courtesy of Cycle Oregon)

gallery.alt: Cyclists crossing a bridge above the river (courtesy of Cycle Oregon)
Cyclists riding toward a covered bridge (courtesy of Cycle Oregon)

contentHtml:
The Aufderheide Scenic Bikeway follows Aufderheide Drive (Forest Road 19) for about 60 miles one way between Westfir and Rainbow, entirely in Lane County. The smooth, quiet paved road climbs almost 4,000 feet through old-growth forest along the North Fork Middle Fork Willamette and McKenzie rivers. It was designated in 2024 as Oregon's 18th Scenic Bikeway.

Stops include the Cougar Dam overlook, six miles along Cougar Reservoir, Terwilliger Hot Springs, Box Canyon Guard Station, Constitution Grove and the Office Covered Bridge, Oregon's longest. Many riders go one way and stay at Westfir Lodge.
excerpt: The Aufderheide Scenic Bikeway follows Aufderheide Drive (Forest Road 19) for about 60 miles one way between Westfir and Rainbow, entirely in Lane County. The s
note: Rated extreme: an all-day ride. Check TripCheck.com or call 511 and the McKenzie River and Middle Fork ranger stations for road conditions.
address: Office Covered Bridge Portal Park, Westfir (south end) to Rainbow near McKenzie Bridge (north end), OR

title: Bee Line
imageAlt: Riding the paved bike path in Honeyman State Park

banner.alt: Riding the paved bike path in Honeyman State Park

contentHtml:
Bee Line is a 23-mile lollipop gravel ride with about 2,200 feet of climbing, roughly 25% gravel and 75% paved. Rated easier, it is a shorter version of the Honeyman route.

It starts on singletrack among big old trees in Honeyman State Park, follows Maple Creek past farmland, climbs about 950 feet into Coast Range forest, and returns on a twisting paved descent past several lakes.

note: Honeyman State Park parking permit required (available on site); flush toilets and water at the start. No food on the route. Logging country: ride single file with lights. Rideable most of the year.
address: Start: Honeyman State Park sand dunes parking area, near Florence, OR

title: Conductor Willy
contentHtml:
Conductor Willy is a 35-mile out-and-back gravel ride with about 2,000 feet of climbing, roughly 85% gravel. Rated easier, it follows the shore of Lookout Point Lake and the Middle Fork Willamette River, crossing the rail line five times.

The turnaround is in the old company town of Westfir, through the old mill site and across the Office Covered Bridge, Oregon's longest. Westfir Lodge and Mountain Market (seasonal) are at about mile 17.
excerpt: Conductor Willy is a 35-mile out-and-back gravel ride with about 2,000 feet of climbing, roughly 85% gravel. Rated easier, it follows the shore of Lookout Point
note: No fee at Signal Point; pit toilets. Very limited cell service. Rideable almost year-round.
address: Start: Signal Point Day Use Area, Lookout Point Lake, near Lowell, OR

title: Cool & Shady
contentHtml:
Cool & Shady is a 52-mile gravel loop with about 4,200 feet of climbing, 40% gravel and 60% paved, rated moderate. It is a go-to summer ride, shaded even at midday.

The route runs along Hills Creek Reservoir, then 16 paved miles beside the Middle Fork Willamette River, climbs about 2,800 feet up Swift Creek to an alpine meadow with views of Diamond Peak, and descends Hills Creek.
excerpt: Cool & Shady is a 52-mile gravel loop with about 4,200 feet of climbing, 40% gravel and 60% paved, rated moderate. It is a go-to summer ride, shaded even at mid
note: No food or water on the route; carry 70 to 100 ounces on a hot day. Red blinking light recommended for traffic on paved sections.
address: Start: dirt pullout south of the Hills Creek Crossing bridge at NF 2118, Hills Creek Reservoir, near Oakridge, OR

title: Covered Bridges Scenic Bikeway
imageAlt: Covered Bridges Scenic Bikeway (photo: Russ Roca)

banner.alt: Covered Bridges Scenic Bikeway (photo: Russ Roca)

gallery.alt: A family riding a leaf-covered path (photo: Russ Roca)
A family with their bikes under a covered bridge (photo: Russ Roca)

contentHtml:
The Covered Bridges Scenic Bikeway is a 35-mile loop from downtown Cottage Grove, designated in 2011. It is mostly flat and family friendly, with little or no traffic, and includes 17 miles of the paved Row River Trail along Dorena Lake to Culp Creek.

Riders pass the Chambers Covered Railroad Bridge, the only covered railroad bridge west of the Mississippi on the National Register, the Dorena Bridge and three more covered bridges, the historic downtown and views of the Cascade foothills. It can also be ridden as an out-and-back on the trail instead of returning by road.
excerpt: The Covered Bridges Scenic Bikeway is a 35-mile loop from downtown Cottage Grove, designated in 2011. It is mostly flat and family friendly, with little or no t
note: One climb on Garoutte Road can be bypassed. Start at the Mosby Creek Trailhead for a car-free ride. Restrooms at Schwarz, Bake Stewart and Wilson Creek parks.
address: Trailhead Park, Main St and 10th St, Cottage Grove, OR

title: Dinner with Brice
contentHtml:
Dinner with Brice is a 49-mile lollipop gravel ride with about 4,900 feet of climbing, 25% gravel and 75% paved, rated moderate. A mostly shaded climb of about 3,700 feet over 16 miles reaches Holland Meadows, with views of the Three Sisters.

A fast descent follows Brice Creek past mossy trees, ferns and small waterfalls, through the old logging town of Disston, with swimming spots including Wildwood Falls at the finish.
excerpt: Dinner with Brice is a 49-mile lollipop gravel ride with about 4,900 feet of climbing, 25% gravel and 75% paved, rated moderate. A mostly shaded climb of about
note: About 8 parking spots at Wildwood Falls; overflow at LaSells Stewart Park across the river (Lane County parking pass). No food or water. Active logging area: check with the ranger district.
address: Start: Wildwood Falls County Park, Row River, east of Cottage Grove, OR

title: Dirty Aufderheide
contentHtml:
Dirty Aufderheide is a 124-mile gravel loop with about 11,100 feet of climbing, 33% gravel, 2% singletrack and 65% paved. Rated moderate, it follows most of the classic Aufderheide Drive between the McKenzie River and Oakridge, then branches onto remote Forest Service roads above the river corridors.

Mountain peaks, hidden lakes, waterfalls and creeks line the way. It can be ridden over two days, or as a 114- mile one-day loop from the Office Covered Bridge in Westfir.
excerpt: Dirty Aufderheide is a 124-mile gravel loop with about 11,100 feet of climbing, 33% gravel, 2% singletrack and 65% paved. Rated moderate, it follows most of the
note: Parking at the community center is not monitored; a $10 donation is suggested. Active timberlands. Best mid-spring to late fall.
address: Start: Upper McKenzie Community Center, near McKenzie Bridge, OR (alt starts at Westfir)

title: Greenwaters
contentHtml:
Greenwaters is a 29-mile lollipop around Hills Creek Reservoir with about 1,200 feet of climbing: 35% gravel, 5% singletrack and 60% paved, rated easier. The start and finish follow a wide singletrack through mossy old- growth forest along the Middle Fork Willamette River.

The loop runs clockwise around the reservoir on mostly paved, tree-canopied roads with lake views and one climb near the dam.
excerpt: Greenwaters is a 29-mile lollipop around Hills Creek Reservoir with about 1,200 feet of climbing: 35% gravel, 5% singletrack and 60% paved, rated easier. The st
note: Flush toilets at the start; $5 donation suggested. No food or water. Best on warm winter or spring days; heavy lake traffic Memorial Day to Labor Day.
address: Start: Greenwaters Park (east parking lot), Oakridge, OR

title: Honeyman
imageAlt: Riding the paved path in Honeyman State Park

banner.alt: Riding the paved path in Honeyman State Park

contentHtml:
Honeyman is a 54-mile lollipop gravel ride with about 5,300 feet of climbing, about 30% gravel and 70% paved, many of the paved miles on single-lane logging roads. It is extremely remote.

Highlights include Sweet Creek Falls, quiet roads along Siltcoos Lake, the dunes and the Civilian Conservation Corps bathhouse at Cleawox Lake, Maple Creek farmland and a logging-road climb.
excerpt: Honeyman is a 54-mile lollipop gravel ride with about 5,300 feet of climbing, about 30% gravel and 70% paved, many of the paved miles on single-lane logging roa
note: Parking permit required (available on site); water and flush toilets at the start. No food or water on the route. Best late March to early June.
address: Start: Honeyman State Park sand dunes parking area, south of Florence, OR

title: Huck & Heidi
contentHtml:
Huck & Heidi is a 51-mile gravel loop with about 4,000 feet of climbing, 35% gravel and 65% paved, rated demanding. It climbs Huckleberry Road, then rides two sections of the Aufderheide Scenic Byway along the Willamette River.

Wild rhododendrons, beargrass, mossy trees and the Office Covered Bridge, Oregon's longest, line the way.
excerpt: Huck & Heidi is a 51-mile gravel loop with about 4,000 feet of climbing, 35% gravel and 65% paved, rated demanding. It climbs Huckleberry Road, then rides two s
note: Water and flush toilets at the start. No food or water on the route. Steep descents near miles 15 and 33. Best in early summer and fall.
address: Start: Office Covered Bridge parking area, Westfir, OR

title: McKenzie Pass Scenic Bikeway

gallery.alt: Reaching the top of the pass

contentHtml:
The McKenzie Pass Scenic Bikeway is an epic one-way road ride of about 35 miles from Sisters west over McKenzie Pass on Highway 242, which follows an 1860s wagon route. After an easy first 8 miles, a climb of about 5 miles starts at McGregor's Curve and passes Windy Point, with views of Mt. Washington, and lava- rock walls to the summit.

At the top, a lava 'moonscape' surrounds the Dee Wright Observatory, whose windows frame 360-degree views. The 25-mile descent drops about 4,000 feet through switchbacks into the wetter McKenzie River forests to Highway 126.
excerpt: The McKenzie Pass Scenic Bikeway is an epic one-way road ride of about 35 miles from Sisters west over McKenzie Pass on Highway 242, which follows an 1860s wago
note: Rated extreme; requires top fitness. Restrooms and water at Village Green Park, the summit and the McKenzie General Store. Highway 242 closes seasonally: check TripCheck.com or ODOT District 10 in Bend (541-388-6169) for conditions. Published lengths range from 35 to 38 miles.
address: Start: Village Green Park, Sisters, OR

title: Moon Moss
contentHtml:
Moon Moss is a 43-mile gravel loop with about 4,900 feet of climbing, 70% gravel, rated demanding. It climbs about 2,700 feet in just over 6 miles to Moon Point, then visits the Warner Mountain lookout.

Beargrass fields on Warner Ridge, views of Diamond Peak, Mount Thielsen and Bailey Peak from Juniper Ridge, a Swift Creek descent and a gentle paved finish along the Middle Fork Willamette River follow.
excerpt: Moon Moss is a 43-mile gravel loop with about 4,900 feet of climbing, 70% gravel, rated demanding. It climbs about 2,700 feet in just over 6 miles to Moon Point
note: No food or water; limited cell service. Best in mid-summer, when the flowers bloom.
address: Start: pullout past the Middle Fork Willamette bridge at NF 2127 and NF 21, near Oakridge, OR

title: O'Leary Landslide Loop
imageAlt: Two cyclists on a paved road

banner.alt: Two cyclists on a paved road

contentHtml:
O'Leary Landslide Loop is a 56-mile loop with about 5,500 feet of climbing, mixing gravel, trail, broken pavement and paved road. Rated very demanding and extremely remote, it opens with a climb of about 3,500 feet in 10 miles.

After a nearly 10-mile gravel descent to Cougar Reservoir, with a swim at the boat ramp, the route loops the reservoir and descends to the Belknap Covered Bridge and the McKenzie River.
excerpt: O'Leary Landslide Loop is a 56-mile loop with about 5,500 feet of climbing, mixing gravel, trail, broken pavement and paved road. Rated very demanding and extre
note: Miles 5 and 10 cross a decommissioned road with landslides and fallen trees: expect hike-a-bike. Ride with others and carry a satellite messenger. E-bikes not recommended. Best late spring and early summer.
address: Start: McKenzie Bridge General Store, McKenzie Bridge, OR (ask staff before parking)

title: Roaring Buffalo
contentHtml:
Roaring Buffalo is a gravel loop of about 38.5 to 40 miles with about 3,500 feet of climbing, roughly 65% gravel, rated moderate. Nearly all the climbing comes in the first 23 miles, through shaded forest of Douglas- fir, cedar and red alder.

A long, winding descent called the Grasshopper starts around mile 23, and the last 10 miles follow the river with views of Buffalo Peak and old-growth trees. Elk, deer and owls are often seen.
excerpt: Roaring Buffalo is a gravel loop of about 38.5 to 40 miles with about 3,500 feet of climbing, roughly 65% gravel, rated moderate. Nearly all the climbing comes
note: No food or water. Snow can linger at higher elevations (miles 15 to 20). Watch for potholes on the descent. Best spring through fall.
address: Start: dirt pullout on the west side of the North Fork road (Aufderheide Drive), driving in from Oakridge/Westfir, OR

title: Row River Trail
imageAlt: Bicyclists enjoying a lakeside vista along the Row River Trail

banner.alt: Bicyclists enjoying a lakeside vista along the Row River Trail

contentHtml:
The Row River Trail is a 16.4-mile paved rail-trail on a former Oregon Pacific & Eastern Railroad line from Cottage Grove to Culp Creek, a former logging mill site. It follows the Row River past Dorena Dam and along Dorena Lake, passing historic covered bridges, and is part of the Covered Bridges Scenic Bikeway.

The first 3 miles, from Cottage Grove to the Mosby Creek Trailhead, are managed by the city and the rest by the Bureau of Land Management. Trailheads include Mosby Creek, Dorena Dam and Harms Park.
excerpt: The Row River Trail is a 16.4-mile paved rail-trail on a former Oregon Pacific & Eastern Railroad line from Cottage Grove to Culp Creek, a former logging mill s
note: Mostly flat. Root heaves in the pavement are marked with paint.
address: Trailhead on E Main St, Cottage Grove, to Culp Creek Trailhead, 37802 Row River Rd, OR

title: Siltcoos Station
contentHtml:
Siltcoos Station is a 17-mile lollipop with about 1,000 feet of climbing, mostly on narrow, winding paved roads with about 15% gravel. Rated easier, it is almost a road ride.

It passes Siltcoos Lake, the largest lake on the Oregon coast, its wetlands, rural farmland and Coast Range forest.
excerpt: Siltcoos Station is a 17-mile lollipop with about 1,000 feet of climbing, mostly on narrow, winding paved roads with about 15% gravel. Rated easier, it is almos
note: No food or water. Red blinking light and rear radar recommended. Year-round; best in spring.
address: Start: gravel pit parking on the north side of Canary Road, just before the Siuslaw Valley Fire & Rescue station, near Florence, OR

title: Willamette Valley Scenic Bikeway

gallery.alt: On the Willamette Valley Scenic Bikeway

contentHtml:
The Willamette Valley Scenic Bikeway, the first official Scenic Bikeway in the United States, runs 135 paved miles one way along the Willamette River between the Coast Range and the Cascades. Its southern end is Armitage County Park near Coburg in Lane County.

The moderate route passes hop fields, vineyards and small towns, Champoeg State Heritage Area, Keizer and the Capitol in Salem, Ankeny National Wildlife Refuge and Thompson's Mills State Heritage Site, with side trips to the Wheatland and Buena Vista ferries. Its high point is 740 feet, after Brownsville.
excerpt: The Willamette Valley Scenic Bikeway, the first official Scenic Bikeway in the United States, runs 135 paved miles one way along the Willamette River between th
note: Rideable year-round; bring rain gear in winter. April through November brings sunshine, flowers and farmers markets.
address: Armitage County Park, Coburg (south end) to Champoeg State Heritage Area (north end), OR

title: Lobster Creek
contentHtml:
Lobster Creek winds through rolling foothills and riparian meadows in the Oregon Coast Range. About 5 miles of the creek were designated a recreational Wild and Scenic River on March 12, 2019, under the Dingell Act, and the BLM adopted its Comprehensive River Management Plan in September 2025.

Its cold, clean water makes it one of the region's leading salmonid producers, with resident cutthroat trout, Pacific lamprey, wild fall chinook and coho salmon and winter steelhead. Forests along the creek are managed to sustain mature and old-growth stands, and lightly traveled Lobster Creek Road runs alongside, giving visitors a quiet setting.
excerpt: Lobster Creek winds through rolling foothills and riparian meadows in the Oregon Coast Range. About 5 miles of the creek were designated a recreational Wild and
note: Email: blm_or_no_mail@blm.gov
address: Lobster Creek Road, Oregon Coast Range (BLM Northwest Oregon District, Marys Peak Field Office)
photoCredit: Bureau of Land Management via National Wild and Scenic Rivers System

title: McKenzie River
contentHtml:
The McKenzie River rises at Clear Lake in the central Oregon Cascades and flows south and west through the Willamette National Forest. On October 28, 1988, 12.7 miles from Clear Creek to Scott Creek were designated a recreational Wild and Scenic River, not including the Carmen and Trail Bridge reservoir dams.

Lava flows shaped its pools, waterfalls and whitewater: lava from Belknap Crater dammed the river to create Sahalie and Koosah falls. Known as the "Blue McKenzie" for its clear, cold water, it has wild rainbow, bull and cutthroat trout and spring chinook, challenging whitewater, and the 26-mile McKenzie River National Recreation Trail.
excerpt: The McKenzie River rises at Clear Lake in the central Oregon Cascades and flows south and west through the Willamette National Forest. On October 28, 1988, 12.7
note: Managed by the Willamette National Forest. The designated reach crosses Linn and Lane counties.
address: Willamette National Forest, along OR 126 between Clear Lake and Trail Bridge, OR
photoCredit: National Wild and Scenic Rivers System

title: North Fork Middle Fork Willamette River
imageAlt: North Fork of the Middle Fork Willamette River (photo: Greg Vaughn)

banner.alt: North Fork of the Middle Fork Willamette River (photo: Greg Vaughn)

contentHtml:
The North Fork of the Middle Fork Willamette River was designated a Wild and Scenic River on October 28, 1988: 42.3 miles from Waldo Lake to the Willamette National Forest boundary (8.8 wild, 6.5 scenic and 27 recreational). Water quality is one of its most outstanding traits, and its source, Waldo Lake, is considered one of the purest lakes in the world.

A steep glaciated valley holds 34 waterfalls in a three-mile stretch. The river is managed for wild trout with fly-fishing-only rules, played a key role in the logging history of Westfir, and parallels Aufderheide Drive for about 30 miles. Roosevelt elk, black-tailed deer, black bears, northern spotted owls and bald eagles live here.
excerpt: The North Fork of the Middle Fork Willamette River was designated a Wild and Scenic River on October 28, 1988: 42.3 miles from Waldo Lake to the Willamette Nati
note: Managed by the Willamette National Forest.
address: Aufderheide Drive (Forest Road 19) north of Westfir, Willamette National Forest, OR
photoCredit: Greg Vaughn / National Wild and Scenic Rivers System

title: Cottage Grove Covered Bridge Tour Route
imageAlt: Mosby Creek Covered Bridge (photo: David Bassett)

banner.alt: Mosby Creek Covered Bridge (photo: David Bassett)

contentHtml:
The Cottage Grove Covered Bridge Tour Route is a 20-mile loop through the Row River Valley, about 1 to 2 hours by car, in an area with the largest collection of covered bridges in the West. From I-5 exit 174, head east on Row River Road along the north shore of Dorena Lake, return west on Shoreview Drive and Garoutte Road, and follow Mosby Creek and Layng roads back into downtown Cottage Grove.

Stops include the two-tone Currin Bridge, the 1949 Dorena Bridge, the Stewart Bridge, the 1920 Mosby Creek Bridge (Lane County's oldest, still open to cars), the volunteer-built Centennial Bridge and the Chambers Bridge, believed to be the only covered railroad bridge left west of the Mississippi. Much of the drive follows the paved Row River Trail.
excerpt: The Cottage Grove Covered Bridge Tour Route is a 20-mile loop through the Row River Valley, about 1 to 2 hours by car, in an area with the largest collection of
note: Year-round. Most bridges welcome bikes and pedestrians; check which allow vehicles. Currin and Stewart bridges are currently closed and fenced off.
address: Start: I-5 exit 174, Cottage Grove, OR

title: McKenzie Pass-Santiam Pass Scenic Byway
imageAlt: Lava flow and peaks from Dee Wright Observatory

banner.alt: Lava flow and peaks from Dee Wright Observatory

contentHtml:
The McKenzie Pass-Santiam Pass Scenic Byway is an 82-mile loop from Sisters over two Cascade passes: Santiam Pass (4,817 feet), where the Pacific Crest Trail crosses, and McKenzie Pass (5,335 feet), crowned by the lava-rock Dee Wright Observatory with views over an ancient lava flow to 11 peaks.

Along the way are Suttle Lake, Scott Lake, Clear Lake Resort, the wild and scenic McKenzie River and historic stretches of the Santiam Wagon Road. Back in Sisters, browse downtown boutiques and galleries.
excerpt: The McKenzie Pass-Santiam Pass Scenic Byway is an 82-mile loop from Sisters over two Cascade passes: Santiam Pass (4,817 feet), where the Pacific Crest Trail cr
note: The McKenzie Pass section (OR 242) is closed to cars part of the year; check TripCheck.com before you go.
address: Loop from Sisters, OR, via US 20/OR 126 and OR 242

title: McKenzie River Scenic Byway
contentHtml:
The McKenzie River Scenic Byway is a 34-mile Oregon State Scenic Byway along OR 126 and the McKenzie River, from Springfield through the lower McKenzie Valley and quiet riverside communities to Rainbow, where it meets the West Cascades Scenic Byway.

Stops include Hendricks Bridge Park, the 1920s Leaburg-Walterville hydroelectric project on the National Register, the Old McKenzie Fish Hatchery with trails and signs on geology and the drift boat, the 1938 Goodpasture Covered Bridge near Vida, and Blue River Lake near Wolf Rock. The river is famed for fly-fishing.
excerpt: The McKenzie River Scenic Byway is a 34-mile Oregon State Scenic Byway along OR 126 and the McKenzie River, from Springfield through the lower McKenzie Valley a
address: OR 126 from Springfield to Rainbow, OR

title: Pacific Coast Scenic Byway

gallery.alt: Along the Pacific Coast Scenic Byway
Along the Pacific Coast Scenic Byway
Along the Pacific Coast Scenic Byway

contentHtml:
The Pacific Coast Scenic Byway, an All-American Road, follows US 101 for 363 miles along the whole Oregon coast, from Astoria at the Washington border to Brookings at the California border.

Highlights along the whole route include clamming on Tillamook Bay, kayaking Alsea Bay, the dramatic rocks and islands of the south coast and jet boat trips up the Rogue River at Gold Beach.

EV charging stations are spaced along the route, making an electric road trip from Astoria to Brookings possible.
excerpt: The Pacific Coast Scenic Byway, an All-American Road, follows US 101 for 363 miles along the whole Oregon coast, from Astoria at the Washington border to Brooki
address: US 101 from Astoria to Brookings, OR

title: West Cascades Scenic Byway

gallery.alt: Along the West Cascades Scenic Byway

contentHtml:
The West Cascades Scenic Byway is a 220-mile National Scenic Byway along the northern half of Oregon's Cascade Range, from Estacada, about 25 miles from Portland, south to Westfir near Oakridge.

From Estacada it follows the Clackamas River on OR-224 and Forest Road 46 to Detroit Lake, then the McKenzie River past Clear Lake and 100-foot Sahalie Falls, ending on the Aufderheide road (Forest Road 19) at the Office Covered Bridge, Oregon's longest at 180 feet.

Along the way are old-growth groves such as the Delta Old Growth Trail, three National Recreation Trails, Olallie Lakes and the PGE powerhouse at Estacada. The full drive takes 7 to 9 hours, or sections can be driven on their own.
excerpt: The West Cascades Scenic Byway is a 220-mile National Scenic Byway along the northern half of Oregon's Cascade Range, from Estacada, about 25 miles from Portlan
note: Forest Roads 19 and 46 are generally closed November 15 to April 30 because of snow.
address: Estacada (OR-224) to Westfir near Oakridge (OR-58), via Forest Road 46, Detroit, OR-22, OR-126 and Forest Road 19

title: Central Coast Food Trail
imageAlt: River Roasters Coffee in Historic Old Town Florence (courtesy of Eugene, Cascades & Coast)

banner.alt: River Roasters Coffee in Historic Old Town Florence (courtesy of Eugene, Cascades & Coast)

contentHtml:
The Central Coast Food Trail is a self-guided, year-round route of 35 stops along Oregon's central coast: seafood, farms, bakeries, breweries, distilleries and wineries from Lincoln City through Gleneden Beach, Depoe Bay, Otter Rock, Newport, Toledo, Siletz, Waldport and Yachats to Florence in Lane County.

Florence stops include River Roasters coffee, Homegrown Public House (local brews and a dog menu), Nosh Eatery and the pirate-themed Stillwagon Distillery.

note: Email: ddcentral@thepeoplescoast.com. Trail site: ccfoodtrail.com
address: Lincoln City to Florence along the central Oregon coast

title: South Willamette Valley Food Trail
imageAlt: Barrel-aged beer and charcuterie at Alesong Brewing & Blending

banner.alt: Barrel-aged beer and charcuterie at Alesong Brewing & Blending

gallery.alt: Mountain bikers at the Office Bridge in Westfir

contentHtml:
The South Willamette Valley Food Trail is a self-guided journey of 53 stops through Oregon's agricultural heartland: bakeries, restaurants, farms, growers markets, breweries, wineries and food-focused lodges.

It centers on Eugene and Springfield and reaches Veneta, Junction City, Coburg, Creswell, Cottage Grove, the McKenzie River and Oakridge, with stops across the county line in Monroe and Harrisburg.

Highlights include King Estate Winery, North America's largest Demeter-certified Biodynamic vineyard, Alesong Brewing & Blending, the Lane County Farmers Market and seasonal berry, lavender, apple and truffle harvests.
excerpt: The South Willamette Valley Food Trail is a self-guided journey of 53 stops through Oregon's agricultural heartland: bakeries, restaurants, farms, growers marke
note: 53 stops; self-guided, no set mileage
address: Eugene, Springfield and surrounding towns. Mapped at King Estate Winery, 80854 Territorial Hwy, Eugene

title: Belknap Covered Bridge
imageAlt: Inside Belknap Covered Bridge (photo: Traci Williamson)

banner.alt: Inside Belknap Covered Bridge (photo: Traci Williamson)

contentHtml:
Built in 1966 after a 1964 flood washed out the bridge before it, the 120-foot Howe truss Belknap Covered Bridge crosses the McKenzie River near Rainbow. It is the fourth covered bridge on a site used since 1890, the most recently built historic covered bridge in Lane County and the farthest east of Oregon's covered bridges.

It is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and remains open to traffic.
excerpt: Built in 1966 after a 1964 flood washed out the bridge before it, the 120-foot Howe truss Belknap Covered Bridge crosses the McKenzie River near Rainbow. It is
note: Vehicles up to 11 tons; maximum height 13'1".
address: McKenzie River, one mile west of McKenzie Bridge off OR 126, near Rainbow, OR

title: Centennial Covered Bridge
contentHtml:
Built in 1987, mostly by volunteers, to mark Cottage Grove's 100th birthday, the 84-foot Howe truss Centennial Covered Bridge crosses the Coast Fork Willamette River downtown. It is a 3/8-scale model of the nearby Chambers Covered Bridge, built from timbers of the dismantled Meadows and Brumbaugh bridges.

A time capsule of 1980s items was placed in the entrance at its dedication. It is open to pedestrians and bicycles only.
excerpt: Built in 1987, mostly by volunteers, to mark Cottage Grove's 100th birthday, the 84-foot Howe truss Centennial Covered Bridge crosses the Coast Fork Willamette
note: Pedestrians and bicycles only.
address: Main St, next to City Hall, downtown Cottage Grove, OR 97424

title: Chambers Covered Railroad Bridge
imageAlt: Chambers Railroad Covered Bridge (photo: Joni Kabana)

banner.alt: Chambers Railroad Covered Bridge (photo: Joni Kabana)

gallery.alt: Chambers Railroad Covered Bridge (photo: Natalie Inouye)

contentHtml:
Built in 1925 by lumberman J.E. Chambers to carry lumber trains from the Lorane Valley to a Cottage Grove mill, the 78-foot Howe truss Chambers Covered Railroad Bridge crosses the Coast Fork Willamette River. It is the only remaining covered railroad bridge west of the Mississippi River.

Dismantled and rebuilt on site after storm damage and restored in 2011, it is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and now serves as a footbridge and interpretive site for pedestrians and cyclists.
excerpt: Built in 1925 by lumberman J.E. Chambers to carry lumber trains from the Lorane Valley to a Cottage Grove mill, the 78-foot Howe truss Chambers Covered Railroad
note: Pedestrians and bicycles only.
address: S River Rd, Cottage Grove, OR (parking at the southeast end of the bridge)

title: Coyote Creek Covered Bridge
contentHtml:
Built in 1922, the 60-foot Howe truss Coyote Creek Covered Bridge carries Battle Creek Road over Coyote Creek near Crow, on the old Territorial Highway route. It is also called the Battle Creek Bridge or Swing Long Bridge, and has housed buttresses, ribbon openings under the eaves and rectangular portals.

It is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and remains open to light traffic.
excerpt: Built in 1922, the 60-foot Howe truss Coyote Creek Covered Bridge carries Battle Creek Road over Coyote Creek near Crow, on the old Territorial Highway route. I
address: Battle Creek Road, just off Territorial Highway, near Crow / Veneta, OR 97487

title: Currin Covered Bridge
contentHtml:
Built in 1925 by Lane County crews to replace an 1883 bridge, the 105-foot Howe truss Currin Covered Bridge crosses the Row River. It is Oregon's only covered bridge painted two colors, with white portals and red sides.

It is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
excerpt: Built in 1925 by Lane County crews to replace an 1883 bridge, the 105-foot Howe truss Currin Covered Bridge crosses the Row River. It is Oregon's only covered b
note: Currently closed and fenced off to all access due to unsafe conditions (spring 2026); repair funding is being sought.
address: Row River at Layng Road, east of Cottage Grove, OR

title: Deadwood Covered Bridge
contentHtml:
Built in 1932, the 105-foot Howe truss Deadwood Covered Bridge crosses Deadwood Creek on a curve of Deadwood Loop Road, its floorboards deliberately slanted to help drivers enter safely. It is one of three Coast Range covered bridges, with Lake Creek and Wildcat Creek.

Bypassed in the 1970s and restored by Lane County in 1986, it is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and is open to traffic.

note: Vehicles up to 10 tons; maximum height 10'7".
address: Deadwood Loop Road, near Swisshome, OR

title: Dorena Covered Bridge
imageAlt: Scenic drive by Dorena Covered Bridge (photo: Melanie Griffin)

banner.alt: Scenic drive by Dorena Covered Bridge (photo: Melanie Griffin)

contentHtml:
Built in 1949 after Dorena Dam created Dorena Reservoir, the 105-foot Howe truss Dorena Covered Bridge crosses the Row River at the upper end of the lake. Also called the Star Bridge, it once gave access to the Star Ranch.

Listed on the National Register of Historic Places and rehabilitated in 1996, it is closed to traffic and is now a wayside park with restrooms and swimming-hole access, popular for weddings and events.
excerpt: Built in 1949 after Dorena Dam created Dorena Reservoir, the 105-foot Howe truss Dorena Covered Bridge crosses the Row River at the upper end of the lake. Also
note: Pedestrians only.
address: Government Road at Row River Road, upper end of Dorena Reservoir, east of Cottage Grove, OR

title: Earnest Covered Bridge

gallery.alt: Earnest Covered Bridge over the Mohawk River (photo: Debbie Williamson-Smith)

contentHtml:
Built in 1938, the 75-foot Howe truss Earnest Covered Bridge crosses the Mohawk River near Marcola, replacing the 1903 Adams Bridge. This white bridge, also called the Mohawk River Bridge, appeared in the 1965 film Shenandoah and was restored by the film company after filming.

Listed on the National Register of Historic Places, it is a popular picnic spot for day-trippers and plein air painters and is open to traffic.

title: Goodpasture Covered Bridge
imageAlt: Goodpasture Covered Bridge over the McKenzie River

banner.alt: Goodpasture Covered Bridge over the McKenzie River

contentHtml:
Built in 1938, the 165-foot Howe truss Goodpasture Covered Bridge crosses the McKenzie River near Vida. Gothic-style windows line both sides, and it is Oregon's second-longest covered bridge and one of its most photographed.

Lane County repaired and strengthened it in 1987 to carry log trucks. It is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and remains open to traffic.

title: Lake Creek Covered Bridge
imageAlt: Lake Creek Covered Bridge (photo: Jamie Hooper)

banner.alt: Lake Creek Covered Bridge (photo: Jamie Hooper)

gallery.alt: Lake Creek Covered Bridge (photo: Jennifer Archer)

contentHtml:
Built in 1928, the 105-foot Howe truss Lake Creek Covered Bridge, also called the Nelson Mountain Bridge, crosses Lake Creek on Nelson Mountain Road near Greenleaf, on the way to Triangle Lake. Nearby Lake Creek has natural rock slides and small waterfalls.

Renovated in 1984, it is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and is open to traffic.

title: Lowell Covered Bridge
imageAlt: Lowell Covered Bridge over the Middle Fork Willamette River

banner.alt: Lowell Covered Bridge over the Middle Fork Willamette River

contentHtml:
Built in 1945 to replace a 1907 bridge, the 165-foot Howe truss Lowell Covered Bridge crosses Dexter Lake on the Middle Fork Willamette River and is the widest covered bridge in Oregon. It was raised six feet in 1953 ahead of the flooding from Dexter Dam.

Bypassed by a concrete span in 1981, it is listed on the National Register of Historic Places, closed to vehicles, and now serves as a covered-bridge interpretive center.

note: Closed to vehicles.

title: Mosby Creek Covered Bridge
imageAlt: Mosby Creek Covered Bridge (photo: Natalie Inouye)

banner.alt: Mosby Creek Covered Bridge (photo: Natalie Inouye)

gallery.alt: Mosby Creek Covered Bridge (photo: Natalie Inouye)

contentHtml:
Built in 1920 for $4,125, the 90-foot Howe truss Mosby Creek Covered Bridge crosses Mosby Creek on Layng Road east of Cottage Grove. Named for 1853 pioneer David Mosby and also called the Layng Bridge, it is Lane County's oldest covered bridge.

It sits beside the main Row River Trail trailhead, near the railroad bridge from the opening of Stand by Me. It is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and its single lane remains open to traffic.

title: Office Covered Bridge
imageAlt: The Office Covered Bridge over the North Fork of the Middle Fork Willamette River

banner.alt: The Office Covered Bridge over the North Fork of the Middle Fork Willamette River

contentHtml:
Built in 1944 by the Westfir Lumber Company to carry log trucks between its mill and the mill office, the 180- foot Office Covered Bridge crosses the North Fork of the Middle Fork Willamette River at Westfir. It is the longest covered bridge in Oregon.

Its triple Howe truss and separate covered pedestrian walkway are unique in the state. Lane County acquired and stabilized it in 1992, and it is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

title: Parvin Covered Bridge
contentHtml:
Built in 1921, the white, single-lane 75-foot Howe truss Parvin Covered Bridge crosses Lost Creek near Dexter, replacing an earlier bridge condemned for worm damage. It is also called the Lost Creek Bridge.

It is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and, after a period as a pedestrian-only bypass, was reopened to traffic in 1986.

title: Pengra Covered Bridge
contentHtml:
Built in 1938, the 120-foot Howe truss Pengra Covered Bridge carries Place Road over Fall Creek near Jasper. Its lower chords are single timbers 16 by 18 inches and 126 feet long, cut by Booth-Kelly Lumber Company loggers: some of the longest single timbers used in an Oregon bridge.

Named for pioneer B. J. Pengra, Oregon's surveyor general from 1862, it was closed in 1979 and reopened to traffic in 1995. It is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

title: Stewart Covered Bridge
contentHtml:
Built in 1930, the 60-foot Howe truss Stewart Covered Bridge crosses Mosby Creek at Garoutte Road near Cottage Grove, above a popular swimming hole. Damaged by floods and snow over the years, it is a stop for cyclists on the Row River Trail.

It is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

title: Unity Covered Bridge
contentHtml:
Built in 1936, the 90-foot Howe truss Unity Covered Bridge, also called the Fall Creek Bridge, crosses Fall Creek at Unity near Lowell. A full-length window on its east side lets drivers see oncoming traffic at the intersection and gives views of the creek, making it popular with photographers and cyclists.

Renovated in 1986 and re-roofed in 2014, it is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and is open to traffic.

title: Wendling Covered Bridge
imageAlt: A white covered bridge road in the fall (photo: Sally McAleer)

banner.alt: A white covered bridge road in the fall (photo: Sally McAleer)

contentHtml:
Built in 1938 for $2,241, the 60-foot Howe truss Wendling Covered Bridge crosses Mill Creek on Wendling Road northeast of Marcola. It is one of four Lane County covered bridges built that year, with Pengra, Goodpasture and Earnest, and the cross planking on its approaches rumbles as cars cross.

It is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and is open to traffic.

title: Wildcat Creek Covered Bridge
imageAlt: Wildcat Creek Covered Bridge (photo: Gregory Burns)

banner.alt: Wildcat Creek Covered Bridge (photo: Gregory Burns)

gallery.alt: Wildcat Creek Covered Bridge (photo: Natalie Inouye)

contentHtml:
Built in 1925 on the old Stagecoach Road to the coast, the 75-foot Howe truss Wildcat Creek Covered Bridge, also called the Austa Bridge, crosses Wildcat Creek near its confluence with the Siuslaw River west of Walton. The Austa boat ramp nearby gives access to the river and a riverside picnic spot.

It is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and is open to traffic.

title: Heceta Head Lighthouse
imageAlt: Lighthouse on the cliff above the rocky shore

banner.alt: Lighthouse on the cliff above the rocky shore

gallery.alt: The lighthouse on a foggy cliff above the ocean

contentHtml:
First lit in 1894, Heceta Head Lighthouse's 56-foot tower stands 205 feet above the Pacific on a seabird- nesting headland and throws the strongest beam on the Oregon coast, visible 21 miles out. It is one of the most photographed lighthouses on the coast.

A half-mile trail climbs about 150 feet from the parking area to the lighthouse; the ground floor is open to visitors without reservations. The 1893 assistant keeper's house is now a bed and breakfast, and the park has a sheltered beach, part of the Oregon Coast Trail, and winter and spring whale watching.

title: Gold Lake Road
contentHtml:
Gold Lake Sno-Park is the highest of the three Willamette Pass sno-parks, with a small network of cross- country ski loops. Across the highway, Gold Lake Road leads to more ski trails and the Gold Lake snow shelter.

A warming cabin doubles as the base for the Willamette Backcountry Ski Patrol, and the three-sided Westview and Bechtel ski shelters have wood stoves and sleeping lofts. Skilled backcountry skiers can tour about 4 miles north on the Pacific Crest Trail to the enclosed Maiden Peak Shelter, free to the public.

Across the highway, Fuji Creek Road climbs about 3 miles to the challenging Island and Birthday Lakes ski trails and the three-sided Fuji Shelter, with a wood stove and an overnight loft.

imageAlt: Public skate at The Rink Exchange

banner.alt: Public skate at The Rink Exchange

contentHtml:
The Rink Exchange, at the Lane Events Center in Eugene, is Lane County's only ice arena. It offers public skate sessions all season, freestyle ice, learn-to-skate lessons, youth and adult hockey, birthday parties and private ice rentals.

The Road Trip Cafe serves skaters, and the Pro Shop sharpens skates.

title: Belknap Hot Springs
contentHtml:
Belknap Hot Springs is a developed resort on the McKenzie River, open 365 days a year, with two mineral hot spring pools, acres of gardens including the Secret Garden, and lodge rooms, cabins, RV and tent sites.

The pools are fed by a source of about 196 degrees F across the river and are held around 92 degrees F in summer and 102 degrees F in cooler months. The lower pool is open to walk-in day use; overnight guests can soak 9:00 AM to 9:00 PM.

imageAlt: A fall soak at Bigelow Hot Springs

banner.alt: A fall soak at Bigelow Hot Springs

contentHtml:
Bigelow Hot Springs, also called Deer Creek Hot Springs, is a small natural rock-ring pool (about 8 by 13 feet and 1 to 2 feet deep) for 2 to 4 people, in a fern grotto on the bank of the McKenzie River.

The spring emerges at about 104 degrees F, and the pool runs 102 to 104 degrees F in summer and fall. From the bridge on Forest Road 2654, walk down to the river; the pool is on the downstream side, opposite the parking.

title: McCredie Hot Springs
contentHtml:
McCredie Hot Springs are natural, unimproved pools on both banks of Salt Creek, reached by an easy trail from the McCredie Day Use Area. The source emerges at 163 degrees F and mixes with creek water in 2 to 4 shallow pools that run about 98 to 114 degrees F; soakers move rocks to adjust the temperature.

The pools across the creek tend to be less crowded. Clothing-optional use is commonly reported.

Vault toilets are at the parking lot and composting restrooms near the springs, with drinking water and bottled water for sale.

contentHtml:
Wall Creek Warm Springs, also called the Meditation Pool, is a single natural creekside pool at the end of the level Warm Springs Trail #3582, which follows Wall Creek through old-growth forest about half a mile from the trailhead.

The oval pool is about 10 by 12 feet and 3 feet deep, with a silt bottom. It is warm rather than hot, about 95 degrees F, varying with the flow from the bottom of the pool.

title: Office Covered Bridge
imageAlt: The Office Covered Bridge viewed from Portal Park

banner.alt: The Office Covered Bridge viewed from Portal Park

contentHtml:
At 180 feet, the Office Covered Bridge in Westfir is the longest covered bridge in Oregon and the only covered bridge west of the Mississippi with a separate covered pedestrian walkway. Built in 1944 by the Westfir Lumber Company to link its mill with its main office, it uses a triple Howe truss, and it still carries traffic at the south end of the Aufderheide Scenic Byway.

A 1979 fire destroyed the mill but spared the bridge and the office, which is now Westfir Lodge. Portal Park at the bridge's north end hosts the annual Bridge Lighting Festival.

title: Sea Lion Caves

gallery.alt: Sea lions at Sea Lion Caves

contentHtml:
Sea Lion Caves, open since 1932, is America's largest sea cave and the only known mainland Steller sea lion rookery in the continental United States. An elevator drops visitors 208 feet into the basalt cavern, more than 12 stories high and about as wide as a football field, where wild sea lions haul out year-round.

The privately owned wildlife preserve and bird sanctuary also has an observation deck over the coast.

title: Indian Ridge Lookout

gallery.alt: Two twin beds inside the lookout
View east to the Three Sisters and Mount Jefferson

contentHtml:
Indian Ridge Lookout is a cab on a 30-foot tower at 5,405 feet, built in 1958 and used for fire detection until 1973; it is still staffed occasionally in emergencies. It is named for the old Indian hunting trail along the summit.

The Three Sisters stand close to the northeast, Hidden Lake lies below the north edge of the mountaintop with a short trail down to it, and the open ridge is covered in beargrass and huckleberries. The 16 by 16-foot cab sleeps 4 in two twin beds.

title: Timber Butte Replica Lookout

gallery.alt: View from the Timber Butte porch

contentHtml:
Timber Butte is a faithful replica of a 1930s L-4 gabled lookout cabin at 3,650 feet, built in 2005 by volunteers with a $10,000 Lane County grant. The 14 by 14-foot ground cabin is ringed by a catwalk and reached by a ramp, a 300-foot walk uphill from parking.

It sleeps 4, with a propane heater, a propane cooktop on the deck and cookware. Fall Creek's swimming holes and trails are below, and Lane County's covered bridges make the drive a tour of its own.

title: Warner Mountain Lookout
imageAlt: Warner Mountain Lookout in the snow

banner.alt: Warner Mountain Lookout in the snow

contentHtml:
Warner Mountain Lookout is a rarity: a cupola-style cab, a design normally set on the ground, perched on a 41-foot tower at about 5,300 feet. It was built in the 1980s from materials salvaged from the Grass Mountain Lookout, and the road sign calls the place Warner Ridge.

It is staffed in summer and rented in winter only. Guests ski, snowshoe or snowmobile 2 to 10 miles depending on the snow line, melt snow for water and enjoy panoramic views and starry skies. It sleeps 4, with propane heat and cooking.

contentHtml: The Tracktown marker celebrates Eugene's running films, Tracktown (2016), Without Limits and Personal Best, shot in and around the city's storied Hayward Field. Tracktown was made by University of Oregon runner Alexi Pappas, who also stars as an Olympic-bound runner sidelined by injury.
excerpt: The Tracktown marker celebrates Eugene's running films, Tracktown (2016), Without Limits and Personal Best, shot in and around the city's storied Hayward Field.

contentHtml: Eugene's Without Limits marker honors the 1998 film of the Steve Prefontaine story, with Billy Crudup as Pre and Donald Sutherland as coach Bill Bowerman. It was filmed at Hayward Field and across the area, including Heceta Beach and Bowerman's home.

Just upstream from this Oregon Film Trail marker, the four boys dodge a train on the railroad trestle in Stand by Me's (1986) famous scene. Most of the film was shot in Brownsville, about 45 minutes north.

The opening shots of Lost in the Stars (1974) were filmed just south of the marker. The Currin Covered Bridge is nearby.

contentHtml: Around the bend from this Oregon Film Trail marker, the four boys share their campfire scene in Stand by Me (1986), about two-tenths of a mile northwest along the old rail line. Dorena Lake also backdrops the opening scenes of Emperor of the North (1973).

gallery.alt: The marker, looking southeast toward Row River Road

contentHtml: Just southeast of this Oregon Film Trail marker, Buster Keaton crashed a real locomotive off a burning trestle for the climax of The General (1926), at $45,000 the most expensive single shot of the silent era. Vintage trains from the Oregon, Pacific and Eastern Railway and nearby sawmills were used in the film.

title: Alesong Brewing & Blending
imageAlt: Pomegranate salad and a tasting flight

banner.alt: Pomegranate salad and a tasting flight

contentHtml:
Alesong Brewing & Blending is an intentionally small brewery, winery and cidery in the hills southwest of Eugene, focused on oak aging. It is known for barrel-aged wild and sour ales and was a medalist at the 2026 Great American Beer Festival.

The tasting room has a from-scratch kitchen, non-alcoholic drinks and patio views.

note: Last call for hot food 6:30 PM.

title: Chiefs Brewhouse
contentHtml:
Chiefs Brew House is a Native-owned restaurant and farm brewery that has served classic American comfort food and BBQ in Coburg since 2010. Its beers are brewed on site, including the Chiefs Grass Seed Lager, made with grass seed grown on the owners' land.

In June and July, farm events on Friday and Saturday evenings bring live music and barbecue dinners to the farm brewery.
excerpt: Chiefs Brew House is a Native-owned restaurant and farm brewery that has served classic American comfort food and BBQ in Coburg since 2010. Its beers are brewed
note: Farm brewery: 32817 Coleman Rd, Eugene. Email: info@chiefsbrewhouse.com
address: 91108 N Willamette Street, Coburg, OR 97408

title: Claim 52 Brewing
contentHtml:
Claim 52 Brewing, founded in 2012, is known for hazy IPAs and its Thicc and Stuffed fruited-sour series. Under owner Jeremiah Marsden since 2024, it consolidated at its expanded Lincoln Street taproom in May 2025 and added a Newport Bayfront taproom in 2026.

The Eugene taproom pours beer, wine, cider, seltzer, cocktails and non-alcoholic drinks with food from partner Seasoned, and hosts trivia and themed nights.
excerpt: Claim 52 Brewing, founded in 2012, is known for hazy IPAs and its Thicc and Stuffed fruited-sour series. Under owner Jeremiah Marsden since 2024, it consolidate
note: Email: eugene@claim52brewing.com
address: 232 Lincoln St, Eugene, OR 97401

title: Coast Fork Brewing
contentHtml:
Coast Fork Brewing + Provisions is a family-owned brewery and farm-supply store in historic downtown Cottage Grove. The public house pours its own beers, local ciders, spirits and mocktails with kitchen food made from local ingredients, and fills crowlers to go.

Next door, Provisions sells animal and pet feed, housewares, garden goods and fermentation supplies. Trivia, acoustic nights and live local music run weekly.
excerpt: Coast Fork Brewing + Provisions is a family-owned brewery and farm-supply store in historic downtown Cottage Grove. The public house pours its own beers, local
note: Provisions feed store: Wednesday - Sunday, 10:30 AM - 5:30 PM.
address: 106 S 6th St, Cottage Grove, OR 97424 (just off Main St)

title: ColdFire
contentHtml:
ColdFire Brewing was founded in 2016 by brothers Dan and Stephen Hughes, brewing small batches rooted in European traditions: classic lagers, Northwest IPAs and cellared beers.

Its public house in the heart of Eugene, opened in November 2025, serves the beers with wood-fired food. The Barrel House at 263 Mill Street opens for special events, and production is in Junction City.
excerpt: ColdFire Brewing was founded in 2016 by brothers Dan and Stephen Hughes, brewing small batches rooted in European traditions: classic lagers, Northwest IPAs and
address: ColdFire Public House, 260 Ferry Street, Eugene, OR 97401

title: Drop Bear Brewery
contentHtml:
Drop Bear Brewery is an Australian-themed brewery and restaurant on south Willamette Street, owned by Australian-born Lorraine and David Lehane. It pours Aussie-inspired beers, plus limited "X Factor" taps of wild-yeast and mixed-fermentation styles.

The kitchen serves pizza with vegan options, and there are trivia nights, live music, private parties and a mobile beer garden.
excerpt: Drop Bear Brewery is an Australian-themed brewery and restaurant on south Willamette Street, owned by Australian-born Lorraine and David Lehane. It pours Aussie
note: Email: greatbeer@dropbearbrewery.com
address: 2690 Willamette Street, Eugene, OR 97405

title: Falling Sky
contentHtml:
Falling Sky Brewing is a downtown Eugene brewpub, opened in 2012 on Oak Alley, where "we brew, make, cure and bake everything in house." It was a medalist at the 2026 Great American Beer Festival.

Falling Sky also runs the Pour House Delicatessen at 790 Blair Blvd and a pizzeria at the University of Oregon.
excerpt: Falling Sky Brewing is a downtown Eugene brewpub, opened in 2012 on Oak Alley, where "we brew, make, cure and bake everything in house." It was a medalist at th
note: All-day happy hour on Mondays.
address: 1334 Oak Alley, Eugene, OR

title: Gratitude Brewing
contentHtml:
Gratitude Brewing opened in late December 2019 in the former Sam Bond's Brewing space. It closed temporarily in May 2023 and reopened that fall in partnership with Tradewinds Catering.

It brews its own craft beers, offers non-alcoholic options and serves food from a scratch kitchen; its beers also pour at local restaurants and tap houses.
excerpt: Gratitude Brewing opened in late December 2019 in the former Sam Bond's Brewing space. It closed temporarily in May 2023 and reopened that fall in partnership w
note: Email: info@gratitudebrewing.com
address: 540 E 8th Ave, Suite A, Eugene, OR 97401

title: Homegrown Public House & Brewery
imageAlt: Fish tacos and burger from Homegrown in Florence

banner.alt: Fish tacos and burger from Homegrown in Florence

contentHtml:
Homegrown Public House & Brewery is a licensed nano-brewery gastropub in Florence's Historic Old Town, serving salads, flatbreads, sandwiches and seafood with beers brewed in house.

It is a stop on the Central Coast Food Trail.
excerpt: Homegrown Public House & Brewery is a licensed nano-brewery gastropub in Florence's Historic Old Town, serving salads, flatbreads, sandwiches and seafood with b
address: 294 Laurel St, Florence, OR 97439 (Historic Old Town)

title: Hop Valley Brewing
contentHtml:
Hop Valley Brewing was founded in 2009 in Springfield, on land once central to hop growing. The Springfield brewery and restaurant serves beer brewed on site for lunch and dinner, with a pet-friendly patio.

Owner Tilray closed the Eugene production brewery in July 2025, and a new Eugene pub opened in September 2026 at 550 Pearl Street, Unit 150, in the 5th Street Market Alley (541-485-2337, open daily 12:00 - 9:00 PM).
excerpt: Hop Valley Brewing was founded in 2009 in Springfield, on land once central to hop growing. The Springfield brewery and restaurant serves beer brewed on site fo
note: Call the Springfield pub for hours.
address: Springfield pub: 980 Kruse Way, Springfield, OR 97477

title: McKenzie Brewing
contentHtml:
McKenzie Brewing traces its roots to Steelhead Brewing, Eugene's first brewpub, opened in 1991. It brews in small batches with water from the McKenzie River.

Urban Restaurant Group bought it in 2024: the brewpub became Kennedy's Steakhouse, and McKenzie's tasting room reopened beside it in the 5th Street Public Market, still brewing on site. All ages are welcome.
excerpt: McKenzie Brewing traces its roots to Steelhead Brewing, Eugene's first brewpub, opened in 1991. It brews in small batches with water from the McKenzie River.
note: Email: marketing@mckenziebrewing.com. Other days not listed; check the website.
address: 590 Pearl St, Suite 107, Eugene, OR 97401 (5th Street Public Market)

title: Ninkasi Brewing
contentHtml:
Ninkasi Brewing was founded in 2006 by Jamie Floyd and Nikos Ridge, whose first batch was Total Domination IPA, and is among Oregon's largest independent craft breweries.

Its Whiteaker campus has the Better Living Room tasting room and restaurant, with craft beer, cocktails, food, live music and private events. Headquarters and dock sales are at 155 Blair Blvd.
excerpt: Ninkasi Brewing was founded in 2006 by Jamie Floyd and Nikos Ridge, whose first batch was Total Domination IPA, and is among Oregon's largest independent craft
address: Tasting room: 272 Van Buren St, Eugene, OR 97402

title: Plank Town
contentHtml:
Plank Town Brewing Co. is a brewpub established in 2013 in Springfield's restored Odd Fellows building at the corner of 4th and Main in the historic downtown.

It pours handcrafted beers from 20 taps plus two cask beer engines, with a Northwest-inspired menu.
excerpt: Plank Town Brewing Co. is a brewpub established in 2013 in Springfield's restored Odd Fellows building at the corner of 4th and Main in the historic downtown.
address: 346 Main Street, Springfield, OR

title: The Wheel Apizza Pub and Brewery
contentHtml:
The Wheel Apizza Pub is a New Haven-style apizza pub and brewery at the foot of Skinner Butte, with naturally leavened dough and produce, grain, meat and hops from Oregon farms.

All of its Pacific Northwest beers are brewed in house by founding brewer Tobias Schock with Oregon-grown ingredients.
excerpt: The Wheel Apizza Pub is a New Haven-style apizza pub and brewery at the foot of Skinner Butte, with naturally leavened dough and produce, grain, meat and hops f
address: 390 Lincoln Street, Eugene, OR 97401

title: Viking Brewing
contentHtml:
Viking Brewing has made Viking-inspired honey ales since 2013, specializing in braggot, a beer-and-mead style, as the Viking Braggot Co. Honey makes up about 15 to 30% of the fermentable sugar, shaping the flavor of its blonde, red, IPA and stout.

Its Southtowne Pub closed in June 2025, but the original brewery and taproom in a west Eugene industrial park remain open, with a patio beer garden, live music and pub food from the Viking food truck.
excerpt: Viking Brewing has made Viking-inspired honey ales since 2013, specializing in braggot, a beer-and-mead style, as the Viking Braggot Co. Honey makes up about 15
address: Westside Brewery Taproom, Commercial St, west Eugene, OR

title: Apona Vineyards
contentHtml:
Apona Vineyards is a winery and estate tasting room in Veneta in the southern Willamette Valley, with 32 acres of LIVE-certified vines on a 100-acre farm with a horse barn and equine heritage.

Tastings last 90 minutes, with flights from $25 to $40, wines by the glass and light bites such as charcuterie, cheese boards and baked brie.
excerpt: Apona Vineyards is a winery and estate tasting room in Veneta in the southern Willamette Valley, with 32 acres of LIVE-certified vines on a 100-acre farm with a
note: Reservations recommended; groups of 9 to 10 need a large-group tasting. Leashed dogs welcome outside. No outside food or drink. Email: info@aponavineyards.com
address: 25443 Fleck Rd, Veneta, OR

title: Bradshaw Vineyards
contentHtml:
Bradshaw Vineyard is a family vineyard in the Lower Long Tom AVA near Junction City, established by the Bradshaw family in 1989 to grow high-quality Pinot Noir. It sits at about 400 feet on Bellpine soil.

A King Estate partner since the winery's early days, it grows six Pinot Noir clones on a variety of rootstocks; its foundation block came from the King Estate nursery.
excerpt: Bradshaw Vineyard is a family vineyard in the Lower Long Tom AVA near Junction City, established by the Bradshaw family in 1989 to grow high-quality Pinot Noir.
note: Vineyard only; no public tasting room.
address: Ferguson Road area, Junction City, OR (Lower Long Tom AVA)

title: Brigadoon Vineyards
imageAlt: A glass of Pinot over the vineyard

banner.alt: A glass of Pinot over the vineyard

contentHtml:
Brigadoon Wine Company is a family farm winery in the Lower Long Tom AVA, a father-son partnership of the Shown family committed to organic agriculture.

The tasting room overlooks a canyon and the vineyard, with picnic terraces. Bring a picnic or buy a cheese and charcuterie board.
excerpt: Brigadoon Wine Company is a family farm winery in the Lower Long Tom AVA, a father-son partnership of the Shown family committed to organic agriculture.
note: Also by appointment. December - March: open Friday - Sunday only.
address: 25167 Ferguson Rd, Junction City, OR 97448

title: King Estate Winery
contentHtml:
King Estate Winery, founded in 1991 by the King family at the southern tip of the Willamette Valley, is a 1,033-acre estate and the largest certified Biodynamic vineyard in North America.

The tasting room serves wine tastings on Mondays and wine with food Wednesday through Sunday.
excerpt: King Estate Winery, founded in 1991 by the King family at the southern tip of the Willamette Valley, is a 1,033-acre estate and the largest certified Biodynamic
note: By reservation only (Tock); walk-ins may wait up to an hour. Reservations last two hours; 20% service charge for parties of 5 or more. No pets. Tours not currently offered.
address: 80854 Territorial Highway, Eugene, OR 97405

title: LaVelle Vineyards
contentHtml:
LaVelle Vineyards, founded in 1994, is a family-owned boutique winery near Elmira, with a 16-acre estate vineyard on a 25-acre property. It specializes in estate Pinot Noir, Pinot Gris, Riesling and Gamay Noir.

The old-world tasting room looks over the vines, and outside are fire pits and a Japanese-inspired Canopy Garden of native Oregon plants.
excerpt: LaVelle Vineyards, founded in 1994, is a family-owned boutique winery near Elmira, with a 16-acre estate vineyard on a 25-acre property. It specializes in estat
note: No reservations needed; parties of 6 or more call ahead. Leashed pets welcome. Email: sherry@lavellevineyards.com
address: Elmira, west of Eugene, OR

title: Saginaw
contentHtml:
Saginaw Vineyard is the Byler family's winery at the southern end of the Willamette Valley, with about 10 acres of Pinot Noir, Pinot Gris and other grapes and production under 2,000 cases.

Its tasting room, opened in 2001, is in a 1901/1905 farmstead barn, with live music on Fridays and Sunday brunch. The family also runs a wine bar at 926 E Main St in downtown Cottage Grove.
excerpt: Saginaw Vineyard is the Byler family's winery at the southern end of the Willamette Valley, with about 10 acres of Pinot Noir, Pinot Gris and other grapes and p
note: Email: club@saginawvineyard.com
address: 80247 Delight Valley School Rd, Saginaw (Cottage Grove), OR 97424

title: Sarver Winery, LLC
contentHtml:
Sarver Winery sits in the hills west of Eugene, about 30 minutes from town, with a 35-acre vineyard of more than 20,000 vines first planted in 1984.

The tasting room pours estate-grown wines with cheeses, salamis and fresh-baked bread, inside or on the patio, with a valley view that "goes on forever."
excerpt: Sarver Winery sits in the hills west of Eugene, about 30 minutes from town, with a 35-acre vineyard of more than 20,000 vines first planted in 1984.
address: 25600 Mayola Lane, Eugene, OR 97402

title: Walnut Ridge Vineyard
contentHtml:
Walnut Ridge Vineyard is a family winery a few miles west of Junction City in the Lower Long Tom AVA, with 30 acres of southwest-facing vines in the Coast Range foothills.

It makes small-batch, estate-grown wines, poured in the estate tasting room, and runs wine clubs called "Krewes."
excerpt: Walnut Ridge Vineyard is a family winery a few miles west of Junction City in the Lower Long Tom AVA, with 30 acres of southwest-facing vines in the Coast Range
note: Reserve on Tock. Texts preferred. Email: info@walnutridgevineyard.com
address: 94739 Turnbow Ln, Junction City, OR 97448

title: Alton Baker Park
imageAlt: Oregon Disc Golf Course at Alton Baker

banner.alt: Oregon Disc Golf Course at Alton Baker

contentHtml:
The Oregon Disc Golf Course at Alton Baker Park, established in 2013, is a flat, moderate 18-hole course; the PDGA Red layout runs 4,742 feet at par 55. A round takes about an hour and a half.

Tees mix pavers, turf, rubber mat, wood chips, grass and dirt, with Prodigy T2, Gravity, Mach III and El Guapo baskets. Restrooms and drinking water are available, and dogs are allowed.
excerpt: The Oregon Disc Golf Course at Alton Baker Park, established in 2013, is a flat, moderate 18-hole course; the PDGA Red layout runs 4,742 feet at par 55. A round
note: 18 holes · Par 55 · $5 per person per day (quarterly $50, annual $175)

title: Clearwater Park
contentHtml:
Clearwater Park is a close 9-teepad skills course with 2 baskets on each fairway, played as an 18-basket double run of about 5,128 feet at par 54, established in 2017. Shots mix wooded and open-field lines over mostly level ground.

Tees are concrete, turf and rubber mat, with DISCatcher Pro baskets. Restrooms and drinking water are available, and it is dog, cart and stroller friendly.

address: Clearwater Park, Springfield, OR

title: Dexter State Park
contentHtml:
The Dexter State Park course, established in 2001, is a hard, technical, hilly 18-hole course beside Dexter Reservoir, 6,024 feet at par 54. It is well marked and well maintained.

Tees are concrete and pavers, with DISCatcher Pro 24 baskets. A restroom is on site but no drinking water; dogs must be leashed. Watch for poison oak, slippery tee pads and some mud.

title: Garden Lake Park
contentHtml:
Garden Lake Park in Creswell has a flat, moderate 9-hole course of 2,320 feet at par 26, established in 2020, with holes from 72 to 501 feet.

Tees are gravel, with Mach V baskets. Restrooms are available, and it is dog and cart friendly.

note: 9 holes · Par 26 · Free to play. City park hours apply.

title: Jasper State Park
contentHtml:
Jasper State Park's flat, moderate 9-hole course was established in 2022, about 2,324 feet at par 27 from the short tees. Each hole has a short and a long tee and at least two basket positions.

Tees are grass, with Prodigy T2 baskets. Restrooms and drinking water are available, and dogs are allowed. Tee pads and signs are still being built, so use the map to navigate.

note: 9 holes · Par 27 · State park day-use fee

title: Office Bridge DGC
contentHtml:
Office Bridge is a mid-length, technical 18-hole course established in 2022 on the grounds of the old Hines mill by the Office Covered Bridge, mixing open areas and woods with elevation. Ruins of the former mill are still visible and come into play.

Tees are asphalt, with Patriot baskets. Restrooms and drinking water are available, and it is dog and cart friendly.
excerpt: Office Bridge is a mid-length, technical 18-hole course established in 2022 on the grounds of the old Hines mill by the Office Covered Bridge, mixing open areas
note: 18 holes · Free to play. On private land.
address: Old Hines Mill grounds by the Office Covered Bridge, Westfir, OR

title: Old Mill DGC
contentHtml:
Old Mill is a challenging, very hilly 18-hole course in Oakridge, established in 2020 and designed around the park's landscape and its logging and sawmill history, which tee signs and sculpture posts recall. The Extra Blue layout runs 5,828 feet at par 61.

Tees are turf, with Veteran baskets. A restroom is available but no drinking water; dogs are allowed.
excerpt: Old Mill is a challenging, very hilly 18-hole course in Oakridge, established in 2020 and designed around the park's landscape and its logging and sawmill histo
note: 18 holes · Free to play
address: Old Mill park, Oakridge, OR (park off Roaring Rapid Dr or Fish Hatchery Rd)

title: Pitney DGC @ O.S.H.
contentHtml:
The Pitney course is a flat, easy 9-hole course of about 2,100 feet at par 27 on the Oregon State Hospital - Junction City campus, built on wetlands and wide open to the wind. It is good for families.

Tees are rubber. There are no restrooms or drinking water; dogs are allowed.
excerpt: The Pitney course is a flat, easy 9-hole course of about 2,100 feet at par 27 on the Oregon State Hospital - Junction City campus, built on wetlands and wide op
note: 9 holes · Par 27 · Free. Check in with hospital security for a map and scorecard. No drugs, alcohol, tobacco or vaping on hospital grounds.
address: Oregon State Hospital campus, 29398 Recovery Way, Junction City, OR 97448 (off OR 99)

title: Stewart Pond
contentHtml:
Stewart Pond, established in 2015, was the first 18-hole course on BLM land. The hilly, moderate summer layout runs 6,837 feet at par 56, with most holes 250 to 514 feet, and takes about 1.5 to 2 hours.

Tees are concrete, with DISCatcher Pro baskets. It is dog, cart and stroller friendly; there are no restrooms or drinking water. Only 12 baskets are in play in winter.
excerpt: Stewart Pond, established in 2015, was the first 18-hole course on BLM land. The hilly, moderate summer layout runs 6,837 feet at par 56, with most holes 250 to
note: 18 holes (12 in winter) · Par 56 · Free to play; tournaments need a BLM permit
address: Stewart Pond, west Eugene, OR (BLM land)

title: The Grove
contentHtml:
The Grove at North Regional Park was built in 2009 by volunteers and the City of Cottage Grove. The intermediate course, also fun for beginners, crosses open fields, runs through a tree tunnel on hole 2 and alongside streams, and climbs and descends a large hill.

Tees are concrete, rubber mat and asphalt, with DISCatcher Pro baskets. It is dog, cart and stroller friendly; there are no restrooms or drinking water.
excerpt: The Grove at North Regional Park was built in 2009 by volunteers and the City of Cottage Grove. The intermediate course, also fun for beginners, crosses open fi
note: 18 baskets · Free to play. Cottage Grove Disc Golf Club on Facebook.
